His comments come days after a Supreme Court bench he led issued an interim order restraining the Bar Council of India and state bar councils from taking any punitive action against NALSAR students or faculty over the protest, with Kant himself saying on the bench that BCI's intervention was "totally uncalled for" and that the dispute was fundamentally "a matter of dialogue" between the students and himself, not something the regulator needed to police. BCI has since said it closed all proceedings against the NALSAR 2026 graduating batch, while the student body has maintained publicly that "no institution, including the Supreme Court and the CJI, are beyond legitimate scrutiny in a constitutional democracy."
key_points: Chief Justice **Surya Kant** says he "never consented" to NALSAR University's invitation to be chief guest at its convocation.
"**The question of me attending does not arise**," he told reporters — a notable walk-back after the invitation dispute became national news.
The row began after **70 NALSAR graduates** publicly objected to his invite over his earlier remarks about student protests.
The **Bar Council of India (BCI)** then tried to block those graduates from being enrolled as lawyers — before the Supreme Court itself stepped in and restrained BCI's action.
The CJI had earlier called BCI's intervention "**totally uncalled for**," saying the students "have the right to protest."

depth.background: NALSAR University of Law in Hyderabad is one of India's top national law schools, and its convocations traditionally invite senior legal figures as chief guest. This year, that tradition ran into controversy: after Chief Justice Surya Kant made oral remarks (around July 22) about student protests in Delhi, a group of about **70 NALSAR graduates** publicly objected to his being invited as their convocation's chief guest — arguing he was not the right figure to preside over their graduation given those comments. The **Bar Council of India (BCI)**, the statutory body that enrolls lawyers and regulates the legal profession, then directed state bar councils not to enroll the protesting graduates as advocates, effectively threatening their ability to practice law over a political protest. That order was swiftly criticized across the legal community and withdrawn within hours, but the underlying dispute — about whether the CJI should attend, and whether BCI had any business punishing students for protesting — kept escalating, eventually reaching the Supreme Court itself.

cards.title: Government to set up high-powered committee on banking reforms for 'Viksit Bharat 2047'
cards.what_happened: Addressing the **Public Sector Banks (PSB) Conclave 2026** in New Delhi, Sitharaman said the government would soon constitute a **high-powered committee** to examine the banking sector's role in reaching the Viksit Bharat 2047 goal. The two-day conclave, run by the Department of Financial Services, is structured around seven themes — deposit mobilisation, banking for youth, supporting the investment cycle, supporting global capability centres (GCCs), agriculture and horticulture value-chain infrastructure, innovation in credit cards, and priority-sector lending. Sitharaman said the conclave's recommendations and outcomes will be placed directly before the new committee, and urged bank leaders to submit their own ideas for reform.
key_points: Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** said the government will soon form a **high-powered committee** on public-sector bank reforms.
It was announced at the two-day **Public Sector Banks Conclave 2026** in New Delhi.

The panel will absorb recommendations from **seven themes**: deposit mobilisation, youth banking, the investment cycle, global capability centres, agri value chains, credit-card innovation, and priority-sector lending.
The goal is aligning India's banking sector with the **'Viksit Bharat 2047'** vision — India's target of becoming a developed economy by its 100th year of independence.
Bankers were directly asked to submit their own reform ideas into the process.

depth.background: **'Viksit Bharat 2047'** is the Indian government's long-term goal of becoming a fully developed economy by 2047, the centenary of independence. Public sector banks (PSBs) — banks majority-owned by the government, like SBI, PNB, and Bank of Baroda — control a large share of India's lending and are seen as central to funding that growth, from small-business credit to infrastructure. The Department of Financial Services periodically convenes bank chiefs to set policy direction, and past reform waves have included bank mergers and recapitalisation.

cards.title: Navy sailor, wife and two young children found dead at Mumbai's Navy Nagar in suspected murder-suicide
cards.what_happened: Local police and naval security personnel were alerted after the family, identified in reports as sailor Puranmal Shambhulal Mehra (30), his wife Oma Puranmal Mehra (28), and their two children, stopped responding to calls. Their bodies were discovered at their Navy Nagar residence on Saturday night. Police sources say the sailor was found hanging, while his wife and children were found on a bed; investigators suspect the wife and children may have consumed a poisonous substance, though this has **not been confirmed** pending forensic tests. Reports indicate the sailor had been in a financial dispute with his father-in-law, and that his wife had recently told her father she feared for her safety. No suicide note has been recovered. Police have filed an Accidental Death Report and are investigating.
key_points: An Indian Navy sailor, his wife, and their **two children (aged 3 and 2 months)** were found dead at their home in **Navy Nagar, Colaba**, south Mumbai.
Police were alerted after the family **failed to respond** to calls, and bodies were discovered on **Saturday night**.
Preliminary findings suggest the sailor died by suicide, while his wife and children are suspected to have died separately — final cause awaits **post-mortem and forensic reports**.
Reports cite a **financial dispute with the wife's father** in the days before the deaths.
Police have registered an **Accidental Death Report (ADR)** and opened an investigation; no note has been found.

depth.background: **Navy Nagar** in Colaba is a high-security residential area for Indian Navy personnel and their families in south Mumbai. Cases involving apparent family murder-suicides are typically investigated carefully by police because the true circumstances — mental health, financial stress, coercion — often only emerge after post-mortem and forensic review, and initial media reports can get ahead of confirmed facts.

cards.title: Supreme Court orders Karnataka to keep complying with Cauvery water releases to Tamil Nadu, defers next hearing a week
cards.what_happened: Tamil Nadu moved the Supreme Court on **August 3** alleging Karnataka had failed to comply with a **July 28 CWMA order** directing it to release 3,500 cusecs of water daily at Biligundlu from its Krishna Raja Sagar and Kabini reservoirs between July 29 and August 12. Court filings show actual flows in that window ranged only between **158 and 550 cusecs** — a fraction of what was ordered. On **August 17**, hearing the matter again, the bench directed Karnataka to continue complying with CWMA directions, while noting that recent heavy rainfall had pushed inflows at Biligundlu above **12,000 cusecs** by that morning. The court deferred further hearing to around **August 24** to review the latest release data.
key_points: The Supreme Court told Karnataka to keep complying with **CWMA orders** on releasing Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu.
The panel had ordered **3,500 cusecs a day** released from the KRS and Kabini reservoirs from July 29 to August 12.
Actual releases fell as low as **158–550 cusecs** in early August, far below the mandated level.
By the morning of August 17, inflow had jumped past **12,000 cusecs** after heavy catchment rainfall.
The bench of Justices **Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta** deferred the next hearing to around **August 24**.

depth.background: The **Cauvery river dispute** is one of India's oldest and most politically charged water-sharing fights, pitting upstream **Karnataka** against downstream **Tamil Nadu**, which depends on the river for drinking water and irrigation across its delta farmlands. A standing body, the **Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA)**, sets monthly release quotas based on rainfall and reservoir levels, but Karnataka has repeatedly been accused of under-releasing water, especially in dry years, sparking recurring protests and litigation.

cards.title: A hotel fire kills at least 7 Shravan pilgrims in West Bengal's Tarapith; the owner is arrested as claims of a blocked exit emerge
cards.what_happened: A fire broke out around **5 a.m.** at the five-storey **Hotel Bideshini**, located beside a pond near the Tarapith police station, reportedly triggered by a **short circuit** that spread rapidly through the building. Most guests — including several children — were asleep at the time; eyewitnesses said smoke filled the area within minutes. Police and fire department personnel rescued **22 people**, but at least **7 pilgrims died**, with some later reports putting the toll as high as 8. The victims had travelled from different districts to perform puja during Shravan. Hotel owner **Kalyan Paul** was **arrested**, and police are investigating whether the hotel's firefighting systems met safety rules. Multiple survivors say a rear exit door was locked, preventing escape — directly contradicting claims Paul made earlier the same morning. Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** announced **ex-gratia payments of ₹2 lakh** for each victim's next of kin and **₹50,000** for the injured, from the PM's National Relief Fund.
key_points: A fire tore through **Hotel Bideshini** in **Tarapith, Birbhum district**, around **5 a.m.** on Monday
At least **7 people died**, most reports say, all of them **pilgrims** — some later reports put the toll at 8
**22 people were rescued** by police and fire crews as smoke filled the building within minutes
Hotel owner **Kalyan Paul** has been **arrested**; police are probing whether fire-safety rules were followed
Guests allege a **rear exit was locked**, contradicting the owner's earlier claims

depth.background: Tarapith is one of West Bengal's most visited pilgrimage towns, built around a centuries-old Kali temple, and draws heavy footfall during religious observances — the fire broke out on the **third Monday of Shravan**, a Hindu holy month when devotees travel from across the region to perform puja (worship rituals) there. Small pilgrimage-town hotels in India have repeatedly come under scrutiny for weak fire-safety compliance, a recurring issue after past hotel-fire tragedies elsewhere in the country.

cards.title: Gujarat High Court orders immediate transfer of Surat's DCP after video shows police publicly flogging handcuffed accused
cards.what_happened: On **July 14**, video footage emerged showing a Surat DCP and a group of policemen publicly slapping and beating **handcuffed accused persons** and parading them through the streets. A lawyer filed a written complaint, and a division bench of Chief Justice **Sunita Agarwal** and Justice **D N Ray** took up the matter as a suo motu Public Interest Litigation. On **August 17**, the court ordered DCP **Rajdeepsinh Nakum's immediate transfer**, saying it was necessary to ensure the ongoing investigation into the incident is impartial. The court noted the officer's conduct broke explicit government circulars prohibiting public beating and parading of the accused, and pointed to both the Supreme Court's **D K Basu** guidelines and the Gujarat HC's own 2022 findings in a similar Kheda flogging case.
key_points: Gujarat HC ordered the **immediate transfer** of Surat DCP Rajdeepsinh Nakum to ensure an impartial probe.
Video showed police **publicly slapping, beating and parading handcuffed accused persons** in Surat on July 14.
The court took up the case as a **suo motu PIL** — acting on its own, after a lawyer's written complaint.
Nakum allegedly violated **government circulars that ban public beating and parading** of the accused.
The order leans on the Supreme Court's **D K Basu ruling**, a landmark judgment on how police must treat people in custody.

depth.background: Public 'flogging' or parading of accused persons by police — sometimes filmed and shared as a show of toughness — has surfaced as a recurring controversy in Gujarat, including a 2022 incident in Kheda that also drew judicial criticism. India's Supreme Court set binding rules for how police must treat anyone in custody in its **1997 D K Basu vs State of West Bengal** judgment, which followed cases of custodial abuse and death. Those rules require police to identify themselves, inform a relative of an arrest, and avoid using force beyond what's needed to make an arrest — public beatings and parading violate this directly.

cards.title: India flies its first fully indigenous jet-powered loitering munition, built by a Lucknow startup in under a year
cards.what_happened: On **August 11**, the Divyastra Mk3 completed its maiden flight down a test airstrip in Uttar Pradesh, powered entirely by an **Indian-made jet engine** built by DG Propulsion, with the airframe developed by Kawa UAV Pvt. Ltd. (branded HoverIt). During the trial, the engine met all its pre-defined performance parameters. The company says the platform went from initial concept to a fully airborne weapon system in **under eight months**, with **no imported jet engine and no foreign critical subsystems** anywhere in the aircraft — a first for an Indian jet-powered loitering munition. The achievement was formally announced by the company on **August 16**.
key_points: Lucknow-based **Kawa UAV (HoverIt)** successfully flew the **Divyastra Mk3** — India's first jet-powered 'suicide drone' with **zero imported engine parts**.
The jet engine itself was built by another Indian firm, **DG Propulsion** — no foreign critical subsystems at all.
The programme went from **concept to maiden flight in under eight months**, a fast timeline for a jet-propulsion aircraft.
It's based in Uttar Pradesh's **Defence Industrial Corridor**, a state-backed hub for local weapons manufacturing.
The flight validates India's ability to design and build **complex aerospace propulsion systems** entirely at home.

depth.background: A **loitering munition** — often nicknamed a 'suicide drone' — is a weapon that flies to a target area, circles ('loiters') while looking for something to hit, then dives in and detonates on impact, combining a drone's surveillance with a missile's destructive punch. India has increasingly pushed for **'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (self-reliant India)** in defence manufacturing, aiming to cut dependence on imported weapons after repeated supply disruptions from foreign suppliers during conflicts. Most loitering munitions to date use simpler propeller engines; a **jet-powered** version can fly faster and farther, but building an indigenous jet engine — the hardest part of any aircraft — has historically been a major gap in India's defence industry.

cards.title: RBI quietly defends the rupee near 95.5/dollar as Middle East oil prices squeeze the market
cards.what_happened: India's rupee slipped to **95.49 per US dollar** in early trading on Monday, its weakest levels in recent sessions, before state-run banks began selling dollars — a move traders widely interpreted as **RBI intervention** — to slow the decline. The pressure came as **Brent crude held near $88.50 a barrel**, up roughly 6% over the past week, with the Middle East conflict and continued disruption to Iranian oil-tanker traffic keeping supply fears elevated. India's stock benchmarks also fell: the **Sensex dropped 281 points (0.36%) to 77,728** and the **Nifty fell 78 points (0.32%) to 24,288**, with IT exporters — Infosys (-2.7%), HCL Technologies (-2.5%), TCS (-1.9%) and Tech Mahindra (-1.8%) — among the biggest losers. Banking names bucked the trend, with Axis Bank, Tata Steel and Kotak Mahindra Bank among the day's gainers.
key_points: The rupee slipped to **95.49 per dollar** before state-run banks stepped in to sell dollars and limit the fall
Traders say the selling was most likely done **on the RBI's behalf**
The **Sensex fell 281 points** to 77,728 and the **Nifty fell 78 points** to 24,288
IT stocks led the losses — **Infosys fell 2.7%**, TCS 1.9%, as elevated oil prices weighed on sentiment
**Brent crude** held near **$88.50 a barrel**, up 6% last week, on continued Iran-related supply fears

depth.background: India imports over 80% of the crude oil it uses, so when global oil prices rise — as they have amid the ongoing standoff between the US/Israel and Iran, and Iranian attacks on tankers near the **Strait of Hormuz** — it directly strains India's trade balance and puts downward pressure on the **rupee**. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) doesn't fix the currency's value, but it regularly steps into the market, buying or selling dollars through state-run banks, to smooth out sharp, disorderly swings rather than fight the underlying trend. The rupee has hovered close to the psychologically important **95-per-dollar** level for several sessions, and traders say the central bank appears determined not to let it breach that line abruptly.

cards.title: Telangana's new voter-roll draft drops over 45 lakh people as 'shifted' — Hyderabad hit hardest
cards.what_happened: The Election Commission published Telangana's draft electoral roll today, **August 17**, the next step after its door-to-door SIR exercise. Of roughly **73.39 lakh (7.34 million)** voters who did not submit the required enumeration forms, more than **45 lakh (4.5 million)** have been marked as having 'permanently shifted' elsewhere and left off today's draft roll. In **Hyderabad district** alone, 19.41 lakh names — nearly **41% of all enumeration forms** — were placed in the 'Absent, Shifted, or Dead' category and removed, and authorities are separately sending notices to 5.82 lakh electors there. The claims-and-objections window is open from today through **September 16**, with objections to be resolved by October 15 and a final roll published **October 19**. BRS leader KT Rama Rao has demanded transparency from the Election Commission and raised the possibility of Supreme Court intervention, while Congress Chief Minister Revanth Reddy has acknowledged roughly 21% of voters statewide could face deletion and has directed his own ministers to review why local Congress organizers failed to help voters file paperwork.
key_points: The Election Commission published Telangana's draft roll today after its **Special Intensive Revision**
Over **45 lakh (4.5 million)** voters were marked as **'permanently shifted'** and dropped
**Hyderabad district** saw the steepest drop — over **41% of its enumeration forms** flagged
Objections can be filed from **today until September 16**; the final roll comes out **October 19**
Congress-run Telangana's own CM admits **~21%** of voters statewide could face deletion

depth.background: The **Special Intensive Revision (SIR)** is a nationwide Election Commission of India exercise to re-verify every voter's details door-to-door, meant to remove duplicate, dead, or relocated names from the rolls. It became a major national controversy after its **Bihar rollout in 2025**, when opposition leader **Rahul Gandhi** accused the Election Commission of colluding with the ruling BJP to quietly delete genuine voters — a claim he calls 'vote chori' (vote theft) — while the Commission and BJP say it's a legitimate accuracy exercise. Telangana, currently governed by the **Congress party** under Chief Minister **A. Revanth Reddy**, is now going through the same process, with the regional opposition party **BRS (Bharat Rashtra Samithi)**, led by **KT Rama Rao**, as the main political rival watching closely.

cards.title: RBI abruptly cuts short its dollar-deposit scheme after banks poured in over $52 billion
cards.what_happened: RBI announced it is closing the deposit-collection window for its FCNR(B) dollar-swap scheme a full month early — moving the deadline from **September 30 to August 31, 2026** — while giving banks until **September 11** to complete the actual swap trades. The central bank cited overwhelming demand: by **August 13**, the broader scheme (which also covers corporate foreign borrowing) had already pulled in a reported **$56.85 billion** in total forex inflows, of which more than **$52 billion** came from the FCNR(B) deposit leg alone. Only the deposit window is being cut short — the separate window for foreign corporate borrowing (ECBs and OFCBs) stays open until **December 31**. The reversal is notable because RBI Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** had said on August 5 there were no plans to close the scheme early, making this a sharper pivot than usual just over a week later.
key_points: RBI moved the deadline for its **FCNR(B) dollar-swap scheme** from **September 30 to August 31**
Banks had already brought in **over $52 billion** through the scheme by August 13
The total swap facility, including corporate borrowing, pulled in nearly **$57 billion**
It echoes a **2013 scheme** RBI used to defend the rupee during that year's market shock
The Governor had said just over a week earlier there were **'no plans'** to end it early

depth.background: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) — the country's central bank — announced this swap scheme on **June 5, 2026**, after the rupee had fallen more than **6%** in the first half of the year amid foreign capital leaving India. Under the scheme, Indian banks could take in fresh dollar deposits from Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) — called FCNR(B), or Foreign Currency Non-Resident Bank deposits — and swap those dollars with the RBI at a fixed, favorable exchange rate, making it cheaper for banks to attract and hold foreign currency. It deliberately mirrors a similar scheme RBI ran in **2013** under then-Governor Raghuram Rajan, which helped stabilize the rupee during that year's 'taper tantrum' — a period when global investors pulled money out of emerging markets like India.

cards.title: Supreme Court pauses Allahabad High Court probe into Rahul Gandhi's assets
cards.what_happened: On **17 August 2026**, a Supreme Court bench led by **Chief Justice of India Surya Kant**, with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, heard Gandhi's challenge to the Allahabad High Court's orders. The bench directed the High Court to **defer its scheduled August 20 hearing** until the Supreme Court examines the matter further, and ordered the CBI or any other investigating authority **not to submit any report** to the High Court in the meantime. During the hearing, the judges questioned why the High Court had passed its orders **without giving Gandhi a chance to be heard** — a basic fairness requirement in law. Gandhi has filed two petitions: one challenging the High Court's orders directly, and a separate **transfer petition** asking that the entire case be moved from the Allahabad High Court to the Delhi High Court. Both petitions were filed on August 7 and taken up together today.
key_points: SC tells Allahabad HC to **defer** its Aug 20 hearing
CBI, ED barred from filing any report **for now**
Complaint filed by a **Karnataka BJP worker** in 2026
Court asks why Gandhi wasn't given a **hearing** first
Gandhi also seeks to **transfer** the case to Delhi HC

depth.background: **Rahul Gandhi**, the Congress leader and **Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha** (India's lower house of Parliament), is facing a **disproportionate assets** complaint — an allegation that someone's wealth exceeds what their known, legal income can explain. The complaint was filed by **S. Vignesh Shishir**, a BJP worker from Karnataka. In **May 2026**, the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court ordered the **CBI** (India's federal police agency) and the **ED** (the agency that probes financial crimes and money laundering) to verify the complaint and report back; in July, unhappy with the CBI's response, the court demanded a senior officer personally file a fresh affidavit on the probe's progress.

cards.title: Seven killed in stampede at Bihar's Ashok Dham temple on Shravan Monday
cards.what_happened: On the morning of **17 August 2026**, thousands of devotees queued outside Ashok Dham Temple in Lakhisarai to perform jalabhishek on the third Monday of Shravan. Officials say the crowd swelled suddenly after **two trains arrived around 6:30–6:45 am**, adding a large batch of pilgrims to an already packed queue. A barricade gave way and an **electric pole fell** near the men's line; a cable wire came down with it, and a rumour spread that it was a live, electrified wire. The panic pushed the crowd onto the women's queue on the other side, causing people to fall over one another. **At least seven people, mostly women, died** and 12 to 14 others were injured and hospitalized; officials cautioned the toll could rise as some injured remain under observation. Bihar Chief Minister **Samrat Choudhary** called the incident 'tragic and heart-wrenching' and announced **₹4 lakh** compensation for each deceased victim's family, while Prime Minister Modi expressed condolences to the bereaved.
key_points: **Seven** devotees, mostly women, killed in Lakhisarai stampede
**12 to 14** injured; several still under observation
Crush began after an electric pole fell near the queue
A rumour of a live wire sparked **panic** and a rush
Bihar announces **₹4 lakh** ex-gratia for each victim's family

depth.background: Ashok Dham Temple in Bihar's Lakhisarai district is a major Lord Shiva shrine that draws huge crowds every Monday during **Shravan** (also called Sawan), the Hindu holy month when devotees offer water and milk to Shiva idols in a ritual called jalabhishek. Monday's crush happened on the **third Monday of Shravan 2026**, one of the busiest days of the pilgrimage season. India has a long, grim history of stampedes at religious gatherings because narrow approach roads and exposed electrical wiring get overwhelmed when tens of thousands of people converge in a short window.

prev_ref.title: Jharkhand exam-scandal hunger striker enters his 14th day, hospitalized, as protesters say Modi's new exam reforms don't go far enough

cards.title: Jharkhand agrees to scrap tainted exams as hunger strike enters its fourth week — but protesters aren't satisfied
cards.what_happened: Late on Sunday, the Jharkhand government agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC preliminary exam along with two backlog recruitment tests, following weeks of pressure. Three JPSC board members submitted their resignations after being questioned by state investigators over the alleged irregularities. The broader agitation entered its **23rd day** on August 16, with Mahto continuing his hunger strike — now in its fourth week — as his health deteriorates with fever. Despite the government's concession, protesters say it doesn't go far enough: their central demands remain a cancellation of the separate JSSC-CGL exam and a **CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation)** probe into the leaks, neither of which has been granted. Protest leaders have announced plans to **gherao** Chief Minister Hemant Soren's official residence in Ranchi on August 20, demanding his resignation if the remaining demands aren't met.
key_points: The Jharkhand government agreed to **cancel the JPSC preliminary exam** and two backlog recruitment tests after weeks of protest.
**Three JPSC board members resigned** amid a state investigation into the alleged irregularities.
Hunger-striking student leader **Devendra Nath Mahto** is now in his **fourth week** without food, his health worsening with fever.
Protesters still plan to **gherao (surround) Chief Minister Hemant Soren's residence on August 20** and are demanding his resignation.
The core demand — a **CBI probe** and cancellation of the separate JSSC-CGL exam — has **still not been met**.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported that Devendra Nath Mahto was on the 14th day of his hunger strike and hospitalized after a march to gherao the Jharkhand Assembly turned chaotic when police used lathi charges, that police had blocked him from joining Ranchi's Independence Day flag march, and that Chief Minister Hemant Soren had launched a student-outreach initiative without agreeing to protesters' core demands.
thread.changed: The government has now made its first real concession — cancelling the JPSC preliminary exam and two backlog tests, with three JPSC board members resigning — but protesters say it's not enough and have announced a gherao of the Chief Minister's residence on August 20 demanding his resignation, while the hunger strike continues into its fourth week.

depth.background: Student aspirants preparing for Jharkhand's state recruitment exams — run by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) — have been protesting since early August over alleged **paper leaks and irregularities** in the recruitment process, which controls access to thousands of coveted government jobs. Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto began an indefinite hunger strike on August 2, and the agitation has since grown into a broader movement demanding an independent probe and the cancellation of tainted exams. Prime Minister Modi's Independence Day speech promised nationwide exam reforms, but protesters said those pledges didn't address their specific demands, and the standoff continued even as Mahto was hospitalized.

cards.title: Iran's Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks send oil higher again, dragging down the Sensex, Nifty and rupee
cards.what_happened: A fresh wave of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz has pushed oil prices back up and rattled Indian markets. Starting **August 8**, an ADNOC tanker was struck by a missile the UAE blamed on Iran's IRGC; by **August 13-14**, two more ADNOC vessels had been hit — the UAE's Foreign Ministry called it 'piracy' and accused Iran of using the Strait as 'a tool of economic coercion.' Brent crude rose from **$86.91 a barrel on August 14 to $88.85 on August 17**, more than 5% in a week, as hopes of reopening the Strait faded and shipping traffic collapsed to just 8-15 transits a day versus roughly 130 before the conflict. Indian markets felt it directly: the **Sensex fell 71 points on Friday** and opened **287 points lower today (-0.37%) at 77,722**, with the Nifty down 61 points to 24,305 and PSU bank stocks under particular pressure, as traders cited renewed Hormuz-driven oil anxiety and foreign fund outflows. The rupee, which hit an all-time low of 96.84/USD in May during an earlier escalation, is trading near 95.4/USD — still vulnerable given India imports about 70% of its crude in dollars.
key_points: Brent crude climbed from **$86.91 to $88.85 a barrel** this week after **three attacks on ADNOC tankers** in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Sensex opened today down **287 points (-0.37%)** at 77,722; the Nifty fell **61 points** to 24,305.
Shipping traffic through the Strait has collapsed to **8-15 vessels a day**, down from about **130 a day** before the conflict.
India imports about **70% of its crude**, so a sustained oil spike widens its import bill and pressures the **rupee**, trading near 95.4/USD.
A 10% rise in global crude can lift India's headline inflation by roughly **0.2 percentage points**, trade economists estimate.

depth.background: This is the latest flare-up in a US/Israel-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz that has run since roughly February 2026 and repeatedly disrupted the world's most important oil chokepoint — a corridor that normally carries close to a quarter of the world's seaborne crude. The UAE's state oil company ADNOC has been targeted three times in the past week; Abu Dhabi has accused Iran's Revolutionary Guard of the attacks and called them 'piracy' and a violation of a UN Security Council resolution. India has partly cushioned itself from earlier spikes by buying discounted Russian crude, which now supplies roughly half its imports.

prev_ref.title: Bangladesh says its next PM won't visit India until Sheikh Hasina is extradited, hardening the post-Hasina rift

cards.title: A top Indian business delegation lands in Dhaka this week, testing whether trade can move even as the Hasina extradition standoff freezes politics
cards.what_happened: A high-profile, **18-member delegation from the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII)** — India's top industry lobby — is visiting Dhaka on **August 17-18**, with an advance team already on the ground preparing the visit. The delegation, made up of senior representatives across sectors, is scheduled to meet Bangladesh's Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed, Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority, and the country's top business chamber (FBCCI). The stated agenda: trade barriers, investment, connectivity, and industrial cooperation — including Dhaka's complaints about India's recent tightening of land-port rules for Bangladeshi exports. The visit lands squarely amid the coldest political period between the two countries in years, with Bangladesh's presumptive next prime minister publicly refusing to visit India until Sheikh Hasina is extradited to face charges over the deadly 2024 crackdown on protesters.
key_points: An **18-member CII delegation** — India's top industry body — visits Dhaka on **Aug 17-18** to meet Bangladesh's commerce and finance ministers.
The visit comes even as Bangladesh's presumptive next PM says he **won't visit India** until Sheikh Hasina is extradited.
Talks will cover trade barriers, investment, and industrial cooperation, including friction from India's recent **land-port restrictions**.
It follows other quiet resets: **border trade resumed at Nathu La** in August after a six-year gap.
The visit shows India and Bangladesh trying to **keep commerce moving** while the political relationship stays frozen over Hasina.

thread.previously: We reported Bangladesh's presumptive next PM said he would not visit India until Sheikh Hasina is extradited, hardening the political rift between the two countries.
thread.changed: Despite that political freeze, a senior 18-member Indian trade delegation (CII) is visiting Dhaka this week to meet Bangladesh's commerce and finance ministers — showing the two sides are trying to keep economic ties moving on a separate track from the frozen political relationship.

depth.background: India-Bangladesh relations have been in a deep freeze since Sheikh Hasina's government fell in August 2024 and she fled to India, where she remains despite Dhaka's repeated extradition requests. Bangladesh's interim/incoming leadership has said its next prime minister will not visit India until Hasina is handed over — a red line that has kept high-level political contact minimal even as trade between the two neighbors, worth billions of dollars annually, keeps happening on the ground. India tightened rules on Bangladeshi goods moving through its land ports earlier this year, adding friction on top of the political freeze.

cards.title: Bangladesh says its next PM won't visit India until Sheikh Hasina is extradited, hardening the post-Hasina rift
cards.what_happened: Bangladeshi officials confirmed that Rahman will **not travel to India** for a planned visit until Hasina is extradited to face justice, alongside other individuals Dhaka wants returned. The demand escalated after Hasina, still in India, gave an **open press interaction in New Delhi on August 5**, which Bangladeshi officials saw as provocative given her fugitive status and her tribunal conviction for crimes against humanity. India has given no public indication it intends to extradite Hasina, and has historically treated her presence as a humanitarian shelter rather than a political statement. The dispute effectively freezes near-term high-level diplomacy between the two countries at a moment when Bangladesh is trying to stabilize under new leadership.
key_points: Bangladesh has told India that presumptive PM **Tarique Rahman** won't visit until New Delhi **extradites Sheikh Hasina**, the ousted former PM sheltering in India.
The demand also covers **other fugitives** wanted by Dhaka in connection with the 2024 uprising that toppled Hasina's government.
Talks on a Rahman visit had been underway for weeks, but relations soured further after **Hasina gave a public press interaction in New Delhi on August 5**.
Hasina has been convicted by Bangladesh's **International Crimes Tribunal** for crimes against humanity tied to the deadly 2024 crackdown on protesters.
Dhaka says the overall **atmosphere needs to improve** before any high-level visit can proceed.

depth.background: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh's prime minister for 15 years, fled to India in **August 2024** as a mass uprising toppled her government amid allegations of a violent crackdown on student-led protests that killed hundreds. She has remained in India ever since, while Bangladesh's interim and now incoming governments have repeatedly demanded her return to face trial. **Tarique Rahman**, leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), is set to become the country's next prime minister, and had been in quiet discussions with New Delhi about a possible bilateral visit — a normal early step for a new government to reset ties with a major neighbor.

prev_ref.title: West Bengal Congress leader and his son shot dead in Nadia, ahead of state elections

cards.title: A TMC-linked panchayat chief is among 3 arrested in the killing of a Bengal Congress leader and his son
cards.what_happened: Congress leader Anisur Rahman and his son Abu Sufian were driving home late on **Saturday night** when their car was blocked by attackers who **fired multiple rounds and then attacked them with sharp weapons**; both died. Police have now arrested three people: **Fatema Bibi**, the TMC panchayat chief of Haranagar gram panchayat, and two alleged associates, Saheb Ali Mondal and Mithun Sheikh. The victims' family and local Congress leaders allege the real mastermind is Bibi's husband, **Jubbar Sheikh**, a locally powerful TMC figure who was already in judicial custody on unrelated charges before this killing. West Bengal's Congress unit had already staged a statewide **'black day'** protest over the killings even before any arrests were made.
key_points: Police arrested **Fatema Bibi**, the Trinamool Congress panchayat chief of Haranagar, plus two associates, over Saturday's killing.
Congress leader **Anisur Rahman**, 24-year-old son **Abu Sufian** were shot and then attacked with sharp weapons after their car was blocked.
Bibi's husband, a locally influential TMC leader already in **judicial custody**, is accused by the family of masterminding the attack.
The killing happened in Bethuadahari, Nadia district, days before West Bengal's **state elections**.
West Bengal Congress had already held a statewide **'black day'** protest over the killings before these arrests.

thread.previously: Congress leader Anisur Rahman and his son Abu Sufian were shot dead in Nadia district ahead of West Bengal's state elections, and the state Congress unit held a statewide 'black day' protest.
thread.changed: Police have now made arrests — including a TMC-linked panchayat chief, Fatema Bibi — and the victims' family is accusing her jailed TMC-leader husband of masterminding the killing.

depth.background: West Bengal's politics has a long, ugly history of **political violence tied to local panchayat (village council) power struggles**, especially in districts like Nadia where Trinamool Congress (TMC) and opposition parties compete fiercely for grassroots control. Panchayat chiefs control local patronage — contracts, welfare disbursement, land — which makes these posts high-stakes and, at times, violently contested. Congress has been a shrinking but still-present opposition force in the state, and any attack on its local leaders ahead of elections gets read through a sharply political lens.

cards.title: Two more people killed as Uttarakhand's flash floods claim fresh victims in Dehradun and Udham Singh Nagar
cards.what_happened: In Dehradun, 25-year-old Neha Arya fell into the water at Sahastradhara while posing for a photograph and was later declared dead despite rescue efforts. Separately, in Udham Singh Nagar, Class 11 student Pawan Chauhan disappeared while bathing in the swollen Gola river; police, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams have launched a search operation that was ongoing as of the latest reports. Both incidents occurred amid a broader spell of heavy monsoon rain across north India, with the IMD separately issuing a red alert for a fresh Bay of Bengal low-pressure system threatening Odisha, Bengal, and Jharkhand.
key_points: **Neha Arya**, 25, fell into rushing water at Sahastradhara in Dehradun while posing for a photo and was declared dead.
A **Class 11 student**, Pawan Chauhan, went missing after being swept away in the swollen **Gola river** in Udham Singh Nagar.
**SDRF and NDRF teams**, alongside police, have launched search-and-rescue operations for the missing student.
The deaths add to Uttarakhand's mounting monsoon toll, already strained by the ongoing **Pipalkoti tunnel collapse** rescue.
Authorities are renewing warnings against visiting **swollen rivers and waterfalls** during peak monsoon.

depth.background: Uttarakhand's steep Himalayan terrain and glacier-fed rivers make it especially prone to flash floods during the June–September monsoon, when sudden, heavy rain upstream can turn a shallow stream into a deadly torrent within minutes. The state is already managing a multi-day rescue at the Pipalkoti tunnel collapse, where the death toll has climbed to 8, and this year's monsoon has been unusually deadly regionally — neighboring Himachal Pradesh's monsoon death toll has reached 183 in 47 days. Popular tourist and pilgrim spots like the Sahastradhara waterfall near Dehradun draw large crowds even during dangerous water conditions.

cards.title: Modi pledges 5 to 8 new semiconductor plants within 8 years as India's chip-making push accelerates
cards.what_happened: During his 75-minute Independence Day address from the Red Fort on August 15 — India's 80th year of independence — PM Modi said India expects to add between five and eight new semiconductor plants over the next seven to eight years, and that three major plants have already begun operating, with their output set to be exported as well as used domestically. The announcement sat alongside a broader pitch to make India a global defence-manufacturing hub, and other Independence Day pledges including the AI-skills program and progress on the indigenous 'Sudarshan Chakra' air defence system.
key_points: PM Modi said India will add **5 to 8 new semiconductor fabrication plants** over the next **7 to 8 years**.
He said **three major chip plants have already started operations** under India's self-reliance push.
Output from these plants will also be **exported**, Modi said, not just used domestically.
The pledge was folded into his **'Atmanirbhar Bharat'** and 'Viksit Bharat by 2047' vision at Independence Day.
It came in the same 80th Independence Day speech that also unveiled a **1-crore-youth AI-skills program**.

depth.background: India launched its semiconductor mission a few years ago with large financial incentives to attract chip manufacturers, partly in response to the global chip shortage exposed during the pandemic and to the broader US-China race over who controls advanced chip supply chains. Building a semiconductor fabrication plant ('fab') is enormously capital- and time-intensive — projects typically take years and tens of billions of dollars before producing a single usable chip — so government pledges on fab counts are watched closely for follow-through. India already has projects announced in states like Gujarat and Assam under this push.

cards.title: IMD issues red alert as fresh Bay of Bengal low-pressure system threatens Odisha, Bengal and Jharkhand with extreme rain
cards.what_happened: The IMD said Sunday that a **fresh low-pressure area** has formed over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining West Bengal-north Odisha coast, and is expected to intensify and move north-westward over the next day. In response, it issued a **red alert** — its highest-severity warning — for Odisha's Mayurbhanj district and West Bengal's Jhargram and Paschim Medinipur districts, forecasting extremely heavy rainfall of over **20 cm in 24 hours** in the worst-hit spots. The wider warning zone covers heavy-to-very-heavy rain across Gangetic West Bengal, Odisha and Jharkhand for the next four days, with isolated extremely heavy rain expected on **August 17** in Odisha and **August 18** in Gangetic West Bengal. The IMD also warned of squally winds up to **60 km/h** along the coast and told fishermen not to head out to sea through August 18.
key_points: The IMD has flagged a **fresh low-pressure area** over the northwest Bay of Bengal, expected to intensify over the next **24 hours**.
A **red alert** — the IMD's highest warning level — is in force for Odisha's Mayurbhanj and West Bengal's Jhargram and Paschim Medinipur districts.
Some parts of Odisha could see more than **20 cm of rain in 24 hours**, with isolated 'extremely heavy' falls expected on **August 17**.
Winds of **40-60 km/h**, gusting higher, are forecast along the coast; fishermen have been told to stay ashore through **August 18**.
The alert lands on top of an already brutal monsoon season that has killed hundreds across India this year.

depth.background: India's monsoon season regularly spins up low-pressure systems over the Bay of Bengal that pull moisture inland and dump it, sometimes catastrophically, over the eastern and central states. The IMD uses a four-colour warning system — green, yellow, orange, and **red** for the most severe risk — to tell state governments and the public how urgently to prepare. This year's monsoon has already been unusually deadly: Himachal Pradesh alone has recorded **183 deaths** in 47 days, and separate flash floods and landslides have hit Uttarakhand and other states through July and August.

cards.title: Death toll in Uttarakhand's Pipalkoti tunnel collapse climbs to 8, two workers still trapped
cards.what_happened: The accident occurred on Thursday when debris and water suddenly surged into the under-construction THDC tunnel, trapping 22 workers inside. By Saturday, rescue teams had recovered another body, taking the confirmed death toll to **eight**, while **two workers remained missing**. Uttarakhand's Disaster Management Minister **Madan Kaushik** said the rescue operation would 'continue till the end,' while local officials said crews were battling **high water levels** and had so far only been able to reach a few hundred metres from the site of the collapse. NDRF, SDRF and local police teams remain on site searching for the two still unaccounted for.
key_points: Rescuers recovered **another body** on Saturday, taking the confirmed death toll to **eight**.
**Two workers** remain missing and trapped inside the under-construction tunnel.
The accident happened when **debris and water burst into** a hydroelectric tunnel being built by state-run **THDC**, initially trapping **22 workers**.
Rescue teams (NDRF, SDRF, police) say **high water levels** inside the tunnel are slowing the search, with crews able to reach only a few hundred metres in.

thread.previously: We reported that one of three workers missing after a tunnel collapse at a hydroelectric project in Chamoli, Uttarakhand, had been found dead as the rescue operation entered its third day.
thread.changed: Rescue teams recovered **another body** on Saturday, taking the confirmed death toll to **eight**, while **two workers remain trapped** and the search is being slowed by **high water levels** inside the tunnel.

depth.background: The collapse happened at the **Vishnugad-Pipalkoti Hydroelectric Project**, an under-construction tunnel being built by the state-run **Tehri Hydro Development Corporation (THDC)** in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand — a Himalayan state that regularly sees flash floods and landslides during the monsoon. It is one of several deadly monsoon disasters to hit the wider region this season, alongside flooding and landslides reported elsewhere in Uttarakhand and neighboring states.

cards.title: Modi's Independence Day flagship: AI-skill training for 1 crore youth within a year
cards.what_happened: Speaking from the ramparts of the Red Fort on India's 80th Independence Day, Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** announced that the government would provide AI-skill training to **1 crore (10 million) youth over the next year**, framing it as key to India leading in the AI era. The announcement came alongside other youth-focused measures, including free coaching support, as part of a speech that referenced youth more than 50 times. It represents a dramatic scale-up: government data shows only about **53,449 candidates** had enrolled in AI-related job roles under the existing PMKVY 4.0 scheme as of June 30, 2026, with roughly **25,466 certified** so far.
key_points: Modi announced AI-skill training for **1 crore (10 million) youth** within the **next one year**.
It was the centerpiece of his **80th Independence Day** address from the Red Fort, which mentioned 'youth' more than **50 times** in a 75-minute speech.
It's a huge scale-up from the government's existing AI-skilling track — **PMKVY 4.0** had enrolled just **~53,449 candidates** as of June 30, 2026.
The stated goal: equip Indian youth to **'lead the world'** in artificial intelligence as the technology reshapes jobs globally.

depth.background: India's flagship skilling program, the **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)**, has run for a decade training workers in trades from electronics to hospitality, and now includes an AI-focused track under its fourth phase. The announcement lands against a backdrop of rising anxiety over AI's effect on jobs worldwide, and domestically amid ongoing protests in states like Jharkhand over exam and recruitment irregularities that have left many young job-seekers frustrated.

cards.title: Former Bengal deputy speaker and TMC veteran Asish Banerjee found dead; note blames 'smear campaign'
cards.what_happened: Police say Banerjee was found hanging at the **TMC office in Rampurhat, Birbhum district**, on Sunday morning, and recovered a **one-page handwritten note** believed to be his. In it, he denies any role in **corruption**, including specific allegations involving the **Tarapith-Rampurhat Development Authority (TRDA)** — he wrote he had no part in its tender decisions, cheque approvals, building-plan clearances or no-objection certificates. He said he had not always been able to protest wrongdoing inside the party but had never personally taken money for favours, and that he now felt entering politics had been **a mistake**. TMC's national general secretary **Abhishek Banerjee** posted publicly blaming the **BJP and sections of the media** for running a smear campaign that drove him to this, urging critics to reflect on the human cost of their allegations. **Dhruba Saha**, the BJP MLA who defeated Banerjee earlier this year, expressed grief and called for a proper investigation while rejecting any BJP role.
key_points: **Asish Banerjee, 74**, found dead at a **TMC office in Birbhum**, West Bengal, on Sunday
Five-time **Rampurhat MLA** and Bengal Assembly **Deputy Speaker from 2021 to 2026**
Purported suicide note denies **corruption**, calls entering politics 'a mistake'
TMC's **Abhishek Banerjee** blames a **BJP-driven 'smear campaign'** for his death
He had lost his Rampurhat seat to **BJP's Dhruba Saha** in this year's Assembly election

depth.background: The **Trinamool Congress (TMC)** ruled West Bengal for 15 years before losing power to the **BJP** in the 2026 Assembly election. Banerjee, a veteran TMC leader who had held ministerial charges including school education and agriculture, lost his own seat in that defeat and stepped down as the party's Birbhum district chief in June. He was found dead months later at a party office next to his home in Rampurhat, with police recovering a handwritten note at the scene.

cards.title: Passenger's licensed pistol accidentally fires during airport security check in Varanasi, injures two staff
cards.what_happened: Around **9:30 AM on Sunday**, Kamlesh Kedarnath Rai, a resident of Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh, arrived at Varanasi airport with his wife to board **Air India Express flight IX-1810** to Mumbai. He had declared his **licensed 7.62mm pistol** and **21 live cartridges** at check-in, as required. While staff of **AAICLAS** (the Airport Authority of India's security arm) were inspecting the weapon at the arms-and-ammunition counter, a round was **accidentally discharged**. The bullet ricocheted and struck two screening personnel — **Rohit Raj**, injured in the thumb, and **Suman Kumari**, injured in the foot. Both were rushed to New Lakshmi Trauma Centre in Varanasi for treatment, and police detained Rai for questioning as the **Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS)** opened a review into whether standard firearm-handling procedure was followed.
key_points: A **licensed 7.62mm pistol** discharged during a mandatory weapons check at **Varanasi's Lal Bahadur Shastri airport**
**Two screening staff**, Rohit Raj and Suman Kumari, injured by a ricocheting round
Passenger **Kamlesh Rai** of Azamgarh was flying **Air India Express IX-1810** to Mumbai with his wife
Incident occurred around **9:30 AM** on Sunday while 21 live cartridges were being inspected
Aviation security regulator **BCAS** is now reviewing whether protocol was followed

depth.background: Indian law allows travellers to carry a **licensed firearm** in checked baggage, but only after declaring it at check-in and having it physically inspected and unloaded by trained screening staff at a designated counter before it goes into the cargo hold — it can never go into the cabin. Varanasi's airport is one of India's busiest, handling heavy pilgrim and domestic traffic. This inspection step exists precisely to make sure a declared weapon is safe before it is stowed, which is what makes today's accidental discharge notable — it happened during the very process meant to prevent exactly this.

cards.title: Amit Shah accuses Sonia Gandhi of halting Vande Mataram mid-song, Congress denies it
cards.what_happened: On Independence Day, August 15, the Congress party sang the full version of Vande Mataram at its Delhi headquarters, which organizers say was a first. A row erupted when BJP leaders alleged that Congress Parliamentary Party chief **Sonia Gandhi** tried to stop the song partway through. Congress rejected this, saying she was simply asking for a chair for veteran leader **Mallikarjun Kharge**, who had been standing. On Sunday, August 16, Union Home Minister Amit Shah escalated the attack at a rally in Chittorgarh, Rajasthan, saying Gandhi's 'sins will never be forgiven' and demanding a public apology; West Bengal BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari echoed the demand. Separately, a descendant of the song's author wrote to Sonia Gandhi calling the incident a 'brazen repetition of a historical mistake.'
key_points: **Amit Shah** attacked Sonia Gandhi at a rally in **Chittorgarh, Rajasthan**
Alleges she stopped the national song **midway** at Congress HQ on Aug 15
Congress says she was only asking for a **chair** for Kharge, not stopping the song
Bankim Chandra's descendant wrote to Sonia Gandhi demanding an apology
West Bengal BJP's **Suvendu Adhikari** joined the call for an apology

depth.background: Vande Mataram, written by **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay**, is India's National Song — a status distinct from the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana. It carries a contested history: Congress has historically sung only the song's first two stanzas at official events, a practice tracing back to a **1937** debate in which Muhammad Ali Jinnah objected to the later verses' imagery. That history makes the song a recurring flashpoint the BJP uses to question Congress's patriotism.

cards.title: Government opens one-time window for small taxpayers to declare hidden foreign assets
cards.what_happened: The CBDT notified the **Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers – Disclosure Scheme Rules, 2026 (FAST-DS)**, which takes effect today, August 16, and stays open until **December 31, 2026**. It gives people who were Indian residents in the relevant year a one-time chance to voluntarily disclose foreign assets or income they failed to report. Under Category 1, undisclosed foreign assets/income up to **₹1 crore** in aggregate can be declared by paying 30% tax plus an equal penalty amount — an effective **60%** levy. Under Category 2, foreign assets bought with already-taxed money but never disclosed, valued up to **₹5 crore**, can be declared for a flat fee of **₹1 lakh**. Declarations must be filed electronically in Form 1, with March 31, 2026 fixed as the valuation date for computing asset values, and successful declarants get immunity from Black Money Act prosecution and penalty on the disclosed items.
key_points: New disclosure scheme **FAST-DS 2026** opens today, closes **December 31**
Covers undisclosed foreign assets/income up to **₹1 crore** in one track
Second track allows assets up to **₹5 crore** for a flat **₹1 lakh** fee
Effective tax on declared money can reach **60%** under the main track
Aimed at students, tech employees and NRIs who missed reporting foreign holdings

depth.background: Indian tax law requires residents to list every foreign bank account, stock, ESOP or property in a special section of their income-tax return called **Schedule FA**. Missing this — even by accident — can trigger India's strict **Black Money Act, 2015**, which allows heavy penalties and even prosecution regardless of intent. The scheme was first flagged in the **Union Budget 2026-27** as relief specifically for smaller, often unintentional, defaulters rather than large-scale tax evaders. The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has now notified the actual rules that bring it into force.

prev_ref.title: Himachal Pradesh's monsoon death toll climbs to 157 as floods and landslides batter the state

cards.title: Himachal Pradesh's monsoon death toll climbs to 183 in 47 days as losses cross ₹972 crore
cards.what_happened: State disaster management data now puts Himachal Pradesh's monsoon death toll at **183** across 47 days since June 30, up from the 157 recorded on August 9. Of the total, **104 deaths were road accidents** tied to landslide-hit roads, while the remaining **79 came from other hazards**: 14 from landslides directly, 27 from falls off steep rocks or trees, 15 from other weather-related incidents, 8 from snakebites, 8 from electrocution, 5 from drowning, and 1 in a flash flood. The state also reports **291 people injured** and **31 still missing**, with total property and infrastructure losses — roads, bridges, homes — now above **₹972 crore**. The State Emergency Operation Centre says **153 roads remain blocked**, **191 electricity transformers** are down, and **58 water supply schemes** are affected, with Mandi the worst-hit district.
key_points: The monsoon death toll in Himachal Pradesh has risen to **183** over **47 days**, up from 157 just six days earlier.
**104 of the 183 deaths** were road accidents linked to landslide-damaged or washed-out roads.
Property and infrastructure losses have crossed **₹972 crore** since June 30.
**291 people are injured** and **31 remain missing**, with 153 roads still blocked by landslides.

thread.previously: As of August 9, the toll stood at 157 (89 from road accidents, 68 from other hazards), with 257 injured and about ₹886 crore in losses; five districts were under an IMD orange alert.
thread.changed: Six days later, the toll has risen to 183 (104 road accidents, 79 other hazards), with 291 injured, 31 missing, and losses now above ₹972 crore — confirming road accidents on damaged routes remain the single biggest cause of death.

depth.background: Himachal Pradesh, a mountainous northern Indian state, has been enduring one of its **deadlier monsoon seasons in recent years**, with landslides and flash floods repeatedly cutting off roads and damaging homes across hill districts like **Mandi, Sirmaur, Kullu and Shimla**. As of August 9, the state's disaster management authorities had already put the toll at 157, with the majority of deaths caused indirectly — through road accidents on landslide-damaged routes — rather than by floods or landslides themselves.

prev_ref.title: West Bengal Congress leader and his son shot dead in Nadia, ahead of state elections

cards.title: West Bengal Congress holds statewide 'black day' after Nadia double killing
cards.what_happened: West Bengal Congress workers observed a **statewide 'black day'** on Sunday, a day after Anisur Rahman and his son Abu Sufian were shot and killed in Nadia district. The protest had been called by state Congress chief **Subhankar Sarkar** on Saturday night, immediately after the killings, and went ahead as planned across the state on Sunday with party workers demonstrating and demanding accountability. As of the protest, **police had not announced any arrests**, and the family's allegation that a jailed TMC leader was behind the attack has not been independently confirmed by investigators. A large police presence was deployed to the Nadia area, with an investigation described as ongoing.
key_points: The **West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee (WBPCC)** observed a **statewide black day** on Sunday over the Nadia killings.
No arrests have been announced yet in the deaths of **Anisur Rahman** and his son **Abu Sufian**, more than a day after the attack.
The protest keeps pressure on the state government just as **West Bengal's 2026 assembly elections** approach.
The family's allegation — that a jailed TMC leader was behind the attack — remains unconfirmed by police.

thread.previously: Congress leader Anisur Rahman and his son Abu Sufian were shot and attacked with sharp weapons in Nadia's Nakashipara area on Saturday evening; the family blamed a jailed TMC leader, and West Bengal Congress chief Subhankar Sarkar called for a statewide 'black day' protest on Sunday.
thread.changed: That called-for protest actually went ahead on Sunday, with Congress workers observing the black day across West Bengal to demand a proper investigation — while police have still not announced any arrests in the killings.

depth.background: Congress leader Anisur Rahman and his 24-year-old son Abu Sufian were killed near their home in Nadia district's Nakashipara area on Saturday evening, when attackers reportedly stopped their car and opened fire before attacking them with sharp weapons. West Bengal has a long, well-documented history of deadly political violence between the Trinamool Congress (TMC), BJP, and Congress/Left, especially in rural districts around election time. This killing comes as the state heads toward assembly elections due in 2026, a period when such violence has historically spiked.

cards.title: Modi's 'dimaagi Naxal' line in his Independence Day speech triggers a fierce BJP-Congress row over who counts as a threat
cards.what_happened: Speaking from the Red Fort on his 80th Independence Day address — his 13th consecutive one, and his shortest in four years at around 75 minutes — Modi said India has succeeded in clearing armed Naxals from the forests, but warned that 'dimaagi Naxals are looking for opportunities to create violence, unrest... they want to drag society on the wrong path.' He went further, saying such people 'have their place in the power corridors... were in government committees as advisors' and that 'Maoist thinking impacted policies,' calling on society to 'identify these ideological Naxalites and isolate them.' Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh hit back, calling it 'a sure sign of desperation' and arguing Modi 'ends up doing whatever these so-called urban Naxals or dimaagi Naxals are demanding' — a jab at policy inconsistency. BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari responded by saying Rahul Gandhi's own 'mindset reflects that of a dimaagi Naxal ecosystem.' The exchange continued into a second day of statements from both sides.
key_points: In his 80th Independence Day speech, Modi said armed Naxals are largely gone from India's forests but **'dimaagi Naxals'** — people with a Maoist mindset — remain, including inside **government advisory committees**.
Congress's **Jairam Ramesh** called it 'a sure sign of desperation,' arguing Modi is recycling his older 'urban Naxal' label under a new name.
BJP spokesperson **Pradeep Bhandari** turned the phrase back on the opposition, saying Rahul Gandhi's 'mindset reflects' that of a 'dimaagi Naxal ecosystem'.
The term has **no formal legal definition**, unlike 'Naxal', which refers to a decades-long armed Maoist insurgency in central-eastern India.
The row escalated into a second day of statements from both parties, continuing into today.

depth.background: **Naxalism** is a left-wing Maoist insurgency that has run in parts of central and eastern India for decades, and the government has said in recent years it has largely cleared armed Naxals from the forests they once controlled. For years, Modi and BJP leaders have also used the term **'urban Naxal'** to describe activists, academics, and government critics they accuse of sympathizing with Maoist ideology without taking up arms. By coining 'dimaagi Naxal' (literally 'mental/intellectual Naxal') and explicitly placing such people inside government committees, Modi appears to widen that label from outside critics to insiders shaping policy.

cards.title: India's private space sector has grown to 440 startups, with investment up sixfold since 2021
cards.what_happened: The Indian government told Parliament that the country now has roughly **440 registered space-technology startups** on its official Start-up India portal. Private investment into the sector has surged nearly sixfold, from **$100.5 million in 2021-22** to **$618.5 million** by the end of March 2026, with **$187 million** of that raised in 2026 alone. The sector's regulator, IN-SPACe, has granted **113 authorisations to 52 private companies**, including 18 recognized startups such as Skyroot Aerospace, Agnikul Cosmos, Dhruva Space, PixxelSpace, and Bellatrix Aerospace. Two commercial launches by private Indian companies are planned for FY 2026-27, with more than six additional launches expected in FY 2027-28, though that later launch schedule still needs regulatory approval.
key_points: India now has around **440 registered space-technology startups**, per government data shared in Parliament.
Private investment in India's space sector has grown **nearly sixfold**, from **$100.5 million in 2021-22** to **$618.5 million** by March 2026.
**$187 million** of that came in the current year (2026) alone.
The space regulator **IN-SPACe** has granted **113 authorisations to 52 private companies**, including 18 startups like Skyroot Aerospace, Agnikul Cosmos, and Dhruva Space.
Indian private firms are expected to complete **more than eight commercial rocket launches** over FY27 and FY28.

depth.background: India opened its space sector to private companies in 2020, ending decades of a state-run monopoly held by ISRO, the government space agency. Since then, a wave of startups — building everything from small satellites to their own rockets — has emerged, regulated by a new body called **IN-SPACe** that authorizes private space activity. The government has been actively courting private capital into the sector as part of a broader push to grow India's space economy.

cards.title: West Bengal Congress leader and his son shot dead in Nadia, ahead of state elections
cards.what_happened: Congress leader Anisur Rahman and his son Abu Sufian were killed near their home in the Nakashipara area of Nadia district, West Bengal, on Saturday evening. According to the family, the two were returning home by car from Bethua when attackers stopped the vehicle near the Nagadi rail gate and opened fire; the family says the pair were then also attacked with sharp weapons. West Bengal Congress president **Subhankar Sarkar** strongly condemned the killings and called for a **statewide black day** in protest on Sunday. The family has pointed to a jailed TMC leader as being behind the attack, an allegation that has not been independently confirmed. A large police force has been deployed to the area and an investigation is underway, with no arrests confirmed in initial reporting.
key_points: **Congress leader Anisur Rahman** and his son **Abu Sufian** were shot and attacked with sharp weapons near their home in Nadia's **Nakashipara** area on Saturday evening.
Attackers reportedly **stopped their car near a rail crossing** before opening fire; both were declared dead.
The victims' family has alleged a link to a **jailed TMC leader**, though police have not confirmed this and no arrests have been announced.
West Bengal Congress chief **Subhankar Sarkar** condemned the killings and called for a **statewide black day** on Sunday.
The killing lands amid a **long pattern of political violence** in rural West Bengal, ahead of the state's 2026 assembly elections.

depth.background: West Bengal has a long, well-documented history of deadly political violence between rival parties — Trinamool Congress (TMC), the BJP, and the Congress/Left — particularly in rural districts during and around election periods. Nadia, in the state's south, has seen repeated incidents of party workers and local leaders being attacked or killed over the years. This killing comes as the state gears up for **assembly elections due in 2026**, a period when such violence has historically spiked as local power struggles intensify.
