cards.title: Jharkhand exam-scandal hunger striker enters his 14th day, hospitalized, as protesters say Modi's new exam reforms don't go far enough
cards.what_happened: Devendra Nath Mahto is now on the **14th consecutive day** of his hunger strike and has been admitted to Sadar Hospital in Ranchi, after a march to gherao (surround) the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly turned chaotic when police responded with **lathi charges** (baton charges) against protesting students. When Mahto expressed a wish to leave the hospital and join Ranchi's Independence Day Tiranga Yatra (flag march) on August 15, police mounted a **heavy deployment outside his hospital room** and stopped him from attending. Protesters continue to demand the **cancellation of the JSSC-CGL recruitment exam** they say was compromised, along with a **CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation) probe** into the alleged irregularities — comprehensive reforms to the recruitment process generally. Jharkhand Chief Minister **Hemant Soren** has responded by launching an outreach initiative called 'Chhatron Ki Baat, Chhatron Ke Sath' (translating roughly to 'talking with students, standing with students') to solicit student input, but has not agreed to the specific demands. Students have warned they are prepared to escalate into a broader 'mass movement' if their demands continue to go unmet.
key_points: Student leader **Devendra Nath Mahto** is on the **14th day** of an indefinite hunger strike that began August 2.
He's been **admitted to Sadar Hospital** after a Vidhan Sabha gherao march turned chaotic when police used lathi charges.
Police mounted **heavy deployment outside his hospital room** on August 15 to stop him joining the Independence Day flag-hoisting march.
Protesters are demanding the **JSSC-CGL exam be cancelled** and a **CBI probe** into alleged irregularities — neither has happened yet.
Jharkhand's Chief Minister Hemant Soren has launched a student-outreach program, but **the hunger strike hasn't stopped**.

thread.previously: We reported that President Murmu announced sweeping national exam reforms in response to nationwide protests over recruitment-exam paper leaks.
thread.changed: The protest that triggered those reforms hasn't ended — its most visible leader, Devendra Nath Mahto, is now on the 14th day of an indefinite hunger strike, has been hospitalized, and was blocked by police from joining Independence Day's flag-hoisting march, showing Jharkhand's protesters see the national reforms as insufficient.

depth.background: The protests trace back to alleged **irregularities in recruitment exams** run by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) — students allege leaked questions and a rigged, opaque selection process that has cost thousands of young job-seekers a fair shot at coveted government jobs. Devendra Nath Mahto began an indefinite hunger strike on **August 2** as the movement's central, symbolic act of protest. The unrest grew large enough that it became a national story, feeding into **President Murmu's announcement of nationwide exam reforms** during her Independence Day address on August 15 — but that announcement was a general, national-level fix, not the specific local demands (cancelling the JSSC-CGL exam, a CBI investigation) that Jharkhand's protesters are asking for.

cards.title: One of three missing workers found dead as Chamoli tunnel rescue enters its third day
cards.what_happened: Water and debris suddenly surged into an under-construction tail-race tunnel at the Vishnugad-Pipalkoti hydroelectric project near Mayapur-Pipalkoti around **7 pm on August 13**, after a landslide or underground cavity opened roughly 1.4-1.5 km inside the tunnel. **22 workers** were trapped; **19 were pulled out** during an overnight rescue operation, but 7 were confirmed dead and 3 remained missing the following day. On **Saturday, August 15**, one of the three missing workers was located and declared dead at hospital, bringing the confirmed toll to **8 dead**, with 2 workers still unaccounted for. Rescue teams — including the NDRF, SDRF and ITBP — have only advanced a few hundred metres into the tunnel because the water level inside remains around a metre or higher, and continuous rainfall is hampering efforts to pump it out and clear debris. Uttarakhand's disaster management minister, Madan Kaushik, visited the site and said search efforts would continue without pause until the remaining workers are found.
key_points: One of the **three workers still missing** after a Uttarakhand hydropower tunnel disaster was found Saturday and **declared dead at hospital** — taking the toll to 8, with 2 still missing.
The disaster struck on **August 13**, when water and debris rushed into a tunnel at the **Vishnugad-Pipalkoti hydroelectric project**, trapping 22 workers about 1.4-1.5 km inside.
**19 workers were pulled out alive** in the hours after the collapse; rescuers are still trying to reach the last two, over a kilometre inside the flooded tunnel.
Continuous rain and a **water level still around a metre or more** inside the tunnel are slowing NDRF, SDRF, ITBP and police rescue teams.
Uttarakhand's disaster management minister visited the site and said the **"rescue will continue till the end."**

depth.background: The Vishnugad-Pipalkoti project is a **444-megawatt hydroelectric dam** being built by **THDC India Limited** on the Alaknanda river in Chamoli district — a Himalayan region that has seen repeated tunnel and glacier disasters, most notably the deadly 2021 Tapovan glacial-burst flood that killed dozens of workers in a similar under-construction tunnel nearby. Tunnelling through the young, geologically unstable Himalayas is inherently risky: a sudden landslide or hidden underground cavity can let in enormous volumes of water and debris with almost no warning — which investigators believe is what happened here.

cards.title: Maharashtra regulator suspends 14 quick-commerce dark-store licences over food safety violations
cards.what_happened: The Maharashtra FDA carried out a state-wide inspection drive covering **86 quick-commerce facilities** on August 13 and, on **August 14**, suspended the operating licences of **14 of them** — 5 linked to Blinkit, 5 to Zepto, 2 to Instamart, and one each to two smaller operators — citing serious food-safety and hygiene violations. Inspectors found specific breaches including a Blinkit chiller in Malad West running at **6°C**, above safe cold-chain limits; a Zepto facility in Pune's Lohegaon storing products beyond their declared "Use By" dates; and an Instamart site in Andheri keeping food packets directly on the floor with inadequate storage space. Beyond the 14 suspensions, the FDA issued **60 improvement notices** to other facilities and ordered one to stop operations immediately, though it stopped short of permanently cancelling any licence. The inspection checked practices including temperature control, pest control, staff hygiene, and whether facilities followed **FIFO/FEFO** stock rotation.
key_points: Maharashtra's **Food and Drug Administration (FDA)** suspended the licences of **14 dark stores** run by Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after a snap inspection drive.
Inspectors covered **86 facilities** across the state; violations ranged from food stored on the floor to products kept **past their "Use By" dates**.
Of the 14 suspended, **5 were Blinkit**, **5 were Zepto**, and **2 were Instamart** outlets, plus two smaller operators.
A Blinkit facility in Mumbai's Malad West had its chiller running at **6°C** — above the safe limit for the perishables it stored.
The FDA also issued **60 improvement notices** and ordered one facility to halt operations immediately, though no licences were permanently cancelled.

depth.background: "Dark stores" are the small, customer-inaccessible warehouses that power India's **10-minute grocery delivery boom** — Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart have built thousands of them in cities to promise near-instant delivery. That speed depends on tight, high-turnover storage of fresh and perishable food, which is exactly where food-safety risk concentrates: a warehouse racing to restock and dispatch orders in minutes has less margin for error on temperature control, expiry tracking and hygiene than a traditional, slower-moving retail store.

cards.title: Modi says India's 'Iron Dome' — the Sudarshan Chakra air shield — is progressing rapidly, a year after he announced it
cards.what_happened: In his 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort, Modi said work on the Sudarshan Chakra system was moving quickly, though he did not give a specific deployment timeline. He paired the update with broader defence statistics — India's domestic defence output near **₹1.78 lakh crore** for FY26 and exports of **₹38,424 crore** to almost 100 countries — and urged greater investment in drone and counter-drone systems, framing self-reliant defence manufacturing as central to his 'Viksit Bharat' (developed India) vision.
key_points: PM Modi said the indigenous **Sudarshan Chakra** air defence shield, which he first announced exactly a year ago on Independence Day 2025, is progressing **"rapidly."**
India's domestic defence production has grown to **₹1.78 lakh crore** (about **$21 billion**) in FY26, up from just ₹46,000 crore in 2014.
Defence **exports** have risen roughly **50-fold** to **₹38,424 crore**, now reaching close to **100 countries**.
Modi also called for greater investment in **drones and counter-drone technology** as India pushes for defence self-reliance.

depth.background: Modi announced the Sudarshan Chakra project on Independence Day 2025, describing it as an Israel-style **Iron Dome** to shield vital military and civilian sites from missile and drone attack. The push for indigenous defence manufacturing has accelerated in recent years as India seeks to cut its historic reliance on imported weapons, particularly from Russia, and to build an export-capable defence industry of its own. The announcement also lands against a backdrop of recent India-Pakistan military tension and DRDO's stated role in prior cross-border operations.

cards.title: Email bomb threat citing Khalistan and 1984 riots puts Delhi on high alert hours before Independence Day
cards.what_happened: Threat emails arrived in a rapid sequence on August 14 — the Delhi Cantonment SDM office around **11:18 AM**, IGI Airport's Terminal 3 at **11:32 AM**, Jamnagar House at **11:40 AM**, and an office in Saket at **11:42 AM** — before the Delhi High Court received its own threat naming a specific blast time of 2:11 PM on August 15. Security agencies, already running a massive Independence Day operation with more than **25,000 personnel**, anti-drone systems and over **20,000 people screened** around the Red Fort, launched additional sweeps at every named location. No explosives were found anywhere, and authorities have concluded the threats were hoaxes, though multi-agency teams continue investigating who sent them and why so many locations were targeted at once.
key_points: A wave of **email bomb threats** hit the **Delhi High Court, Red Fort, IGI Airport Terminal 3** and government offices starting the morning of **August 14**, a day before Independence Day.
One message explicitly referenced **Khalistan** (the movement for a separate Sikh homeland) and the **1984 anti-Sikh riots**.
The Delhi High Court received a threat warning of a blast at **2:11 PM on August 15** — timed for Independence Day itself.
Extensive searches found **no explosives or suspicious objects**; security agencies have declared the threats **hoaxes** but are still tracing the emails' origin.

depth.background: The Red Fort and central Delhi are always under heavy security for Independence Day, when the Prime Minister addresses the nation from the Fort's ramparts in front of large public crowds. Coordinated bomb-threat hoaxes targeting courts, airports and landmarks have recurred periodically in Indian cities in recent years, usually traced to anonymous emails rather than real devices. This round is notable for explicitly invoking Khalistani symbolism and the 1984 riots, a historically sensitive reference, rather than being a generic threat.

cards.title: Opposition pounces on Modi's Independence Day speech fumble and 'dimaagi Naxal' remark
cards.what_happened: During his address, Modi appeared to **fumble while citing statistics on India's bioeconomy growth** since 2014, a moment Congress and AAP leaders quickly clipped and shared on social media. Congress's **Pawan Khera** described Modi as **"an under-confident, nervous and shaky Prime Minister,"** and AAP chief **Arvind Kejriwal** offered similar criticism of the delivery. Separately, a remark using the phrase **"dimaagi Naxal"** — loosely, someone who is a "Naxal [left-wing extremist] in their thinking" — aimed at critics of the government drew accusations of inflammatory, divisive language on a day meant to unite the country. Congress also renewed substantive criticism, accusing the government of a **"dishonest pitch"** on **women's reservation in Parliament** and of reversing its earlier opposition to a **caste census** before announcing one itself. The **BJP defended** the speech, casting it as a genuine roadmap for **"Viksit Bharat"** by 2047.
key_points: Modi **stumbled while citing bioeconomy growth figures** during his 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort.
Congress's **Pawan Khera** called him **"under-confident, nervous and shaky"**; AAP's **Arvind Kejriwal** echoed the criticism.
A **"dimaagi Naxal"** (roughly, "Naxal in the mind") remark aimed at government critics drew sharp opposition backlash.
Congress accused the government of a **"dishonest pitch"** on women's reservation and flip-flopping on the **caste census**.
The **BJP has defended** the speech as a roadmap for a **"Viksit Bharat" (developed India)**.

depth.background: Every August 15, India's Prime Minister addresses the nation from the ramparts of the **Red Fort** in Delhi — the most-watched political speech of the year, traditionally used to set the government's agenda. This year marked India's **80th year of independence**, and Modi used the speech to announce a slate of new initiatives under the banner **"Shakti Ki Saptadhara."** Opposition parties, led by **Congress** and the **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)**, routinely contest the government's framing and record in the speech's aftermath, and this year's reaction has focused as much on how Modi delivered the speech as on what he said.

prev_ref.title: Sensex and Nifty slip at midday as oil prices firm on fears of a US naval blockade at the Strait of Hormuz

cards.title: Sensex and Nifty claw back most of the day's losses to close only slightly lower
cards.what_happened: India's benchmark indices opened weak and slid further at midday on **Friday, August 14**, as fears about a potential **US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz** pushed crude oil prices higher. By the close, the **BSE Sensex** had recovered most of its losses to end down just **71 points (0.09%) at 78,009.25**, while the **Nifty 50** settled **0.12% lower at 24,366**, helped by **softer-than-expected US inflation data** and broadly positive global cues. The **Bank Nifty** fell a sharper **144 points (0.25%)** to close at **57,491**. Selling was concentrated in **auto, energy, FMCG, metal, pharma and realty** stocks, while **consumer durables and media** shares bucked the trend and gained. Broader markets underperformed the benchmarks, with the **Nifty Midcap 100 down 0.53%** and the **Nifty Smallcap 100 down 0.69%**.
key_points: The **Sensex fell just 71 points (-0.09%)** to close at **78,009**, recovering from a much steeper drop earlier in the day.
The **Nifty 50 dropped 0.12%** to settle at **24,366**.
Markets had sunk further at midday on fears of a **US naval blockade at the Strait of Hormuz**, a key oil chokepoint.
**Softer US inflation data** and positive global cues helped indices recover off their intraday lows.
**Auto, energy, FMCG, metal, pharma and realty** stocks dragged, while **consumer durables and media** shares gained.

thread.previously: Sensex and Nifty had slipped at midday on Friday as oil prices firmed on fears of a US naval blockade at the Strait of Hormuz.
thread.changed: By the close, markets had recovered most of that loss — the Sensex ended down just 71 points and the Nifty 0.12% lower — helped by softer US inflation data, even as auto, metal, and energy stocks stayed under pressure.

depth.background: Indian markets had a rough start on Friday, sliding further at midday as fears grew that the **US might blockade the Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through — amid elevated US-Iran tension. A blockade there would squeeze global oil supply and push up prices, which matters enormously for **India**, one of the world's largest oil importers, because costlier crude widens India's trade deficit and adds to inflation. By the close, though, markets had pared back most of that morning loss.

cards.title: ITBP Deputy Inspector General killed in head-on highway collision in Saharanpur
cards.what_happened: Around 11 am, ITBP DIG Parminder Singh was travelling in a Scorpio vehicle on the Dehradun–Panchkula National Highway near Sarsawa police station in Saharanpur district, Uttar Pradesh, when the vehicle struck a road divider and then collided head-on with an oncoming Swift car. **Singh and his driver Ramsharan died** at the scene or shortly after. The DIG's gunner sustained serious injuries, and three occupants of the Swift — Gurunanak Singh, Devendra Kaur and Gurnam Singh — were also injured. All the injured were admitted to the medical college in Pilkhani for treatment.
key_points: ITBP **Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Parminder Singh, 52**, and his driver Ramsharan, 35, were killed in the crash.
It happened around **11 am** on the Dehradun–Panchkula national highway near Sarsawa police station, Saharanpur.
Singh's vehicle hit a **road divider** and then collided head-on with an oncoming Swift car.
The DIG's gunner and three occupants of the other car were **injured** and taken to hospital in Pilkhani.
ITBP is the **Indo-Tibetan Border Police**, a paramilitary force that guards India's Himalayan frontier.

depth.background: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) is one of India's central armed police forces, primarily responsible for guarding the mountainous India-China border. A Deputy Inspector General is a senior field-command rank within the force. High-speed convoy or official-vehicle accidents on Indian national highways are unfortunately common, and this crash claimed the life of a serving senior officer in transit.

prev_ref.title: India readies its 80th Independence Day, reviving 'Vande Mataram' at the Red Fort for the first time in 150 years

cards.title: Modi unveils 'Shakti Ki Saptadhara' — seven pillars for Viksit Bharat — in his 80th Independence Day speech
cards.what_happened: Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on August 15, Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled a new organizing framework for India's growth called **'Shakti Ki Saptadhara'** — seven streams of strength he said would power the country's next phase of development. The seven pillars are manufacturing, agriculture and food processing, technology and innovation, **Gati Shakti** (India's infrastructure and logistics connectivity push covering rail, highways, waterways, airports, and ports), defence production, the green and blue economy, and India's cultural soft power. On manufacturing, Modi called for India to become a reliable hub in global supply chains, 'from design to manufacturing.' On defence, he said self-reliance and becoming a global supplier of military hardware was now a national priority. He framed the challenge in stark terms, saying India needed to accomplish in five to seven years what it had not managed in the previous five to seven decades.
key_points: PM Modi unveiled **'Shakti Ki Saptadhara'** (Seven Streams of Strength), naming seven pillars to drive India toward **Viksit Bharat 2047**.
The seven streams: **manufacturing**, agriculture and food processing, technology and innovation, **Gati Shakti** connectivity, defence production, the green and blue economy, and India's soft power.
Modi called for India to become a **reliable global manufacturing hub**, 'from design to manufacturing.'
He set defence production as a priority, saying India must become **self-reliant** and a **global arms supplier**.
Modi said India must achieve in the next **five to seven years** what wasn't achieved in the previous **five to seven decades**.

thread.previously: Yesterday's brief covered the government's finalized plans for the ceremony itself — the first-ever singing of 'Vande Mataram' from the Red Fort ramparts, a 2,500-strong human formation spelling the song's name, and an AI-translated broadcast of the PM's speech in over 22 languages.
thread.changed: The ceremony has now happened, and the substance of Modi's speech is known: he used it to unveil 'Shakti Ki Saptadhara,' a new seven-pillar framework for India's growth strategy, rather than just the ceremonial elements previewed yesterday.

depth.background: Every Indian Independence Day since 1947 features a prime ministerial address from the ramparts of the **Red Fort** in Delhi, a platform governments use to set the year's political and policy tone. Modi has repeatedly used this speech to frame his government's long-term economic vision, **'Viksit Bharat 2047'** — the goal of making India a fully developed economy by the 100th anniversary of independence. This year's address, his 13th as PM and the nation's 80th Independence Day, built on themes the government had already previewed — a 'Yuva Shakti' (youth power) framing and the revival of the patriotic song 'Vande Mataram' at the ceremony for the first time.

cards.title: Chief Justice Surya Kant says his 'cockroach' remark was misquoted and used with 'malicious intent' to mislead youth
cards.what_happened: In a DD News interview aired Thursday, August 14, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant addressed the ongoing controversy over his May 'cockroach' remark directly, saying it was 'misquoted' and that 'what was not said is presented as though it was said' in what he called a 'major malicious attempt to mislead the youth of the country.' He clarified the original comment was aimed specifically at people holding fraudulent educational degrees who use activism as cover, not at India's youth in general. The remark had already triggered significant public backlash, including the emergence of the satirical 'Cockroach Janta Party' movement, which grew to roughly three million followers within days. The CJI also used the interview to call for a formal protocol around how courts' informal oral observations are reported by the media, arguing the current lack of context in reporting can distort what judges actually mean.
key_points: **CJI Surya Kant** told DD News his May courtroom remark comparing certain people to 'cockroaches' was **misquoted** and taken out of context.
The original remark, made **May 15**, targeted holders of **fraudulent degrees** who allegedly pose as activists — not youth broadly, he said.
He called the spread of the clip a **'major malicious attempt'** to mislead the country's young people.
The remark had already sparked a satirical online movement, the **'Cockroach Janta Party,'** which gained **3 million followers within 78 hours**.
The CJI also called for a **protocol on reporting oral court observations**, which are often informal and not part of a final ruling.

depth.background: In India, judges frequently make informal spoken remarks during court hearings — called **'oral observations'** — that are distinct from a court's final written judgment but are often reported by media and go viral on social media, sometimes stripped of context. On May 15, Chief Justice of India **Surya Kant**, the country's top judge, made a courtroom comment comparing people who hold fraudulent degrees and pose as social-media or RTI (Right to Information) activists to 'cockroaches.' Clips of the remark spread rapidly online, and a satirical protest movement calling itself the 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP) emerged, reportedly gaining three million Instagram followers within 78 hours, widely read as a youth-led backlash against the remark.

cards.title: Government cuts export tax on petrol, diesel and jet fuel as crude prices ease
cards.what_happened: Effective **August 15, 2026**, India's government cut export duties on petrol, diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF). The **petrol export duty was scrapped entirely**, dropping from ₹3.5 per litre (set August 3) to **zero**. The **diesel** windfall tax was cut to **₹24/litre** from ₹25.5, and the **ATF** rate was cut to **₹19.5/litre** from ₹22. The finance ministry clarified there is **no change to domestic retail fuel prices** — these levies apply only to fuel Indian refiners sell abroad, not what consumers pay at the pump.
key_points: Export duty on **petrol cut to zero**, from **₹3.5/litre** charged just two weeks earlier.
**Diesel** export tax (SAED) cut to **₹24/litre**, down from **₹25.5**.
**ATF (jet fuel)** export tax cut to **₹19.5/litre**, down from **₹22**.
Domestic pump prices for petrol and diesel are **unchanged** — this only affects fuel sold abroad.

depth.background: India taxes fuel exports through a **'windfall tax'** (formally the Special Additional Excise Duty, SAED), first introduced in 2022 when refiners were earning outsized profits exporting fuel refined from cheap Russian crude while domestic supply tightened. The government reviews and adjusts these rates roughly every two weeks based on international oil and fuel prices — raising them when refiner margins spike, cutting them when crude prices fall. Less than two weeks before this cut, the government had actually **raised** these same export levies, reflecting how quickly crude markets have been swinging amid the broader Iran-linked Middle East tensions.

cards.title: Modi says India will add 5-8 more semiconductor plants within 7-8 years
cards.what_happened: In his Independence Day address from Delhi's Red Fort, Prime Minister Modi said India has entered 'a new phase' in chip-making, noting that **three plants — run by Micron, Kaynes and CG Semi — have already started commercial production and begun exporting**. He said India could see **another five to eight semiconductor plants become operational over the next seven to eight years**. Officials noted **12 semiconductor projects have been approved across six states**, representing investment commitments exceeding **₹1.64 lakh crore**. Modi's speech came weeks after the government approved **'Semicon 2.0'** in July, a larger **₹1,27,500 crore** program that funds not just chip fabrication but also **chip design, intellectual property and system design** — the higher-value engineering work India has mostly imported until now. He also announced a plan to train **one crore (10 million) young people** in AI skills within a year.
key_points: Three chip plants — **Micron, Kaynes, CG Semi** — are already producing and exporting, Modi said.
India will add **5 to 8 more semiconductor plants** over the next **7-8 years**.
**12 projects** are already approved across six states, worth over **₹1.64 lakh crore** (~$19.5 billion).
A new **'Semicon 2.0'** scheme worth **₹1,27,500 crore** ($15B+) now also funds chip design and IP, not just fabs.
Government will train **1 crore (10 million) youth** in AI skills over the next year.

depth.background: India has spent years trying to break into semiconductor manufacturing — the industry that makes the chips inside every phone, car and data center — an industry dominated by Taiwan, South Korea and the US. Delhi's original semiconductor incentive scheme, launched in 2021-22, offered subsidies to attract fabs; progress was slow at first, with the first approved plants only starting output in the past year or so. On India's **80th Independence Day**, delivering his traditional address from the Red Fort, Modi used the milestone speech to argue the country has now moved from planning to actual production.

cards.title: Modi announces a nationwide talent hunt for kids as young as 5, as India eyes hosting the 2036 Olympics
cards.what_happened: Speaking from the Red Fort on India's **80th Independence Day**, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country wants to host the **2036 Olympics** and needs to begin preparing now. He announced a **nationwide talent hunt** scouting for sporting ability from village to village, city to city and school to school, focused on children aged **5 to 15**, who would get their abilities assessed and receive specialized training. Modi framed the push as part of a broader seven-point vision he called **"Shakti Ki Saptadhara"** ("seven streams of power") for a **"Viksit Bharat"** (developed India) by 2047, alongside plans to promote India's soft power — yoga, Ayurveda, handicrafts, films, animation and gaming — to draw foreign tourists. It was Modi's **13th consecutive** Independence Day address, making him only the second PM after Jawaharlal Nehru to reach that mark.
key_points: Modi says India is a **strong contender** to host the **2036 Olympics**
A nationwide **talent hunt** will scout children aged **5 to 15** in villages, cities and schools
Scouted kids get **specialized training** to become future Olympic athletes
Announcement came in his **13th consecutive** Independence Day speech, unveiling 'Shakti Ki Saptadhara'

depth.background: India has never hosted an Olympic Games and has historically won very few medals relative to its population — a gap officials blame on weak grassroots talent identification and sports infrastructure. In recent years the government has tried to close that gap through programs like the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, which funds elite athletes directly, and **Khelo India**, a broader sports-development initiative. **Ahmedabad** has emerged as India's proposed host city if a 2036 bid goes ahead, and officials say preparation needs to start well over a decade in advance.

cards.title: President Murmu unveils sweeping exam reforms after nationwide protests over paper leaks
cards.what_happened: On the eve of India's 80th Independence Day, President **Droupadi Murmu** used her nationally televised address to lay out the government's response to the protests: the **Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026**, which took effect on **July 31**. The law sets prison terms of up to **10 years** and fines up to **₹50 lakh** for individuals caught cheating or leaking papers, and penalties up to **₹10 crore** for organized cheating syndicates. Murmu also announced a high-powered task force chaired by **Nandan Nilekani** — the Infosys co-founder known for building India's Aadhaar digital-identity system — to design technology-driven methods that make future exams harder to leak.
key_points: New law imposes up to **10 years in prison** and a **₹50 lakh fine** for individual exam cheats
Organized cheating syndicates face penalties up to **₹10 crore**
A task force chaired by **Nandan Nilekani** will design **leak-proof** exam technology
Reforms followed **Gen Z-led protests** at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak

depth.background: India runs some of the world's largest and highest-stakes competitive exams — **NEET-UG** for medical college admission among them — taken by millions of students each year, often deciding their entire career path. Repeated leaks of exam papers before test day have triggered public fury, since a leak can mean re-tests, delayed results, or an unfair edge for students who paid for stolen questions. A leak in the NEET-UG exam set off nationwide protests, concentrated at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, pressure serious enough that it contributed to the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan** as Union Education Minister.

cards.title: Modi renews his push for women's reservation in Parliament, months after the enabling bill fell short in the Lok Sabha
cards.what_happened: Speaking from the ramparts of the Red Fort on India's 80th Independence Day, Modi devoted part of his address to reviving the women's reservation issue, calling it the **'call of the hour'** for Indian democracy and pointing to the role women already play as elected representatives in panchayats and municipal bodies. He urged **all political parties**, not just his own, to come together and ensure the 33% quota actually gets implemented in the Lok Sabha and state legislatures. He framed the delay as decades of political **'akhada'** (wrestling-ring) manoeuvring, saying the issue had been stuck in this back-and-forth for roughly **40 years** before Parliament finally passed the underlying law in 2023. The speech came four months after his own government's follow-up bill to activate that law failed in the Lok Sabha in April 2026, falling well short of the two-thirds threshold and forcing two connected bills to be withdrawn. The Congress-led opposition did not respond to the substance of the appeal; instead, sparring on Independence Day centred on other issues, including the Leader of the Opposition's absence from the Red Fort ceremony and the government's record on women's safety.
key_points: In his 80th Independence Day speech, Modi called **33% reservation for women** in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies the **'call of the hour'** and urged every political party to back it.
The reservation law already exists on paper — the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** took legal effect in **April 2026** — but it cannot actually seat a single woman yet.
The follow-up bill needed to switch it on, the **Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026**, fell **54 votes short** of the two-thirds majority it needed in the Lok Sabha this April.
Because that vote failed, real implementation now waits on the **2027 census** and a fresh redrawing of constituency boundaries, pushing actual women's seats out to roughly **2034**.
Modi accused the opposition of stalling the issue for **'four decades'**; Congress did not engage directly and instead hit back on unrelated fronts.

depth.background: India has debated a law reserving one-third of Lok Sabha and state assembly seats for women since the mid-1990s, with multiple bills introduced and lapsing over nearly three decades. Parliament finally passed the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** (the 106th Constitutional Amendment) in 2023, and it formally came into force on **16 April 2026** — but the law itself said the quota could only kick in *after* the next delimitation, the redrawing of constituency boundaries based on fresh census data. To trigger that delimitation early, the government brought the **Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026** to the Lok Sabha this April, alongside a Delimitation Bill and a Union Territories Laws Amendment Bill. That attempt collapsed: the bill won only **298 of the 352 votes** required for the constitutionally mandated two-thirds special majority, forcing the government to withdraw the two dependent bills as well.

cards.title: Assam's flood death toll climbs to 104 as the monsoon disaster drags into its second month
cards.what_happened: The Assam State Disaster Management Authority confirmed on **Friday, August 14** that one more death in Sivasagar district pushed the state's cumulative flood toll for 2026 to **104**, while the number of people still affected ticked up slightly to over **78,000**. Floodwaters continue to affect **313 villages across 20 revenue circles** in seven districts — Nagaon, Golaghat, Sivasagar, Kamrup, Hojai, Jorhat and Lakhimpur — with Golaghat the worst hit at roughly **30,778 affected people**, followed by Nagaon at **26,292**. The state is running dozens of relief camps and distribution centres, and boats have evacuated well over a hundred stranded residents in the worst-hit pockets. CM Himanta Biswa Sarma separately announced **₹11.3 crore** to rebuild flood-damaged Anganwadi (government childcare) centres across four districts, while West Bengal's government pledged **₹10 crore** from its own relief fund and India's TVS Group donated **₹5 crore**. Officials say no major river is currently flowing above the danger mark, suggesting the worst of this wave may be passing even as the human cost keeps climbing.
key_points: Assam's 2026 flood death toll has risen to **104** after a fresh death in **Sivasagar district**.
Over **78,000 people** remain affected across **seven districts**, even as the overall numbers slowly recede.
**313 villages** in **20 revenue circles** are still under floodwater, with Golaghat the worst-hit at over **30,000 people**.
Assam's government is running **31 relief camps** and has committed **₹11.3 crore** just to rebuild flood-hit childcare centres.
Neighbouring **West Bengal** has chipped in **₹10 crore** in inter-state relief aid.

depth.background: Assam floods almost every monsoon because it sits in the floodplain of the **Brahmaputra** and its tributaries, one of the world's most flood-prone river systems, fed by heavy rain both locally and upstream in the Himalayas. This year's flooding began in early August 2026 and the death toll passed the symbolic **100 mark on August 10**, driven by a mix of river overflow, embankment breaches and landslide-triggered flash floods in low-lying districts like **Golaghat, Nagaon and Sivasagar**. Assam's government, led by Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, activates a standard playbook every year — relief camps, boat evacuations and central disaster funds — but chronic under-investment in embankments means the damage repeats with only the scale varying.

cards.title: Modi sets a target of 100 GW nuclear power by 2047, a more than tenfold jump from today
cards.what_happened: In his **13th consecutive Independence Day address** from the Red Fort, PM Modi announced India is aiming for **100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047** — the year the country marks a century of independence — as part of his 'Viksit Bharat' (developed India) roadmap. He said India would commission and operationalise **five new nuclear reactors over the next 6-7 years**, and declared the country had this year achieved mastery of **Fast Breeder Reactor technology**, which lets a reactor generate more nuclear fuel than it consumes — a step Modi called crucial to atomic fuel self-reliance. The target marks a jump of more than **11 times today's roughly 8.8 GW** of installed nuclear capacity, which currently supplies only about 3% of India's power. The push builds on the 2025 SHANTI Act, which for the first time allows private firms to build and license nuclear facilities, plus the dedicated Nuclear Energy Mission funding SMRs. Modi explicitly framed the goal as an 'energy security' imperative, language that echoed growing unease in New Delhi about oil-supply risk following weeks of tension around the Strait of Hormuz.
key_points: PM Modi set a target of **100 GW of nuclear power by 2047**, the year India turns **100 years independent**.
That's more than **tenfold India's current nuclear capacity** of roughly **8.8 GW**.
India plans to commission **five new nuclear reactors within the next 6-7 years**.
The **2025 SHANTI Act** lets **private companies** build and run nuclear plants for the first time.
Modi says India achieved 'mastery' of **Fast Breeder Reactor technology** this year, a step toward fuel self-reliance.

depth.background: India's nuclear power program has been a tightly closed **government monopoly** run by the state-owned Nuclear Power Corporation of India (NPCIL) for decades, and today contributes only about **3% of India's electricity** despite the country being the world's most populous and one of its fastest-growing power markets. Because India sits outside the mainstream global nuclear trade regime, it has historically had restricted access to imported uranium fuel and foreign reactor technology, which slowed expansion for years. In 2025, Parliament passed the **SHANTI Act**, opening the sector to private investment for the first time, alongside a new Nuclear Energy Mission that has earmarked **Rs 20,000 crore** for small modular reactors (SMRs). Modi's 100 GW target, unveiled from the Red Fort on India's **80th Independence Day**, is the most explicit numeric goal any government has put on the country's atomic-energy ambitions.

cards.source: Press Information Bureau (PIB), Government of India
cards.title: Modi announces 'next-gen' GST reform as a Diwali gift in his 80th Independence Day speech
cards.what_happened: Speaking from the Red Fort on **August 15, India's 80th Independence Day**, PM Modi announced that the government will bring in **'Next-Generation GST reforms'**, explicitly framing them as **'a Diwali gift'** for ordinary citizens by reducing the tax burden on daily-use items. He said the government has prepared a detailed proposal for **broad-based GST rate rationalisation** — meaning fewer, simpler slabs — aimed at making life easier and cheaper for the common man. The ceremony also featured **'Vande Mataram'**, India's national song, performed as part of the official Red Fort programme for the first time since the song was written 150 years ago. Modi's address was his 13th in a row from the ramparts, a run matched only by Jawaharlal Nehru.
key_points: In his **13th consecutive Independence Day speech** from the Red Fort, Modi announced **Next-Generation GST reforms** to cut taxes on everyday goods.
He called the tax cuts a **'Diwali gift'** for citizens, promising the changes will land before the festival season.
The stated goal is to **lower the tax burden on the common man** and boost consumer spending by simplifying GST slabs and rates.
The speech also revived **'Vande Mataram'** in the official Red Fort ceremony for the first time in the song's **150-year history**.
This is Modi's **80th Independence Day** as PM, making him only the **second PM after Nehru** to deliver 13 straight I-Day addresses.

depth.background: **GST (Goods and Services Tax)** is India's main consumption tax, charged on almost everything bought and sold, split across multiple rate 'slabs' (currently ranging roughly 5% to 28%) that businesses and consumers have long complained are confusing and, in places, too high. Simplifying GST has been discussed for years as a way to cut prices for consumers and reduce compliance headaches for small businesses, but slab changes require **agreement between the Centre and states**, since both share GST revenue. Independence Day speeches from the Red Fort are traditionally where Indian prime ministers set the year's policy tone.

sources.name: Press Information Bureau (PIB), Government of India

cards.title: India will count caste in a census for the first time since 1931
cards.what_happened: India's **Registrar General and Census Commissioner** notified a finalized set of **40 questions** for the 2027 Census, confirmed on **August 14**, with caste enumeration placed at **question number 10** — marking the first time since **1931**, and the first time ever since Independence, that the census will record caste data for **every community**, not just Scheduled Castes and Tribes. The form also covers religion, education, employment, migration and family structure, and — new for this round — will ask for **Aadhaar numbers, mobile numbers, voter IDs, bank account details and COVID-19 vaccination status** where people have them. Census 2027 will also be India's **first digital census**, giving people the option to fill in their own responses online (self-enumeration) rather than only through door-to-door enumerators.
key_points: The Home Ministry has notified a final list of **40 questions** for Census 2027 — and for the first time since **1931**, it includes a full **caste enumeration** for every community.
Past censuses only counted **Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes**; this will be the first to count **all castes**, not just those two categories.
Census 2027 will be India's **first digital census**, with an optional **self-enumeration** option letting people fill in their own details online.
The form will also collect **Aadhaar, voter ID, mobile number and bank account details**, where available — a major expansion in scope.
The decision to add caste data was approved by the government back in **2025**; this notification sets the actual questions.

depth.background: India has run a **population census roughly every 10 years since 1881**, but the last full one was in **2011** — the usual 2021 round was delayed, first by COVID and then by the caste-data decision itself. India's caste system groups people into thousands of hereditary communities, and whether the government should officially count everyone's caste (not just Dalits and Adivasis, who get constitutional protections) has been **politically explosive for decades**, because caste data underpins arguments over **reservation (affirmative action) quotas** in jobs and education. Several states, including Bihar, have already run their own local caste surveys in recent years, adding pressure on the Centre to do a national one.

cards.title: L&T wins a $1.57 billion order to build India's biggest AI data centre, in a bet on the global AI compute boom
cards.what_happened: **Larsen & Toubro** announced on **August 13, 2026** that it secured an order worth up to **$1.57 billion** from **Together AI**, a US-based AI cloud platform, to build and host an AI data centre in **Chennai**. The facility, run through L&T's new AI-infrastructure arm **LTN Compute** at its Vyoma.AI campus, will house **10,000 Nvidia B300 chips** — the largest such deployment announced in India to date. It will support Together AI's cloud platform for AI training, fine-tuning and inference. L&T shares rose as much as **1.2%** in trading following the announcement.
key_points: **Larsen & Toubro** won an order worth up to **$1.57 billion (₹150 billion)** from US cloud firm **Together AI**.
The data centre will run **10,000 Nvidia B300 chips** — the largest such AI chip deployment in India.
It will be built at L&T's **Vyoma.AI** campus in **Chennai**, through its new AI-infrastructure arm **LTN Compute**.
L&T's stock rose as much as **1.2%** on the news.
It marks L&T's entry into the **'AI factory' business** — building physical infrastructure for AI, not just software.

depth.background: India has spent the past year courting AI data-centre investment — including a separate deal for L&T's Vyoma unit to build a facility in Gujarat's Dholera region. Globally, Big Tech's AI infrastructure commitments are approaching **$1.5 trillion**, and countries are racing to host a share of that build-out, competing on cheap power, land and engineering talent against hubs like the Gulf states and Southeast Asia. Nvidia's B300 chip is its newest AI accelerator, in short supply worldwide as AI labs race to lock in compute capacity.

cards.title: India's Supreme Court accuses its food safety regulator of stalling on sugar-and-salt warning labels to protect industry
cards.what_happened: At a hearing on **August 13, 2026**, the Supreme Court sharply criticized FSSAI for failing to implement front-of-pack warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, saturated fat or sodium, despite a **February 2026** court order giving it four weeks to finalize the framework. The bench asked whether FSSAI's inaction reflected pressure from food manufacturers, after the regulator disclosed that a **March 19, 2026** stakeholder consultation found most industry participants opposed warning labels, preferring a softer, non-alarming information system instead. FSSAI's own draft proposal calls for pictorial labels flagging products exceeding **25 grams of sugar, 10 grams of saturated fat, or 5 grams of salt** per recommended daily limit.
key_points: The Supreme Court asked **FSSAI**, India's food regulator, **'Do you not want people to be healthy?'** over its delay on warning labels.
FSSAI was ordered in **February 2026** to finalize front-of-pack warning labels within four weeks — and still hasn't.
A **March 2026** industry consultation found most food companies **opposed** mandatory warning labels.
The court directly asked whether FSSAI's inaction reflects **pressure from food manufacturers**.
The proposed labels would flag foods exceeding **25g sugar, 10g saturated fat, or 5g salt** per recommended daily limits.

depth.background: India is facing a fast-rising burden of diabetes, obesity and heart disease, and health advocates have pushed for years for mandatory front-of-pack warning labels on packaged food — similar to rules already in force in Chile, Mexico and the UK, which use warning symbols to flag products high in sugar, fat or salt. FSSAI's proposed labels are based on daily limits set out in the **2024 ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians**. The regulator has repeatedly missed its own deadlines to finalize the rule, most recently one the Supreme Court set in February 2026.

cards.title: Maharashtra shuts down 14 Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart outlets over cockroaches, rodents and expired food
cards.what_happened: On August 13, Maharashtra's FDA sent inspection teams to 86 quick-commerce food-storage and delivery outlets across the state, checking temperature control, pest management, staff hygiene records, and whether stock was being rotated and sold before expiry (a practice called FIFO/FEFO). By August 14, the agency had suspended the operating licences of 14 of those outlets — five run by Blinkit, five by Zepto, two by Instamart, and two independent vendors — for serious violations. At a Blinkit-linked facility in Malad West, inspectors found the chiller room running warmer than allowed and no medical exam records for about 40 food handlers. At an Instamart-linked site in Bandra West, they reported heavy rodent droppings, a lizard infestation, and rusted storage racks. A Zepto outlet in Pune's Lohegaon area was found storing food past its declared 'use by' date. A separate Pune facility, Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd, was shut over an active cockroach infestation. Beyond the 14 suspensions, the FDA issued 60 improvement notices to other outlets and ordered one facility to stop operating altogether until it fixes its violations.
key_points: Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration (FDA) inspected **86** quick-commerce food outlets across the state on August 13 and suspended **14** licences the next day.
Of the shut outlets, **5 belonged to Blinkit, 5 to Zepto, and 2 to Instamart**, plus two independent vendors linked to the platforms.
Inspectors found **cockroach and rodent infestations, lizard sightings, and food kept past its 'use-by' date** at several 'dark store' warehouses.
One Blinkit-linked store had **no medical fitness records for roughly 40 food handlers**; a chiller room was running above the required temperature.
The FDA also issued **60 improvement notices** and ordered one facility to fully halt operations pending fixes.

depth.background: Quick-commerce apps like Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart promise grocery and food delivery in **10–20 minutes**, relying on a dense network of small local warehouses called 'dark stores' rather than traditional retail outlets. This rapid-delivery model has grown explosively in Indian cities over the past three years, but food-safety oversight has struggled to keep pace with the sheer number of new micro-warehouses opening. State FDAs, not the national food regulator FSSAI, handle store-level licensing and hygiene inspections. Complaints about hygiene at dark stores have been rising for months, prompting this targeted sweep.

cards.title: India's latest urea import tender comes in 12% cheaper, easing the fertiliser subsidy squeeze
cards.what_happened: RCF, which imports urea on the government's behalf, closed its latest tender for 1 million tonnes of urea on the west coast with offers priced between $393.65 and $435 per tonne — about 12% cheaper than what India paid in its June tender. Suppliers collectively offered around 3.1 million tonnes, more than triple the quantity being purchased, a sign that global producers now have spare capacity to sell. This is a sharp turnaround from April 2026, when tender prices touched $959 a tonne — nearly double pre-conflict levels — as the Strait of Hormuz disruption and tight Russian supply squeezed the market. Prices had already fallen by roughly half between April and June as alternative supply came online, and the latest tender extends that decline further.
key_points: State-run Rashtriya Chemicals & Fertilizers (RCF) received offers of **$393.65 to $435 per tonne** for a 1-million-tonne west-coast urea tender — about **12% below June's** purchase price.
Suppliers offered **roughly 3.1 million tonnes** in total, more than three times the tonnage actually sought, signaling improving global supply.
Urea prices had spiked as high as **$959 a tonne in April 2026** — nearly double pre-conflict levels — after Middle East shipping disruptions hit global supply.
India budgeted **₹1.168 trillion (~$12.75 billion)** for fertiliser subsidies in FY27, including about **₹0.32 trillion** earmarked for imports alone.
The government caps urea's retail price for farmers at under **$70/tonne** and absorbs the difference, so cheaper imports directly ease the subsidy bill.

depth.background: Urea is the most widely used nitrogen fertiliser in Indian farming, and India imports roughly a quarter to a third of what it needs because domestic production can't cover demand. Earlier in 2026, a Middle East conflict disrupted shipping through the **Strait of Hormuz**, a chokepoint that normally carries close to a third of the world's seaborne urea trade, while Russia — another major exporter — also faced supply constraints. That squeeze, combined with a spike in natural gas prices (a key input for making urea), pushed import costs to their highest level since 2022. Because India fixes a low retail price for urea and the government pays producers/importers the rest, any swing in global prices flows straight into the federal budget rather than onto farmers.

cards.title: Supreme Court halts Madras High Court order that had cancelled government jobs for Karur stampede victims' families
cards.what_happened: A Supreme Court bench of Justices **JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran** stayed the Madras High Court's order, temporarily reinstating the compassionate jobs while the case is argued further. The court issued notice to Tamil Nadu's Chief Secretary and other respondents on the state government's petition. During the hearing, the judges pushed back on the basis for challenging the policy, with the bench reportedly asking: **"Who are you to question the policy of the government? Suppose the sole member died in the tragedy, shouldn't the government give some employment to son or daughter?"** The case will now continue in the Supreme Court rather than being settled by the High Court's ruling.
key_points: The Supreme Court **stayed** a Madras High Court ruling that had **quashed government jobs** given to families of Karur stampede victims
The stampede at a **TVK rally in September 2025** killed **41 people**
Tamil Nadu CM **Vijay** had personally handed appointment letters to **31 family members** on **July 10, 2026**
The Madras High Court's Madurai Bench had struck down those appointments on **July 27**
The bench, led by Justices **JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran**, questioned why the state shouldn't be allowed to employ victims' kin

depth.background: In **September 2025**, a stampede broke out at a political rally organised by actor-turned-politician **Vijay's** party, the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, killing **41 people** — one of the deadliest incidents at an Indian political rally in years. Vijay went on to become Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister after his party's strong showing in the 2026 state election. As a gesture to the victims' families, his government offered **compassionate government jobs** to close relatives of those who died, and Vijay personally handed over appointment letters to 31 of them in July. The Madras High Court's Madurai bench then struck down those appointments on July 27, ruling the government orders invalid, which the state government challenged before the Supreme Court.

cards.title: DMK declares it's no longer part of the INDIA bloc, leaving Congress as the alliance's only member in Tamil Nadu
cards.what_happened: Speaking to reporters at Chennai airport on **Friday, August 14**, DMK parliamentary party leader **Kanimozhi** said DMK was **"no longer part of the INDIA bloc"** and that Congress was currently the only party actively in the alliance. She has written to Lok Sabha Speaker **Om Birla** asking for DMK's Parliamentary Party to be **reseated away from Congress**, arguing it's no longer appropriate for them to sit together given the changed political circumstances. Kanimozhi also brushed off criticism for attending Birla's tea meeting in Delhi, noting she was the only INDIA bloc leader present since the rest of the bloc boycotted the event.
key_points: DMK leader **Kanimozhi** said DMK is **"no longer part of the INDIA bloc"** and only Congress remains in it
The split follows DMK's alliance **losing power** in the 2026 Tamil Nadu election, where **Vijay's TVK** emerged as the single largest party with **108 seats**
Congress then **backed TVK** to help form the Tamil Nadu government — the move that broke DMK's trust
Kanimozhi has formally asked the Lok Sabha Speaker to **move DMK's seating** away from Congress in Parliament
Kanimozhi was the **only INDIA bloc leader** who attended Speaker Om Birla's tea meeting, which other opposition parties boycotted

depth.background: The **INDIA bloc** is the opposition alliance formed by Congress, DMK and other regional parties to jointly challenge the ruling coalition at the national level. DMK and Congress had been allies in Tamil Nadu for years. That changed after Tamil Nadu's 2026 state election, when the DMK-led alliance lost its majority and **Vijay's TVK party** became the single largest party with 108 seats. Congress then extended support to help TVK form the state government — a move DMK saw as a direct betrayal by its national ally, since it effectively helped its Tamil Nadu rival take power.

cards.title: India's cancer wards are running short of two essential chemotherapy drugs as costs and price caps collide
cards.what_happened: Oncology centres across India — including **AIIMS Delhi** and the **Tata Memorial Centre** — are facing disrupted treatment schedules because of a shortage of two foundational chemotherapy drugs, **cisplatin and carboplatin**, used to treat lung, head-and-neck, ovarian, cervical, bladder and testicular cancers. Pharmaceutical manufacturers say the shortage stems from a sharp jump in the cost of imported **platinum-based raw materials**, made worse in the past month by **West Asia shipping-route disruptions** tied to the wider regional conflict, while government price caps under the DPCO made producing the drugs commercially unviable at the old ceiling price. In response, the **National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA)** approved a **50% increase** in the ceiling price of both drugs for a six-month window, hoping to make manufacturing profitable again and pull supply back into the market. The shortage is not new — cisplatin and carboplatin shortages were first flagged in India as far back as 2023 — but oncologists say it has become acute again over the last month. Doctors warn that delaying chemotherapy cycles, or substituting less-effective alternative drugs, can measurably worsen outcomes for cancer patients already mid-treatment.
key_points: Two essential chemo drugs, **cisplatin and carboplatin**, are running short at major hospitals including **AIIMS Delhi**.
The NPPA approved a **50% price increase** on both drugs to try to restore manufacturers' incentive to produce them.
Manufacturers blame **rising platinum raw-material costs** and **West Asia shipping disruptions**, on top of old price caps.
The drugs treat **lung, ovarian, cervical, bladder, and head-and-neck cancers** — delays can worsen outcomes.
This is a **recurring problem**: shortages of these same drugs were first flagged in India back in **2023**.

depth.background: Cisplatin and carboplatin are decades-old, inexpensive chemotherapy drugs that remain a first-line treatment for several of the most common cancers — there is no simple substitute that works as well for many patients. India regulates the price of essential medicines through the **Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), 2013**, which caps how much manufacturers can charge; the goal is to keep essential drugs affordable, but when input costs rise faster than the cap allows, manufacturers can lose money on every unit and simply stop making it. That is what oncologists say has been happening with these two drugs since raw platinum costs began climbing, a problem intensified by the broader disruption to Middle East shipping routes this year.

cards.title: India's Parliament passes 11 of 12 bills this Monsoon Session — with almost no debate and zero committee review
cards.what_happened: India's Parliament wrapped its 2026 Monsoon Session having introduced **12 Bills** and passed **11** of them, with only the Indian Statistical Institute Bill still pending. According to PRS Legislative Research, none of the 12 Bills introduced this session were referred to a Standing Committee for detailed scrutiny — a sharp drop from 2025, when five of 13 Bills went through that process. **Nine of the 11 passed Bills went through the Lok Sabha without a single MP other than the minister speaking on them.** The one exception was the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, which absorbed **17 hours 34 minutes** of debate across both Houses — more than the other ten Bills combined got (15 hours 24 minutes). Overall, the Lok Sabha sat for just **19%** of its scheduled functioning hours and the Rajya Sabha for **33%**, as repeated disruptions ate into the session. Two politically sensitive bills — on delimitation and FCRA reform — were shelved or sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee rather than debated on the floor, with attention already shifting to 2027 state elections.
key_points: **11 of 12 Bills** introduced this Monsoon Session were passed — but **none** went to a Standing Committee for scrutiny.
**9 of 11** passed Bills saw **no MP besides the minister speak** on them before passing.
Lok Sabha functioned for just **19%** of its scheduled hours amid repeated disruptions.
One bill — on exam-cheating prevention — absorbed **more debate time than the other ten combined**.
Delimitation and a contentious FCRA bill were **shelved or deferred** as focus shifts to 2027 elections.

depth.background: India's Parliament holds three sessions a year, and the Standing Committee system — where a smaller cross-party group of MPs examines a bill clause-by-clause before it reaches the floor — exists specifically to catch drafting problems and unintended consequences that a rushed floor debate can miss. That system has been used less and less in recent years, and **PRS Legislative Research**, a respected nonpartisan tracker of Parliament's functioning, has flagged this session as a new low: **zero of 12 Bills** referred to committee, versus five of 13 last year. Sessions are frequently disrupted by opposition protests over unrelated political flashpoints, eating into the limited floor time available for actual legislative debate.

cards.title: The rupee edges up as oil prices ease, while RBI proposes tying more loan rates directly to its repo rate
cards.what_happened: On Friday, the rupee held around **₹95.67 to the US dollar**, edging higher as Brent crude fell more than 2% on Thursday to roughly **$86.50 a barrel** — a relief for India's oil-import bill even as the US threatened to maintain an **indefinite naval blockade** of Iranian ports. The rupee has still lost **9.32% of its value over the past 12 months**, though it has recovered about 0.67% over the past month. Traders said persistent dollar demand from importers, plus maturing forward contracts, kept weighing on the currency, while the RBI's **near-daily intervention** helped prevent a sharper fall. Separately, the RBI floated a new draft framework that would require **floating-rate personal and MSME (small business) loans** to be linked to external benchmarks such as its repo rate, a change intended to make rate changes pass through to borrowers faster and more transparently — though it would only take effect from **April 2027** if finalized.
key_points: The **rupee** traded around **₹95.67/$1** on Friday, helped by a pullback in crude oil prices.
**Brent crude** fell over **2%** to around **$86.50 a barrel**, easing import-cost pressure on India.
The **RBI has been intervening near-daily** in currency markets to cushion the rupee's slide.
The rupee is still down **9.3% over the past 12 months**, despite a modest 0.7% bounce this month.
RBI's new draft rule would link **floating-rate personal and MSME loans** directly to its repo rate from **April 2027**.

depth.background: The Indian rupee has weakened steadily over the past year, squeezed by a strong US dollar, persistent demand for dollars from Indian importers, and — this year in particular — elevated global oil prices driven by the **Iran war and Strait of Hormuz crisis** (India imports over 80% of its crude). The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) doesn't let the rupee float completely freely; it periodically sells dollars from its reserves to slow sharp declines, a practice called intervention. Separately, RBI has long pushed lenders to price loans more transparently by linking them to a clear external benchmark (like its own repo rate) instead of banks' own internal, harder-to-track formulas.

cards.title: Reliance and Rolls-Royce join the race to build India's next stealth-fighter engine
cards.what_happened: On Thursday, **Reliance Industries** and **Rolls-Royce** announced their intent to jointly develop, manufacture and deliver a 'sovereign indigenous combat engine' for the AMCA program. As part of the plan, the two companies said they will explore setting up a dedicated **Aerospace Gas Turbine Complex** in India, envisioned as a center of excellence for jet-engine and propulsion technology. The announcement comes a week after India's Ministry of Defence told a Parliamentary committee it is also pursuing a **separate route** — joining France's FCAS sixth-generation fighter program — to plug a shortfall of roughly **13 fighter squadrons** in the Indian Air Force. Together, the moves signal that India is pursuing fighter-engine self-reliance through multiple parallel tracks — one government-to-government (Safran-GTRE), one private-sector (Reliance-Rolls Royce) — rather than betting on a single deal.
key_points: **Reliance Industries** and **Rolls-Royce** announced plans to jointly build a combat jet engine for India's **AMCA** stealth fighter.
The pair may set up a dedicated **Aerospace Gas Turbine Complex** in India as a hub for engine technology.
This is a **separate, private-sector-led effort** from the government's existing Safran-GTRE engine deal for the same jet.
India currently has **no domestic capability** to build a fighter jet engine of this class from scratch.
The Indian Air Force faces a shortfall of about **13 fighter squadrons**, adding urgency to speeding up AMCA.

depth.background: India's **Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA)** is the country's first attempt at a fifth-generation stealth fighter, designed by the state-run Aeronautical Development Agency. The single hardest part of building any fighter jet from scratch is the engine — India has never independently designed and built one powerful enough for a modern combat aircraft, and has always relied on foreign engines (like those on the Tejas and Su-30). The government has been separately negotiating with France's Safran and India's own DRDO lab, GTRE, for one engine-development route; this Reliance-Rolls Royce announcement opens a second, privately-backed track for the same underlying problem.

cards.title: A tunnel collapses at a Himalayan hydropower project in Uttarakhand, killing at least 7 workers
cards.what_happened: On the evening of **August 13**, a landslide is believed to have sent a sudden surge of water and debris into the under-construction tail race tunnel at the Pipalkoti hydroelectric project site in Chamoli district, while workers inside were welding reinforcement bars. Of **28 workers on duty**, **22 were trapped** when the collapse happened. At least **7 workers have been confirmed dead** and around **14 injured**; rescue teams managed to pull a number of survivors out, though a handful of workers remained missing as of the latest reports. Disaster response teams from the NDRF, SDRF, ITBP (Indo-Tibetan Border Police) and fire services have been working through rising water and debris inside the tunnel to reach anyone still trapped.
key_points: At least **7 workers killed** and around **14 injured** after a tunnel collapse in Chamoli district.
**22 of 28 workers** on duty were trapped when water and debris suddenly flooded the tunnel.
A **landslide** is believed to have triggered the inrush while workers were welding reinforcement bars.
**NDRF, ITBP and fire services** are racing to reach a small number of workers still missing.
The tunnel belongs to the **Vishnugad-Pipalkoti Hydroelectric Project** on the Alaknanda river.

depth.background: Uttarakhand's Himalayan valleys are dotted with under-construction hydropower tunnels because the state's steep, fast-flowing rivers are ideal for generating electricity — but the same young, fragile mountains make tunnelling there unusually dangerous. The region has a grim recent history: the 2021 Tapovan disaster and the 2023 Silkyara tunnel collapse (where 41 workers were trapped for 17 days) both happened in comparable hydropower or highway tunnels nearby. This latest collapse struck the **Tail Race Tunnel (TRT)** of the **Vishnugad-Pipalkoti Hydroelectric Project**, run by state-run **THDC (Tehri Hydro Development Corporation) Limited**, with construction handled by Hindustan Construction Company (HCC).

cards.title: Parliament curbs states' power to tax mining companies, in a win for the Centre over resource-rich states
cards.what_happened: The **Lok Sabha** passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 on **August 12**, and the **Rajya Sabha** cleared it the following day, **August 13**. The bill inserts a new **Section 9D**, under which states cannot impose taxes, cess, or other levies on mineral rights or mineral-bearing land based on the quantity or value of the mineral, or the royalty payable, except within conditions the Centre prescribes. The Centre will directly regulate major minerals — coal, limestone, iron ore, copper and manganese among them — while states retain authority over 49 minor minerals. The law also invalidates any state levies from before this amendment that companies haven't yet paid or that states haven't yet recovered, though money already collected will not have to be refunded. The bill becomes law once it receives the President's assent.
key_points: Parliament passed the **Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026**.
It bars states from taxing **mineral rights or mineral-bearing land** except on terms the Centre allows.
The Centre keeps control of major minerals like **coal, iron ore, copper and manganese**; states keep 49 minor minerals.
The law also **wipes out un-recovered past state levies**, though taxes already collected won't be refunded.
Mines Minister **G Kishan Reddy** says the goal is a **uniform mineral tax rate** nationwide, not less state revenue.

depth.background: This fight goes back to a landmark 2024 Supreme Court ruling that affirmed states' constitutional power to levy their own taxes on mineral rights and mineral-bearing land — on top of the royalty they already collect — and even allowed them to claim it retrospectively. Mineral-rich states like Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal moved to send large back-dated tax demands to mining companies, including state-run giants like Coal India, following that ruling. The Centre has now used ordinary legislation to substantially narrow what that Supreme Court ruling opened up.

cards.title: India brings back a fugitive drug kingpin from the UAE, in one of the NCB's biggest extraditions this year
cards.what_happened: The NCB confirmed it has secured the extradition of **Virender Singh Basoya**, a fugitive accused of masterminding a multi-crore cocaine trafficking syndicate, bringing him back to India from the **UAE**. A Delhi court had issued a non-bailable warrant against him, which Indian agencies used to pursue red notices and extradition proceedings through diplomatic channels. **Home Minister Amit Shah** publicly confirmed the extradition. Basoya is described as a close associate of Sandeep Dhunia, the main accused in a separate case where **Delhi Police seized over 500 kg of cocaine** in 2024 and arrested five people, including Basoya's associates Jitendra Pal Singh and Tushar Goyal. Investigators allege Basoya ran the network with help from India-based Tushar Goyal and UK-based associates Jitender Gill and Savinder Singh.
key_points: The **Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB)** secured the extradition of **Virender Singh Basoya** from the **UAE**.
Basoya is accused of running a **multi-crore international cocaine syndicate**.
He's linked to a **2024 Delhi seizure of over 500 kg of cocaine**, one of India's biggest drug busts.
**Home Minister Amit Shah** confirmed the extradition publicly.
A **Delhi court's non-bailable warrant** against Basoya enabled the extradition through diplomatic channels.

depth.background: The NCB is India's federal agency for fighting drug trafficking, similar in role to the US DEA. Basoya had already been arrested once in an earlier case but was released on bail, after which he fled the country and continued to allegedly run his network from abroad — a pattern that's common with well-funded traffickers who use international travel and offshore bases to stay ahead of Indian law enforcement. His name surfaced again in 2024, when Delhi Police seized more than **500 kilograms of cocaine** and arrested several of his associates, uncovering what investigators describe as a large, India-linked international syndicate reaching into the UK. Extraditing a fugitive from the UAE typically requires close coordination between Indian agencies, Interpol, and UAE authorities — a process that can take years.

cards.title: Delhi goes on high alert after an email threat invoking Khalistan targets the High Court, Metro and rail lines
cards.what_happened: An email threat received today made explicit references to **Khalistan** and the **1984 anti-Sikh riots**, naming Delhi's High Court, Metro network and train lines as targets, according to Business Today. The threat triggered immediate sweeps of high-priority locations across the capital as security agencies moved to rule out any credible device or attack. It lands the day before Prime Minister Narendra Modi is due to address the nation from the Red Fort for the **80th Independence Day**, an event already under maximum security with roughly **20,000 personnel deployed** around the venue. Separately, India's Intelligence Bureau has issued fresh warnings that Pakistan's ISI may attempt attacks timed to the holiday, with intelligence pointing to attempted infiltration into Jammu & Kashmir as the top concern, alongside heightened vigilance on the Bangladesh border.
key_points: An **email threat** sent today referenced **Khalistan and the 1984 anti-Sikh riots**, naming Delhi's High Court, Metro and train lines.
Security agencies launched **sweeps of high-priority locations** across the capital in response.
It comes as Delhi finalizes **maximum security** for tomorrow's **80th Independence Day** address at the Red Fort.
Separately, India's **Intelligence Bureau** has flagged a broader **ISI-linked terror threat** targeting the holiday.
Agencies say the first priority is stopping infiltration into **Jammu & Kashmir** ahead of August 15.

thread.previously: Yesterday, Delhi authorities locked down central roads and deployed facial-recognition CCTV with a drone ban for the Independence Day full-dress rehearsal, as part of routine annual security preparations.
thread.changed: Today a specific email threat referencing Khalistan and the 1984 riots named the High Court, Metro and train lines as targets, escalating the general rehearsal-stage lockdown into an active, targeted security sweep just before tomorrow's Red Fort address.

depth.background: Every year, Indian security agencies go on high alert around **Independence Day (August 15)**, especially in Delhi, where the Prime Minister addresses the nation from the Red Fort — a symbolically important and historically targeted site. **Khalistan** refers to a decades-old separatist movement seeking an independent Sikh state carved out of Punjab; it has occasionally resurfaced through threats and diaspora activism, especially around anniversaries tied to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, when thousands of Sikhs were killed following Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's assassination. Yesterday, Delhi authorities had already locked down central roads and deployed facial-recognition CCTV and a drone ban for the Independence Day full-dress rehearsal; today's threat adds a concrete, if unverified, target list to those general precautions.
