cards.title: Red Bull tables a five-year, ~$80 million-a-season contract to keep Max Verstappen — and scrap his exit clause
cards.what_happened: Red Bull has tabled a revised **five-year contract offer** to Verstappen worth an estimated **$80 million per season** — a significant raise from his current roughly €65 million annual pay — but with the key condition that his **performance-based exit clause be scrapped entirely**. Verstappen, according to reports, is reluctant to give up that clause and would instead prefer to sign a shorter **one-year contract** that keeps his options open, meaning he would likely stay at Red Bull through 2027 regardless while the team tries to build him a more competitive car. His current exit clause remains **active until October**, adding a real deadline to the negotiations. The story breaks as F1 returns from its summer break with the **Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort** — Verstappen's home race, and reportedly the event's last edition, since it's dropping off the 2027 calendar.
key_points: Red Bull has reportedly offered Verstappen a revised **five-year deal worth roughly $80 million a season**, well above his current ~€65 million.
The offer's key condition: Verstappen must **give up the performance-based exit clause** in his current contract.
Verstappen reportedly **doesn't want to give up that clause**, and prefers a shorter, **one-year deal** instead.
His existing exit clause is **active until October**, adding real time pressure to the decision.
The saga plays out with F1 returning this weekend to Zandvoort — **Verstappen's home race**, and reportedly his last as the event isn't on the 2027 calendar.

thread.previously: We reported Verstappen's exit clause was active and drawing warnings about complications with a potential McLaren move given its engine situation.
thread.changed: Red Bull has now made a concrete counter-offer — a five-year, ~$80M/season deal in exchange for scrapping the clause — while Verstappen reportedly leans toward a shorter one-year deal instead.

depth.background: Verstappen has a performance-linked **exit clause** in his current Red Bull contract, reportedly letting him leave if the team underperforms — relevant because Red Bull has struggled to fight for wins consistently in 2026 while McLaren and Mercedes have looked stronger. That clause has fueled months of speculation linking Verstappen to rival teams. Red Bull, unwilling to lose a four-time world champion, has been trying to lock him down with a new long-term contract — but the terms of any deal, and whether the exit clause survives it, have become the central tension.

cards.title: Honda's long-awaited upgraded engine hits its performance target ahead of Aston Martin's Zandvoort debut
cards.what_happened: Honda's chief engineer, **Shintaro Orihara**, confirmed the manufacturer has met its **internal performance target** for the upgraded RA626H power unit ahead of its debut at the Dutch Grand Prix. The changes include a **revised pre-chamber** (to speed up combustion), a **reshaped combustion chamber and piston**, and **lubrication changes** aimed at reducing mechanical friction — all routes to extracting more usable power. The unit already ran on-track for the first time during an Aston Martin **filming day at the Hungaroring**, gathering data ahead of its planned race debut. Honda flagged one complication: Zandvoort's **Sprint race format** gives teams only a single free practice session, making it harder to properly evaluate a new engine spec under real conditions before it's raced.
key_points: Honda says its new-spec **RA626H power unit** has hit its **internal performance target** ahead of the Dutch GP.
The upgrade modifies the **pre-chamber, combustion chamber and piston shape** to burn fuel more efficiently, plus lubrication tweaks to cut friction losses.
It already ran on track during an Aston Martin **filming day in Hungary** before its planned **race debut at Zandvoort**.
Honda admits this weekend's **Sprint format**, which gives only one practice session, makes properly evaluating the new engine **harder**.
The upgrade is meant to build on Aston Martin's **aerodynamic gains** from its AMR26 car this year.

depth.background: In Formula 1, the engine ('power unit') and the aerodynamic package are separate battles — a team can have a great chassis but still lose lap time if its engine partner falls behind. Honda supplies **Aston Martin's** power units, and after a mixed start to the 2026 rules era, the manufacturer has been working toward a significant mid-season upgrade. Aston Martin, meanwhile, has reportedly made real strides on the **aerodynamic side** of its car (the AMR26), meaning a stronger engine could unlock gains the chassis is already capable of. Zandvoort's Dutch Grand Prix (August 21-23) marks the engine's intended competitive debut.

cards.title: Racing Bulls tells its two title-hopeful rookies they can race flat-out — with one rule: don't touch
cards.what_happened: Team principal Alan Permane confirmed that Racing Bulls will **not impose team orders** to protect one driver over the other, even though Lawson and Lindblad are directly competing with each other for results, for a place ahead of Tsolov in the pecking order, and ultimately for a possible Red Bull promotion. The only boundary Permane set is that the two must **not make contact** with each other while racing. Permane said the team expects to arrive at this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort '**even stronger**' than before the summer break.
key_points: Racing Bulls boss **Alan Permane** set just one rule for teammates **Liam Lawson** and **Arvid Lindblad**: don't touch each other.
The team is chasing its **best-ever Constructors' Championship finish** and won't order either driver to back off.
Both drivers are also racing for a possible future **Red Bull seat**, adding personal stakes to every on-track battle.
F2 champion **Nikola Tsolov** is a further threat to both drivers' longer-term F1 futures.
Permane says the team expects to come back **'even stronger' at Zandvoort** this weekend.

depth.background: Racing Bulls is Red Bull's sister/junior team, and this season it is fighting for its **best-ever finish** in the Constructors' Championship — the team title based on combined points from both drivers. Teammates **Liam Lawson** and 18-year-old rookie **Arvid Lindblad** are not just racing for the team; they are also both competing for the same prize of a future promotion to the senior **Red Bull** team if a seat opens up, with rising Formula 2 champion **Nikola Tsolov** also in the wings as a longer-term threat to both their prospects.

cards.title: Mercedes says grid penalties for title leader Antonelli and George Russell are now 'almost inevitable'
cards.what_happened: Mercedes has acknowledged that both Antonelli and Russell will almost certainly need grid penalties in the second half of the 2026 season because reliability failures in the first half burned through their allotted engine components faster than planned. Antonelli is already on his **fourth set** of power-unit components and Russell his **third**, meaning any further replacement triggers a penalty. Rather than debate whether to take the hit, the team is strategizing about **which race weekend** minimizes the damage — Mercedes team principal **Toto Wolff** has floated the **Italian Grand Prix at Monza** as a candidate, reasoning that even a back-of-grid start there is more recoverable than at a track like Zandvoort, Antonelli's title rival's home race. Mercedes has stated it will **not prioritize Antonelli's title campaign** over Russell when deciding the order.
key_points: Mercedes admits both **Kimi Antonelli** and **George Russell** will need grid penalties before the season ends.
Antonelli, the **championship leader with 219 points**, is already on his **fourth set** of engine components.
A grid penalty usually means starting **around 10 places back** — costly in a tight title fight.
Mercedes is choosing **when**, not if, to take the hit, with **Monza** floated as one option.
The team says it **won't favor Antonelli's title bid** over Russell when deciding whose penalty comes first.

depth.background: In Formula 1, each driver is allotted a limited number of engine parts (the 'power unit') for the entire season under FIA rules. Teams try to make each part last as long as possible, because fitting an extra one beyond the allowance triggers an automatic grid penalty at the next race — typically dropping a driver back around 10 places on the starting grid. **Kimi Antonelli**, a rookie in his first full title-contending season, currently leads the drivers' championship with **219 points**, a **50-point lead** over Lewis Hamilton.

cards.title: Alex Albon extends his Williams contract through 2027, betting on the team despite its 2026 slump
cards.what_happened: Williams announced on **Tuesday, August 18** that Alex Albon has signed a **one-year contract extension**, formally committing him to the team through the end of the **2027 F1 season**. The move removes ambiguity created by exit clauses in his prior deal, which some in the paddock had read as leaving his future open given Williams' poor 2026 form. Team principal **James Vowles** said he was 'delighted' that Albon has 'continued to put his faith in Williams' despite this year's struggles. The announcement lands during F1's summer break, just before the sport resumes at the Dutch Grand Prix, and as Albon's current teammate Carlos Sainz's own contract situation for 2027 remains unresolved, with reports of him weighing a fresh Williams offer against other options including Aston Martin interest for Sergio Perez's old seat.
key_points: Williams confirmed **Alex Albon** signed a **one-year extension** keeping him at the team through the **2027 season**.
It comes as Williams has **slumped to 9th** in the constructors' standings, down from 5th in 2025.
Team principal **James Vowles** said he was 'delighted' Albon kept his faith in the team through the 'blip.'
The move resolves exit-clause uncertainty that had put Albon's own future in doubt.
It narrows the 2027 driver market just as teammate **Carlos Sainz's** own seat talks remain unresolved.

depth.background: **Alex Albon**, a British-born Thai driver, has been Williams' talisman during its multi-year rebuild since returning to F1 with the team in 2022, helping guide it back up the grid. Williams surged to **5th in the constructors' championship in 2025** but has slumped badly in 2026 with its FW48 car, dropping to 9th — a stumble team boss James Vowles has called a 'blip.' Albon's prior contract already carried language covering 2027, but built-in **exit clauses** left real uncertainty about whether he would stay.

cards.title: Cadillac names Marcin Budkowski team principal, hours after abruptly sacking founding boss Graeme Lowdon
cards.what_happened: Cadillac confirmed that **Marcin Budkowski** — a veteran F1 figure who has held senior roles at the FIA, Ferrari, McLaren and Renault/Alpine — will become the team's new principal, arriving just hours after the team abruptly sacked founding boss **Graeme Lowdon**. CEO Dan Towriss told reporters the decision to remove Lowdon was **his alone**, contradicting the team's public statement describing it as a mutual, planned transition. According to multiple outlets, Lowdon himself was informed of his removal only hours before Cadillac made the change public. The timing is notable: it lands during F1's summer break, halfway through Cadillac's debut season, in which the team remains the only one on the 2026 grid yet to score a championship point.
key_points: Cadillac appointed **Marcin Budkowski**, a veteran of the FIA, Ferrari, McLaren and Renault/Alpine, as its new team principal
The move comes **hours after** the team abruptly sacked founding boss **Graeme Lowdon**

depth.background: **Audi** entered Formula 1 as a full manufacturer team in 2026, taking over what was previously the Sauber operation, and has been building its own engine and car programme from the ground up — a project where experienced technical feedback matters as much as outright pace. **Nico Hulkenberg** is one of the grid's most experienced drivers, valued for his ability to help develop a car through technical feedback during exactly this kind of early-stage manufacturer buildup.

cards.title: Ollie Bearman turns down an Aston Martin approach, commits to staying in the Ferrari driver programme through 2028
cards.what_happened: According to reporting from F1 journalist Marc Limacher, **Bearman turned down a significant offer from Aston Martin** and instead chose to extend his commitment to the **Ferrari Driver Academy through 2028**, continuing to race for Haas in 2027. Bearman confirmed his stance directly, saying: **'I'm very much committed to what Ferrari have offered me, and they have supported me since the very beginning, since I joined F3, and I'm only sitting here thanks to them.'** The decision takes one of the market's most sought-after young drivers off the table for rival teams.
key_points: **Ollie Bearman** has rejected a offer from Aston Martin, choosing to extend his **Ferrari Driver Academy** deal through 2028.
He will continue racing for **Haas** in 2027 under the extended arrangement.
Bearman said he remains **'very much committed'** to Ferrari, crediting them for his rise since his F3 days.
The decision removes Bearman as an option in F1's crowded 2027 **'silly season'** driver market.
It comes as fellow young driver moves — Sainz to Williams, Verstappen's Red Bull future — keep the market unsettled.

depth.background: **Ollie Bearman** is a young British driver who rose through Ferrari's junior driver programme and made his F1 debut as a late substitute in 2024 before securing a full-time seat with **Haas**, a team that effectively runs as a Ferrari customer outfit with Ferrari engines and close technical ties. With **eight of F1's 22 seats still unfilled for 2027**, teams up and down the grid — including Aston Martin — have been chasing rising young talent, making this year's driver market unusually fluid.

cards.title: F1 returns from its summer break at Zandvoort for what may be the last Dutch Grand Prix — and a shot at history for Verstappen
cards.what_happened: Formula 1 resumes racing this weekend (**August 21-23**) at Zandvoort after nearly a month off for the summer break, and reports indicate this will be the **final Dutch Grand Prix** on the calendar for the foreseeable future, as the event hasn't been renewed beyond 2026. For Verstappen, who has won at his home track three times since it returned, this is a farewell weekend with real stakes: a fourth win would let him **match Jim Clark's record** of home-race wins and would also be his **first win of the entire 2026 season**, after a year in which title leader Antonelli has built a 50-point championship lead over Lewis Hamilton. Verstappen has already unveiled a special helmet design for the occasion, and Red Bull drivers will wear special race suits. It's a **sprint-format weekend**, and weather forecasts suggest a real possibility of F1's first properly wet race since the 2026 generation of cars was introduced.
key_points: The Dutch Grand Prix **will not be renewed** on the F1 calendar after this year, making this the event's likely farewell.
Home hero **Max Verstappen** has won at Zandvoort three times and has a shot at a 4th win to match **Jim Clark's record**.
It would also be Verstappen's **first win of the 2026 season** if it happens.
It's a **sprint weekend**: a single practice session Friday, then sprint qualifying, sprint race and full qualifying on Saturday.
Forecasts suggest a real chance of F1's **first genuinely wet race** since the 2026 cars were introduced.

depth.background: The **Dutch Grand Prix** returned to F1's calendar in 2021 after a 35-year absence, driven largely by Verstappen's rise and the huge 'Orange Army' of Dutch fans who fill Zandvoort's dunes every year. F1 rotates and refreshes its calendar regularly to fit in new markets (like recent additions in the Middle East and Americas), which sometimes means older European races lose their slot even when they're popular with fans. Verstappen has dominated at his home track since the race's return, but has struggled for outright wins in the **2026 season** under new technical regulations, while Mercedes' **Kimi Antonelli** has built a big championship lead.

cards.title: Carlos Sainz nears a new Williams deal for 2027, effectively shutting Sergio Perez out of the seat
cards.what_happened: According to Spanish outlet **Marca** and multiple F1 outlets, Sainz and his management have used the summer break to focus exclusively on a **new one-year Williams contract** for 2027, after weighing other options and speaking extensively with team principal **James Vowles**. Williams reportedly wants the deal locked in before this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix and is prepared to increase Sainz's pay beyond his current **€13 million** salary to secure him. Sainz's side is also said to be pushing for an **exit clause** in the contract — a mechanism that would let him leave early if a better seat opens up, mirroring the clause that just triggered Max Verstappen's own Red Bull exit drama. With Sainz set to stay, **Sergio Perez's** management-led talks with Williams — explored as a contingency — now look set to go nowhere, even as Cadillac insists publicly that Perez isn't going anywhere.
key_points: Sainz is reportedly in the **final stages** of a new one-year contract with Williams for 2027.
Williams is said to be willing to raise his wage **above his current €13 million** to lock him in.
Sainz's camp reportedly wants an **exit clause**, similar to the one that triggered Max Verstappen's own market shake-up this year.
A deal is expected to be **announced before the Dutch Grand Prix** this weekend at Zandvoort.
Sergio Perez's management had opened **talks with Williams as a backup**, but that door is now closing.

depth.background: F1's driver market ('silly season') runs on a strict calendar most fans never see: contracts for the following year are usually settled by **late summer**, well before the season that they cover even starts, because teams need certainty to plan around sponsors, junior drivers and seat swaps. Carlos Sainz joined **Williams in 2025** after losing his Ferrari seat to Lewis Hamilton, and has spent the year weighing whether to stay or chase a return to a front-running team. Sergio 'Checo' Perez, meanwhile, moved to the new **Cadillac** team but has faced persistent rumors linking him elsewhere, including to Williams if Sainz departed.

cards.title: Toto Wolff backs F1's V8 return as a 'purist' — but says the FIA's timeline is unrealistic
cards.what_happened: In an interview, Mercedes team principal **Toto Wolff** said he supports the idea of F1 returning to **V8 engines** in a future rules cycle, calling it 'the best consensus' and adding 'as a purist, I like it.' He said his preferred version would be a naturally aspirated V8 paired with some form of **energy-recovery system** — a lighter version of the hybrid technology used today — and built to run on **sustainable fuel**, rather than a straightforward throwback engine. However, Wolff pushed back on FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem's push for a **2029** introduction, calling that timeline unrealistic: 'Most manufacturers don't want to pay for a double program. A new engine in two years would cause costs to explode,' since teams would effectively have to develop two engines — today's and the new one — simultaneously.
key_points: Mercedes boss **Toto Wolff** says he supports F1 bringing back **naturally aspirated V8 engines**
FIA president **Mohammed Ben Sulayem** wants the switch as early as **2029**, ending the turbo-hybrid era that began in **2014**
Wolff calls that timeline **unrealistic**, warning a new engine in two years would make costs 'explode'
He wants the V8 paired with an **energy-recovery system** and **sustainable fuel**, not a pure retro engine
Most manufacturers reportedly don't want to fund **two engine programmes at once**

depth.background: Formula 1 has used complex, expensive **turbo-hybrid V6 engines** since 2014 — powerful and efficient, but criticised by some fans and insiders for sounding quieter and being harder (and pricier) to build than the raw V8s and V10s of earlier eras. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has been pushing to bring back a simpler, louder V8 for F1's next big engine cycle, aiming for as soon as **2029 or 2030/31**. Manufacturers like Mercedes, Ferrari, Honda and Audi have poured billions into today's hybrid engines and would need to plan and fund whatever comes next years in advance.

cards.title: Fernando Alonso says his Aston Martin future comes down to the 2027 rules, not this year's car
cards.what_happened: Fernando Alonso confirmed he will decide on his Formula 1 future — whether to continue with Aston Martin, or retire — sometime between the **Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort (August 21-23)** and the **Italian Grand Prix at Monza** the following week. Alonso has stressed that any upgrades or performance improvements to Aston Martin's current car will **not** be what determines his decision; instead, he says it hinges on F1's incoming **2027 technical regulations** and whether he believes the team can be competitive under them. He is in the final year of his current Aston Martin deal. Team principal Adrian Newey has publicly said he remains confident Alonso will stay, describing their working relationship as strong. Alonso has separately shut down rumours linking him to other teams throughout the year.
key_points: **Alonso**, in the final year of his Aston Martin contract, will decide his future between **Zandvoort and Monza**
He says the call is about F1's **new 2027 regulations**, not how competitive Aston Martin's current car is
Aston Martin boss **Adrian Newey** says he's confident of keeping the two-time world champion
Alonso has repeatedly ruled out speculation linking him to rival teams
He still wants to win a **third world title** — this one with Aston Martin

depth.background: **Fernando Alonso**, a two-time world champion now in his 40s, joined Aston Martin in 2023 partly on the promise that the team — bankrolled by billionaire owner Lawrence Stroll and headed technically by star designer **Adrian Newey** — would become a genuine title contender under F1's next big rules reset in **2027**. Aston Martin has struggled to match that ambition on-track through 2026, fueling periodic rumours linking Alonso elsewhere, all of which he has denied. F1's driver market always heats up around the summer break, when contracts for the following year are typically finalised.

cards.title: Ferrari rushes an all-new chassis to Zandvoort as Hamilton's late title bid heats up
cards.what_happened: Ferrari confirmed it will introduce an all-new chassis for Hamilton at the **Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort (August 21-23)**, marking F1's return from its summer break. The new part is a direct evolution of the floor platform Ferrari debuted at the Barcelona race in June, fast-tracked after the team reviewed performance data from the Silverstone weekend. Engineers say the specific goal is to generate **more downforce** from the car's underbody, which should translate into extra cornering grip. The team is holding back its next **power-unit upgrade** — allowed under the FIA's ADUO engine-development rules — for Ferrari's home race at **Monza** (the Italian Grand Prix) rather than debuting it at Zandvoort. Hamilton currently trails Antonelli by **50 points** in the standings as the title fight resumes.
key_points: Ferrari brings an **'all-new chassis'** for Hamilton at the Dutch GP
It's an evolution of the floor first introduced at **Barcelona in June**
Goal: squeeze more **downforce** from the car's body and floor
Hamilton trails championship leader Antonelli by **50 points**
Ferrari saves its next **power-unit upgrade** for Monza, not Zandvoort

depth.background: **Ferrari** enters the second half of the 2026 season chasing Mercedes' **Kimi Antonelli**, an 19-year-old Italian who leads the drivers' championship, and rival **Lewis Hamilton**'s own teammate Charles Leclerc, currently fourth in the standings. Hamilton, in his second season at Ferrari after leaving Mercedes, won at the **Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix** in June, his first victory in red, reviving his title hopes. F1 teams are allowed to keep developing their cars through the season, and floor/chassis upgrades are one of the biggest ways to find extra grip and speed without a full redesign.

cards.title: Ex-F1 steward Johnny Herbert reveals 'Death to Herbert' abuse from Verstappen fans over Hamilton-bias claims
cards.what_happened: In new comments published on **August 16, 2026**, Herbert revealed that the single worst abuse he has ever received on social media came from Verstappen's fanbase, who accused him of favouring Lewis Hamilton whenever he criticised the Red Bull driver on air. He said some messages went as far as reading '**Death to Herbert**,' which he described as the low point of the online reaction. Herbert pointed to his role in the 2024 Mexican Grand Prix penalty decision as the moment the hostility intensified, noting the awkwardness of simultaneously working as a steward handing out penalties and as a pundit publicly discussing them. He pushed back directly on the bias accusation in the interview, standing by his commentary as independent analysis rather than favouritism.
key_points: Herbert says the **worst online abuse** he's received came from Verstappen fans
Messages included death threats reading '**Death to Herbert**'
Fans accuse him of being **biased toward Lewis Hamilton**
Backlash traces to a **20-second penalty** he gave Verstappen at the 2024 Mexican GP
Herbert was axed as an **FIA steward** in Jan 2025 over media conflicts, not this row

depth.background: **Johnny Herbert** is a former F1 driver who went on to become a TV pundit and, until January 2025, an **FIA steward** — one of the officials who rule on driving penalties during race weekends. Late in 2024, Herbert was part of the stewards' panel that handed Red Bull's **Max Verstappen** a 20-second penalty for an aggressive move on McLaren's Lando Norris at the Mexican Grand Prix, a decision Verstappen and his father publicly criticised. Herbert was later removed as a steward — officially because the FIA judged his paid media punditry, including work tied to a betting company, incompatible with the steward role. He has continued as a prominent F1 broadcaster and commentator since.

prev_ref.title: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now active — and McLaren is reportedly circling

cards.title: Verstappen reportedly rejects Red Bull's 5-year offer, wants a 1-year 'prove it' deal instead
cards.what_happened: According to reports, Red Bull has put a **five-year contract offer** on the table for Verstappen, running through 2033. Verstappen, however, is said to want something shorter: a **one-year deal** that would let him evaluate whether Red Bull can actually deliver a competitive car under the new 2027 regulations before committing to anything longer-term — effectively a 'prove it' clause rather than a long-term commitment. Separately, Christian Horner's own bid to return to F1, reportedly with Alpine, is approaching a key veto deadline in September, adding pressure to an already chaotic Red Bull storyline. The team has struggled in 2026 following the departures of Horner and several other senior figures.
key_points: Red Bull has offered Verstappen a **five-year contract** through 2033, according to reports.
Verstappen instead reportedly wants a **one-year deal** to test whether Red Bull can build him a **competitive 2027 car** before committing longer.
His performance-based **exit clause is active** from August to October, after he fell outside the top two in the standings at the summer break.
**Christian Horner's** own hoped-for F1 return is approaching a **September veto deadline** at Alpine — adding another layer to Red Bull's turbulent year.
Red Bull has lost a string of senior figures in 2026, including **Horner, Adrian Newey, Helmut Marko, Rob Marshall and Jonathan Wheatley**.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported that Verstappen's Red Bull contract has a performance clause letting him explore other teams since he was 6th in the standings — about 110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli — at the summer break, that the clause runs August to October, that he hadn't announced any decision to leave, and that only 8 of 2027's grid seats were fully confirmed.
thread.changed: New reporting now details the actual negotiation: Red Bull has offered a 5-year deal through 2033, but Verstappen reportedly wants just a 1-year contract to test the team's competitiveness first — while Christian Horner's own return to F1 is separately approaching a September deadline.

depth.background: Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract contains a performance clause that lets him explore other teams if he's outside the top two in the drivers' championship at the summer break — a threshold he crossed after sitting 6th, well off the pace, making him effectively a free agent for a window running from August to October. He hasn't announced any decision to leave or retire, but he's now widely seen as **F1's biggest 2027 storyline**, with McLaren repeatedly linked as a possible destination. The backdrop is a Red Bull team in upheaval: former team boss Christian Horner and several other senior figures — technical guru Adrian Newey, advisor Helmut Marko, and engineers Rob Marshall and Jonathan Wheatley — have all left the team during 2026.

cards.title: Mercedes says grid penalties are now 'almost inevitable' for both Antonelli and Russell — and Monza looks like the place to take the hit
cards.what_happened: Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord told media it is **'almost inevitable'** that both Kimi Antonelli, who leads the drivers' championship, and George Russell, currently P3, will take grid penalties before the season ends. His exact words: 'Looking at how many components we've used in the first half of the season, it's almost inevitable that at some point there will be penalties to take... it's realistically going to be hard to get to the end of the season on the existing hardware.' Team principal Toto Wolff has gone further, openly discussing where — not if — Mercedes takes the hit: 'Monza can be very special for Kimi, but on paper it looks like it's a good place to take an engine penalty, so I need to speak to Marco [Antonelli's father] on whether we want to take it there,' he said, half-joking that 'we'll take the pressure off in Monza by starting him from the back!' Monza's long straights make overtaking easier than at tracks like Zandvoort or Baku, making it the team's preferred venue to absorb a penalty.
key_points: Mercedes deputy team boss Bradley Lord says penalties for **both title contenders** are **'almost inevitable'** before season's end.
Kimi Antonelli is already on his **4th engine and exhaust**; George Russell on his **3rd set** — one more change triggers an automatic grid drop.
Team boss Toto Wolff is weighing taking the hit at **Monza** (Sept 4-6), where long straights make overtaking easiest.
Mercedes leads the **constructors' championship by 72 points**; Antonelli leads the drivers' standings by **50 points**.
The timing decision could hand track position — and a title-fight opening — to **Ferrari's Hamilton** or Red Bull's Verstappen.

depth.background: Formula 1's power-unit rules cap how many engine components (the ICE, exhaust, energy store, control electronics, among others) each driver can use per season — typically four — before further changes trigger an automatic grid-position penalty. Antonelli has already needed a 4th ICE and exhaust after reliability failures this year (a battery issue in Spain, an engine swap at Belgium), and Russell is on his 3rd set after a water leak forced an engine change in Hungary qualifying and a battery failure in Canada earlier in the season.

cards.title: Honda says its upgraded Aston Martin engine has hit its targets, arriving at Zandvoort as the second half of the team's revival plan
cards.what_happened: Honda has detailed the technical content of a new-specification engine for Aston Martin — sometimes called 'spec-2' — confirming it will debut at the **Dutch Grand Prix, August 21-23**, the first race back from F1's summer break. Honda's GM of Trackside Engineering, Shintaro Orihara, confirmed the engine has hit Honda's internal performance targets but declined to confirm exact horsepower figures, which media estimates put anywhere from **30 to 50 additional horsepower**. The changes include a redesigned combustion pre-chamber for a faster burn, a reshaped piston head for better combustion, and revised internal lubrication to reduce parasitic friction losses. This lands as the second half of a planned Aston Martin revival: the team already introduced a major aerodynamic 'B-spec' chassis at the Hungarian Grand Prix before the break, which immediately helped Alonso and Stroll compete in the midfield instead of running at the back.
key_points: Honda confirms a new-spec engine for Aston Martin has hit its **internal performance targets**, debuting at the **Dutch GP (Aug 21-23)**.
The upgrade redesigns the **combustion pre-chamber, piston shape, and internal lubrication** to cut friction and burn fuel faster.
Estimates of the power gain range from **30 to 50 horsepower**, though Honda won't confirm the exact figure.
Aston Martin's power unit has reportedly been down **over 100bhp** on rivals at points this season.
It follows a chassis 'B-spec' introduced at the **Hungarian GP** that already helped Alonso and Stroll fight in the midfield.

depth.background: Honda's 2026 return to F1 as Aston Martin's works engine partner has been rocky — the power unit has struggled with both performance and reliability, traced partly to Honda reassigning many of its F1 specialists to other projects ahead of the 2026 rules reset. Aston Martin, with an Adrian Newey-designed car and one of the grid's biggest budgets, has been arguably the season's most disappointing team relative to its ambitions, though a new aerodynamic package introduced at the Hungarian GP before the summer break already helped Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll compete with Williams and Haas rather than running last.

prev_ref.title: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now active — and McLaren is reportedly circling

cards.title: Verstappen turned down an €8 million Red Bull buyout of his exit clause, deepening the McLaren speculation
cards.what_happened: Red Bull's leadership formally proposed **buying out Verstappen's exit clause for €8 million**, an offer that would have locked him into the team through **2028** and shut down the growing speculation about a move. Verstappen's management **declined the offer**. He currently sits **sixth in the championship, roughly 110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli**, a gap that has fueled talk he's ready to leave a team he no longer sees as capable of winning. Multiple reports say **McLaren and Verstappen's camp are in advanced, closing-stage negotiations** for a switch, even though McLaren CEO Zak Brown has publicly waved off the rumors. Verstappen has until **October** to formally tell Red Bull whether he's activating the clause and leaving after this season; his manager has separately said Max would like to fulfill his existing contract through 2028 if things improve.
key_points: Red Bull's leadership offered Max **Verstappen €8 million** to buy out the exit clause in his contract — he **declined**.
The offer would have tied Verstappen to Red Bull through **2028**, removing his ability to leave at the end of this season.
His **exit clause activated** after he went into the summer break outside the championship's top two.
Verstappen must formally notify Red Bull by **October** if he intends to leave at season's end.
**McLaren** is reported by multiple paddock sources to be in the closing stages of talks to sign him, despite team boss Zak Brown publicly downplaying it.

thread.previously: Verstappen's performance-linked exit clause became active after he fell outside the championship's top two at the summer break, and McLaren was reported to be circling for a possible signing.
thread.changed: Red Bull has now made a concrete move to keep him — offering €8 million to buy out the clause and tie him to the team through 2028 — and Verstappen's camp has turned it down.

depth.background: F1 driver contracts increasingly include **performance-linked exit clauses** — provisions that let a driver leave early if the team underperforms, protecting top talent from being stuck in an uncompetitive car. Verstappen, a multiple world champion, has driven for Red Bull his entire top-flight career, but the team has struggled with **car development and consistency this season**, and his clause was written to trigger if he fell outside the championship's top two positions by the summer break. That threshold was crossed, activating his right to explore an exit.

prev_ref.title: Christian Horner's best shot at an F1 return hinges on a September veto deadline at Alpine

cards.title: Renault's CEO shuts down talk of Christian Horner joining an Alpine takeover bid
cards.what_happened: Renault Group CEO **François Provost** directly rebutted the Horner-Alpine connection, telling reporters **'there is no discussion today with Christian. We are assessing the options. I want the Renault Group to retain control of our team, regardless of who succeeds Otro.'** This followed earlier reports that Mercedes, another prospective buyer of the Otro stake, had **pulled out of talks** over valuation concerns, which had removed one obstacle some saw as standing between Horner and a deal. Despite Provost's public denial, other reports say Renault is prepared to **formally exercise its veto** specifically to block any Horner-linked consortium from acquiring the stake before September, when that veto power lapses.
key_points: Renault CEO **François Provost** said there is **'no discussion today with Christian [Horner]'** about Alpine.
Renault holds a **veto right** over the sale of Otro Capital's 24% Alpine stake — but that veto **expires in September**.
Provost said Renault wants to **retain control** of the Alpine team 'regardless of who succeeds Otro.'
Reports say Renault is prepared to actively use its veto to **block any Horner-linked buyer** before the deadline.
After September, Otro would be free to sell its stake to **any bidder**, veto-free, reopening the door for Horner.

thread.previously: Christian Horner's best shot at returning to F1 was said to hinge on Renault's veto power over Alpine's ownership expiring in September, after which Otro Capital could sell its stake freely.
thread.changed: Renault's CEO has now publicly denied any current talks with Horner and reports say Renault is prepared to actively use its veto to block a Horner-linked bid before that September deadline.

depth.background: Christian Horner, who led Red Bull's F1 team for nearly two decades before departing, has been searching for a way back into the sport as a **team owner or leader**, and has been linked to a consortium interested in buying a stake in Alpine (formerly Renault's factory F1 team). **Otro Capital** owns a 24% stake in Alpine and has been exploring a sale, but **Renault, as Alpine's parent company, holds veto power** over any change of ownership until a set deadline in September — after which Otro can sell to the highest bidder without Renault's approval.

cards.title: Formula 1's teenage title leader goes undercover at a German karting event — and wins
cards.what_happened: Antonelli entered a karting event in Germany under the alias 'Franz Antonelli' — a play on Verstappen's own pseudonym — reportedly outpacing other competitors at the session despite trying to stay under the radar. The appearance came in the closing days of F1's summer break, just before the grid reconvenes for the Dutch Grand Prix weekend at Zandvoort on August 21–23, where Antonelli will defend a 50-point lead over second-placed Lewis Hamilton and a 59-point lead over his own teammate George Russell.
key_points: Mercedes' **Kimi Antonelli**, F1's **19-year-old championship leader**, raced go-karts in Germany under the alias 'Franz Antonelli.'
The fake name is a **direct nod to Max Verstappen**, who used 'Franz Hermann' to race incognito in 2025.
Antonelli reportedly **smashed rival competitors' lap times** despite the disguise.
He heads into next week's **Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort** holding a **50-point championship lead** over Lewis Hamilton.
The stunt keeps alive an unofficial F1 tradition of stars **racing incognito** between race weekends.

depth.background: Kimi Antonelli was promoted to Mercedes' race seat and has become the sport's breakout story in 2026, becoming the youngest points leader in F1 history at just 19. The 'racing incognito' tradition traces back to Max Verstappen, who first used the pseudonym 'Franz Hermann' in May 2025 to enter karting events without drawing a crowd. Formula 1 is on its summer break before resuming at Zandvoort for the Dutch Grand Prix — confirmed as the venue's final scheduled appearance on the calendar after five years back on the F1 schedule, and the first time the race will run as a Sprint weekend.

cards.title: Cadillac F1's team boss is sacked as the team's billionaire owner faces an FBI probe — even after a record $12.5bn Lakers sale
cards.what_happened: Cadillac unexpectedly removed team principal Graeme Lowden and replaced him with Marcin Budkowski, in a move reported as a sacking rather than a mutual decision. This coincided with mounting reports that Walter is under FBI and SEC investigation, with his phone and computer seized and his firms — including Guggenheim Partners and two insurance subsidiaries — having received grand jury subpoenas back in February. Just days before the leadership change became public, Walter agreed to sell the Lakers to Josh Kushner and former Disney chief Bob Iger for a record $12.5 billion, up from the $10 billion he paid for the team roughly 10 months earlier; the deal still needs NBA Board of Governors approval, expected in September. Reports note the federal probe does not directly touch Cadillac F1 or the Dodgers, and the teams continue operating as normal.
key_points: Cadillac F1 has replaced team principal **Graeme Lowden** with **Marcin Budkowski**, described as a sacking.
Team owner **Mark Walter** is under **FBI and SEC investigation** over roughly **$16–20 billion** in undisclosed private-credit loans.
Walter's phone and computer were **seized by the FBI**; his firms received grand jury subpoenas in February.
Days earlier, Walter sold the **LA Lakers for a record $12.5 billion** — a **25% profit** in just 10 months of ownership.
The investigation does **not directly implicate** Cadillac F1 or the Dodgers, but raises questions about ownership stability.

depth.background: Mark Walter runs TWG Global and Guggenheim Partners, and his sprawling sports empire includes the LA Dodgers, the LA Lakers (until this sale), and — new to the 2026 grid — the Cadillac Formula 1 team, one of F1's newest entrants. As a brand-new team still building competitiveness, Cadillac depends heavily on stable leadership and investor confidence. The federal investigation, run by Manhattan prosecutors and the SEC, centers on roughly $16–20 billion in private-credit loans that flowed from Walter-linked insurers through third parties to entities tied to Walter or TWG Global without being properly disclosed as related-party transactions.

cards.title: Red Bull fends off Cadillac's approach for chief engineer Paul Monaghan with a counteroffer
cards.what_happened: Reports suggested Paul Monaghan was on the verge of leaving Red Bull for **Cadillac**, F1's newest team, as it builds out its technical department ahead of a fuller 2027 push. Red Bull responded with a **counteroffer** substantial enough to persuade the **58-year-old** to stay, according to paddock reporting, and he was back working in the Red Bull garage at the **Hungarian Grand Prix** in Budapest. The near-miss underscores how aggressively Cadillac has been recruiting experienced engineering and technical staff from rival teams as it tries to compress years of institutional knowledge into a much shorter build-up.
key_points: Red Bull has reportedly kept veteran chief engineer **Paul Monaghan** from leaving for **Cadillac** by matching or beating its offer.
Monaghan, nicknamed **'Pedals'** in the paddock, has spent years in senior Red Bull technical roles and was back in the garage at the **Hungarian Grand Prix**.
Cadillac, F1's newest team, has been aggressively **poaching experienced engineering talent** from established outfits as it builds its operation from scratch.
The episode is part of a wider pattern this season of new and expanding teams raiding rivals' technical staff, not just their drivers.

depth.background: When a new Formula 1 team joins the grid — as Cadillac did this season — it typically has no existing engineering department, so it has to build one almost entirely by hiring away experienced staff from established rivals, often at a significant pay premium. This kind of quiet personnel story rarely gets headlines the way driver transfers do, but senior race and design engineers can matter just as much to a car's competitiveness. Paul Monaghan has spent years in senior technical roles at Red Bull, one of the grid's most successful teams, giving him exactly the pedigree a new team like Cadillac would want.

cards.title: F1's 2027 driver market blows wide open: only 8 of 22 seats are filled
cards.what_happened: An official F1 update confirmed that just **8 of the 22 seats** on the 2027 grid are currently filled, leaving **14 seats** open with the season not even past its summer-break halfway point. The update reaffirmed Max Verstappen's status: his Red Bull exit clause is active, and he's reportedly been warned by people close to the sport about the downsides of a move to McLaren, where seat politics and an already title-winning lineup could complicate his fit. Elsewhere, Audi's driver picture firmed up slightly — Gabriel Bortoleto's camp shut down speculation about an exit, saying his contract has **'no clauses,'** while veteran Nico Hülkenberg is expected to continue alongside him. Meanwhile Carlos Sainz's future at Williams and several other seats, including at teams still finalising 2027 plans, remain unresolved.
key_points: F1 has officially confirmed only **8 of the 22 seats** on the 2027 grid are locked in, with **14 seats** still undecided.
**Max Verstappen's** exit clause in his Red Bull contract is now active, and he's been publicly **warned about the downsides** of a rumoured move to McLaren.
**Audi** has moved to shore up its lineup, with Gabriel Bortoleto's camp shutting down exit talk and Nico Hülkenberg expected to partner him.
The uncertainty spans midfield and top teams alike, with **Carlos Sainz's** Williams future among several other seats still unresolved.
2026's 'silly season' is unusually wide open because so many contracts were written to expire together at the end of this year.

depth.background: Formula 1 driver contracts typically run one to three years, and a cluster of them were signed to expire at the end of **2026** — meaning an unusually large share of the 22-driver grid is up for renegotiation at once heading into 2027. Complicating things further, F1's new technical regulations take effect in 2027, prompting teams to rethink which drivers best suit the new cars before locking in long-term deals. Max Verstappen, a four-time champion, has an **exit clause** in his Red Bull contract tied to team performance that has now become active, making him the single biggest variable in the market and drawing interest from rivals including McLaren.

cards.title: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now active — and McLaren is reportedly circling
cards.what_happened: Verstappen went into F1's summer break sitting **6th** in the drivers' championship, well outside the top two — the threshold that activates an exit clause in his Red Bull contract, giving him a window from **August to October** to explore a move elsewhere. He has not announced any decision to leave or retire, but he is now widely described as the driver market's biggest storyline for **2027**, with **McLaren** repeatedly linked as a possible destination — though reports say he's been cautioned about the downsides of that specific move. The broader picture: Formula 1's own account says only **8 of 20 grid seats** are fully confirmed for 2027, leaving **14 seats** still open.
key_points: Verstappen's Red Bull contract has a **performance clause** letting him explore other teams if he's outside the **top two** in the standings at the summer break — and he's currently **6th**, about **110 points** behind leader Kimi Antonelli.
The clause is active from **August to October**, making the four-time champion **F1's biggest driver-market story** heading into 2027.
Verstappen has **not** announced he's leaving or retiring, but reports say he's been **warned about the downsides** of a move to McLaren.
F1 says only **8 of the grid's drivers** are '100% confirmed' for 2027, leaving **14 seats** still open across the field.

thread.previously: We reported that Max Verstappen was expected to confirm he was staying at Red Bull through 2028 around the Dutch Grand Prix.
thread.changed: Instead, it's now clear his contract contains a **performance exit clause** that has been **triggered** because he entered the summer break outside the top two in the standings — he's currently **6th**. He hasn't announced a move, but he's now reportedly F1's biggest free-agent story, with **McLaren** among the teams linked.

depth.background: **Max Verstappen** has won four consecutive drivers' championships with Red Bull, but a sweeping overhaul of F1's technical and power-unit rules for **2026** reset the competitive order, and Red Bull has struggled to keep pace with rivals like McLaren and Mercedes. Verstappen has been openly critical of the new regulations, and reports say his management specifically negotiated a performance-based **exit clause** into his contract because of his 'longstanding apprehension' about how the 2026 rules would affect Red Bull's competitiveness.

cards.title: Bortoleto shuts down Audi exit talk with a 'no clauses' contract
cards.what_happened: Bortoleto told media this week he has a **long-term, multi-year contract** with Audi that runs well beyond 2026. Asked about its structure, he said **"there are no clauses"** — notable in a sport where driver deals are usually loaded with performance triggers and team options. He confirmed he'll be at Audi **"next year, and not only next year, but for the following years as well,"** with reports suggesting the deal stretches toward Audi's 2030 target. The statement directly addresses swirling rumors that Audi could pursue Sainz or Piastri for 2027. It lands as Audi endures a difficult first season as a full works team, sitting near the back of the constructors' standings.
key_points: Bortoleto says his Audi deal has **no exit clauses**, unusual for F1 contracts
Deal runs **beyond 2026**, toward Audi's stated **2030** project target
He's scored **10 of Audi's 12 points** in 2026, the team's top scorer
Move addresses rumors linking **Carlos Sainz** and **Oscar Piastri** to his seat
Audi is in its **debut season** as a full manufacturer works team

depth.background: Audi entered Formula 1 in 2026 as a full works manufacturer, absorbing the former **Sauber** team, with boss **Mattia Binotto** framing it as a long-term project aimed at real competitiveness by **2030**. **Gabriel Bortoleto**, a 21-year-old Brazilian, joined as a rookie in 2025 (Sauber's final season) and has been the team's most productive scorer through a rocky debut works season. Speculation had linked bigger names — Sainz and even reigning-form McLaren driver Piastri — to a future Audi seat, raising doubts about Bortoleto's own long-term status at the team.

cards.title: McLaren admits its 2026 car is too short — and won't fix it until 2027
cards.what_happened: McLaren has confirmed it deliberately chose an unusually short wheelbase — about **3,250mm**, well under the regulation maximum of **3,400mm** — for its 2026 car, aiming to save weight under F1's strict minimum-weight rules. The trade-off: a shorter wheelbase leaves less room for the **floor**, the flat underbody surface that generates most of a modern F1 car's downforce, so McLaren has had less floor area to extract performance from than rivals running longer cars. Because chassis dimensions are fixed for the season, the team cannot correct this until it designs an entirely new car for **2027**. McLaren says that 2027 challenger is already being planned with a **longer wheelbase and revised suspension layout** to free up floor space. The team stresses its current car remains competitive — it leads both titles — but the limitation has capped how much more performance in-season upgrades can unlock.
key_points: McLaren's 2026 car runs a **3,250mm** wheelbase versus the **3,400mm** allowed
The shorter chassis **limits floor size**, capping aerodynamic downforce
Team prioritized **cutting weight** over maximizing floor area
Wheelbase is **locked for the season** — fix only arrives with the **2027 car**
2027 car is already planned with a **longer wheelbase and new suspension**

depth.background: F1's **2026 regulations** brought all-new car and engine rules, forcing every team into fundamental design trade-offs under a tight weight limit. A team's chosen **wheelbase** length is locked in for the whole season, since chassis dimensions can't be redesigned mid-year. McLaren enters the summer break leading **both championships**, but has now confirmed a design compromise that has quietly held back its car's ceiling all season.

cards.title: Verstappen: 2026 rules 'neutralise' the fastest drivers
cards.what_happened: In fresh comments reported on 16 August, Verstappen explained in detail why he thinks the 2026 rules blunt the difference a skilled driver can make. He said gaining time through a corner should be "free lap-time" in any normal racing series, but under 2026's energy rules an aggressive, faster corner exit **penalises the driver on the next straight** because it burns through battery deployment. He said drivers now have to constantly alter gear choice, braking, and throttle technique just to manage energy rather than to go faster, calling it "**neutralising a lot of lap-time**." Verstappen tied this directly to the season's pattern of unusually tight gaps between team-mates and rival cars, arguing it isn't because racing is closer but because the rules cap how much any one driver can exploit their edge. The remarks land just ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, his final home race this year, with Verstappen currently sixth in the standings on 109 points.
key_points: Verstappen says 2026 power rules **neutralise** driver skill mid-corner.
Faster cornering now costs speed on the **following straight**.
Comes just before his **final home race** at Zandvoort.
Verstappen sits **sixth**, on 109 points, well off the lead.
He links the rules to unusually **close team-mate battles** all season.

depth.background: F1's 2026 cars run a radically different power unit: a near **50:50 split** between the petrol engine and an electric motor (MGU-K) whose output nearly tripled from the old rules. That makes energy/battery management, not just raw speed, decide lap time, and Verstappen has criticised the concept since preseason testing. The FIA has already agreed to dial the electric share back to **58:42** for 2027 and **60:40** for 2028 partly in response to driver complaints like his.

cards.title: Cadillac's new boss says cracking Ferrari's engine secrets is the key to ending a winless run
cards.what_happened: In his first detailed remarks since taking over, new Cadillac team principal Marcin Budkowski pinpointed exactly where he thinks the team is losing time: understanding the 'intricacies' of energy management on its Ferrari power unit. Budkowski said engine suppliers do not always hand customer teams 'all the tricks of the trade,' calling that simply 'part of the game' in F1. He pointed to **McLaren** as his model — that team started 2026 complaining it lacked full information from Mercedes about the new-era engine, yet went on to win the **Hungarian Grand Prix** once it closed that knowledge gap. Cadillac's two drivers, Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas, remain without a single World Championship point after 11 rounds of the team's debut season. Budkowski, who officially takes charge at the Dutch Grand Prix on August 21-23, is framing better communication with Ferrari — not new car parts — as the fastest route to Cadillac's first points.
key_points: Marcin Budkowski replaced Graeme Lowdon as Cadillac boss just days ago
Cadillac has scored **zero points** through 11 rounds this season
Budkowski wants to master Ferrari's **energy management** tricks
He cites McLaren's Hungarian GP win as proof it can work
His first race in charge is the Dutch GP on **August 21-23**

depth.background: F1's redesigned 2026 rules brought all-new **power units** (the combined engine-plus-battery system) that lean far more heavily on electrical energy than before, so how a team manages that energy across a lap has become a genuine performance differentiator. Cadillac is F1's newest team, backed by General Motors, and it races with **Ferrari-supplied engines** rather than building its own — a common F1 arrangement known as being a 'customer team.' Cadillac abruptly sacked team boss Graeme Lowdon this week and replaced him with F1 veteran **Marcin Budkowski**, whose past stops include Ferrari, McLaren, the FIA and Renault/Alpine.

cards.title: Christian Horner's best shot at an F1 return hinges on a September veto deadline at Alpine
cards.what_happened: Otro's 24% stake in Alpine is reportedly for sale, but Renault, Alpine's parent, currently holds a **right of veto** over who it can be sold to — and has been widely expected to block any sale to a group linked to Horner. That veto is set to **expire in September 2026**, after which Otro would be free to sell to whichever bidder it chooses. Mercedes had been exploring a purchase of the stake but has since **ended those talks**, reportedly unwilling to meet an asking price of around **$720 million** — more than triple what Otro paid for it in 2023. The backdrop is a Formula 1 where team valuations are surging toward the **$10 billion mark**, making a stake like this increasingly valuable regardless of who ends up buying it.
key_points: Spanish investment group **Otro** owns a **24% stake in Alpine** that is reportedly up for sale.
Alpine's parent company **Renault holds a veto** over any sale of that stake — but the veto **expires in September**.
Once the veto lapses, Otro could sell to **any bidder**, including a group linked to Horner, without Renault's approval.
Mercedes had explored buying the stake but **walked away**, reportedly balking at a **$720 million asking price**.

depth.background: **Christian Horner** was Red Bull's team principal for two decades before being fired in **July 2025**, ending a run that included multiple championship wins. Since then he has been out of Formula 1 entirely, and Alpine — the French manufacturer team — has emerged as his most realistic route back in, if a takeover of its Otro-owned stake goes through with backers connected to him.

cards.title: Alpine boss Flavio Briatore rules out chasing a 'monster' star hire, says the team needs technical consolidation instead
cards.what_happened: Speaking about Alpine's ongoing rebuild, Briatore said the team will not chase a 'monster high-profile' figure to lead its technical department, arguing Enstone's own history shows it can develop such talent internally rather than buy it in. 'For us, it's a question of consolidating the technical side because now we have the engine, and now we need to improve our technology quality in the team,' he said. Alpine has already brought in former Ferrari and McLaren technical chief David Sanchez as executive technical director, ex-FIA figure Jason Sommerville as his deputy, and Kimi Raikkonen's former Ferrari race engineer Dave Greenwood as racing director. Briatore said that when he arrived, the situation was difficult, with frequent staff departures and management changes, and that building a stable, strong technical team matters more now than one big-name hire.
key_points: Briatore said Alpine will **not** sign a 'monster high-profile' technical figure, betting instead on **consolidating** the team it already has.
Alpine has already added ex-Ferrari/McLaren technical chief **David Sanchez**, former FIA figure **Jason Sommerville**, and ex-Ferrari race engineer **Dave Greenwood**.
Briatore, Alpine's **de facto team boss** since Oliver Oakes' shock resignation, says the priority now is **quality and consistency**, not another big name.
Alpine has climbed from **10th to 5th** in the constructors' standings in 2026 after switching to a customer Mercedes engine.

depth.background: Alpine's Enstone-based team has churned through management in recent years, including the shock resignation of team principal Oliver Oakes in May 2025, after which **Flavio Briatore** — in his third stint with the team — stepped in as de facto boss. For 2026, Alpine switched from works Renault engines to a customer Mercedes power unit, which has coincided with a marked improvement in results.

cards.title: Lewis Hamilton says he feels 'released' at Ferrari after 'shouting from the top of the mountain' for changes
cards.what_happened: In comments reported by RacingNews365, Hamilton described how he now feels 'released' to do what he 'does best' after having pushed hard — 'shouting from the top of the mountain' — for changes he felt Ferrari needed to make. He said team principal Fred Vasseur has been instrumental in working with him to implement those changes, which has 'released' him to focus on driving rather than fighting for structural fixes. At the summer break, Hamilton sits second in the drivers' championship, 59 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli, with one win and four further podiums from the season's first 11 rounds — a marked contrast to his difficult first year at Maranello in 2025.
key_points: Hamilton says he now feels **'released'** to perform after pushing Ferrari to make internal changes he wanted.
He credits team principal **Fred Vasseur** for working with him to make those changes happen.
At the summer break, Hamilton sits **2nd in the drivers' championship**, 59 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli, with his **first Ferrari win** at the Spanish Grand Prix.
It's a sharp turnaround from his **difficult debut season** at Ferrari in 2025.

depth.background: Hamilton joined Ferrari for 2025 after over a decade at Mercedes, but his first season in red was widely seen as a struggle as he adapted to a new team and car. Heading into 2026, he has pushed publicly and internally for changes to how Ferrari operates around him, and 2026 has looked like a genuine turnaround — highlighted by his maiden win for the team at the **Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix**.

cards.title: Carlos Sainz nears a one-year Williams renewal — closing the door on an Audi F1 move for 2027

Motorsport outlets say Sainz turned down an initial Williams offer before this latest, more advanced round of talks began, and that an announcement is expected imminently, possibly ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix weekend that starts August 21.

The reported new salary is above his current **€13 million**, though unverified reports of **€30 million** haven't been confirmed.

Audi's arrival as a full F1 works team created a fresh seat that fuelled months of speculation linking Sainz away from Williams, especially as his results and the team's competitiveness were debated through the season.

cards.title: Cadillac's owner shuts down Perez-to-Williams talk, says he'll be racing for them in 2027
cards.what_happened: Amid swirling rumors that **Sergio Perez** could leave Cadillac for **Williams**, team owner and CEO **Dan Towriss** issued a firm on-record denial: **"I'm confident that Checo is going to remain with Cadillac, and we're not distracted by the Williams rumours for a second. We're very confident in the relationship here, and that you're going to see him piloting the Cadillac F1 car [in 2027]."** The statement came just days after Cadillac abruptly fired team principal Graeme Lowdon and installed **Marcin Budkowski**, formerly of Alpine, in his place — a leadership shake-up that had fueled speculation about wider instability at the rookie team, Perez's future included. Despite Cadillac not yet scoring a point this season due to a lack of competitive machinery, Perez has out-qualified teammate **Valtteri Bottas 9 times to 5**, a data point Towriss and the team point to as evidence he remains worth keeping.
key_points: Cadillac co-owner and CEO **Dan Towriss** said he's **"confident"** Sergio Perez stays with the team, dismissing Williams rumors.
Towriss said fans will see **Perez piloting the Cadillac car in 2027**.
The comments follow days of speculation Perez could jump to **Williams**, where **Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz's** seats are both uncertain.
Perez currently **leads teammate Valtteri Bottas 9-5** in their qualifying head-to-head this season.
New team principal **Marcin Budkowski**, installed after Cadillac fired **Graeme Lowdon**, has also backed Perez's future.

thread.previously: Cadillac had already begun moving to shut down rumors that Sergio Perez could leave for Williams, in a story that centered mainly on a separate Verstappen comment about Fernando Alonso.
thread.changed: Cadillac's own team owner, Dan Towriss, went further today with an explicit, on-record commitment that Perez will still be racing for Cadillac in 2027.

depth.background: **Cadillac** is Formula 1's newest team, debuting in 2026 with **Sergio "Checo" Perez** and **Valtteri Bottas** as its two drivers — both experienced former race-winners brought in to anchor a brand-new outfit. The team has struggled in its rookie season and has yet to score a championship point, and this week it fired team principal **Graeme Lowdon**, replacing him with **Marcin Budkowski**, a former Alpine executive. Against that turbulent backdrop, rumors began circulating that Perez could switch to **Williams** instead, a team whose own driver lineup is unsettled heading into 2027.

cards.title: Ex-F1 steward Johnny Herbert asks if Aston Martin's woeful 2026 is the 'first sign' of Adrian Newey's decline
cards.what_happened: Speaking as F1's 2026 season paused for its summer break, former driver and ex-FIA steward Johnny Herbert said Aston Martin's dismal form this year could be the first real sign that Adrian Newey's dominant run as a designer is ending. Herbert pointed to the scale of what Aston Martin assembled around Newey — a new factory, major investment, and full technical authority — and said it was hard to understand 'how things have gone so wrong,' arguing Newey 'hasn't been able to put together a crew that is able to put together a good car.' Between them, drivers Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll have scored just one point all season, a result worse than every team except brand-new entrant Cadillac. Herbert asked directly: 'Is this the demise of Adrian Newey? The first sign of him being on a downward spiral? It happens in sport even to the very best.'
key_points: Former F1 driver and steward **Johnny Herbert** questioned whether Aston Martin's struggles mark the **'first sign'** of design legend **Adrian Newey's** decline.
Aston Martin lured Newey from Red Bull in 2025, making him a **5% shareholder** and technical partner for the team's 2026 car.
Despite Newey's involvement, Aston Martin has had one of the **worst starts of the modern F1 era**, with Alonso and Stroll combining for just **one point**.
Only **Cadillac**, F1's brand-new team, has fared worse than Aston Martin so far this season.
Herbert asked: **'Is this the demise of Adrian Newey?'** — questioning whether even F1's most decorated designer can be undone by team-building failures.

depth.background: **Adrian Newey** is widely regarded as the most successful car designer in Formula 1 history, having built championship-winning cars for Williams, McLaren, and Red Bull across three decades. In 2025, Aston Martin — owned by billionaire Lawrence Stroll — convinced Newey to leave Red Bull, giving him a 5% ownership stake and naming him managing technical partner to lead the team's car for F1's new 2026 technical regulations, alongside a brand-new factory built specifically to support him. Expectations were high given Newey's track record and the scale of investment behind him.

cards.title: McLaren boss admits he feared Norris-Piastri fallout after their title fight — says the opposite happened
cards.what_happened: Speaking as F1 approaches the second half of the 2026 season, McLaren team principal **Andrea Stella** said he had no guarantee the Norris-Piastri relationship would remain intact after their tense 2025 title fight, which Norris won with Piastri finishing third. Stella said he has been struck by how the pair have handled the aftermath — rather than the relationship fraying, he said it has 'actually become even stronger,' both between the two drivers and with the wider team. He noted the dynamic wasn't fully predictable: while Norris came into 2026 fully bought in after his championship, Piastri's response was less certain, but Piastri has instead leaned more heavily on the team to accelerate his development on and off the track. Stella said he remains 'very pleased' with how both drivers are performing in 2026.
key_points: Team boss **Andrea Stella** admits he wasn't sure the Norris-Piastri relationship would survive their 2025 title battle.
**Lando Norris won** the 2025 title; **Oscar Piastri finished third**, having led for much of the season.
Stella says the bond has instead grown **'even stronger'** heading into the second half of 2026.
Piastri has leaned more heavily on the team to work through the disappointment, Stella said.

depth.background: Norris and Piastri fought a season-long title battle in 2025 that went down to the final race, with Norris coming out on top and Piastri dropping to third. Bitter intra-team title fights have wrecked driver relationships before in F1 history — team orders controversies and public friction are common when two drivers from the same team are racing each other for a championship. Going into 2026, there was genuine uncertainty inside McLaren about whether that rivalry would sour the pairing for the new season, especially with Piastri absorbing the disappointment of losing after leading for long stretches.

cards.title: Red Bull says fixing car 'consistency' — not a big upgrade — is the key to its second-half fightback
cards.what_happened: Red Bull team principal **Laurent Mekies** said the RB22's central weakness this season has been a lack of **consistency** rather than a lack of outright pace — the car is unusually sensitive to small variables like kerb strikes, gravel pickup, or changing wind direction, which has repeatedly undermined driver confidence lap to lap. Mekies said fixing that sensitivity, to reliably hand Max Verstappen and teammate Isack Hadjar a car they can trust, is where he sees the most available performance gain for the second half of 2026, rather than pursuing a major new aerodynamic package. His comments echo Verstappen's own description of the car showing unusual **'car degradation'** through races.
key_points: Team boss **Laurent Mekies** says the RB22's core issue is **inconsistency**, not raw pace.
Small factors — kerb damage, wind direction — have been knocking driver confidence in the car all season.
Verstappen has separately flagged **'car degradation'** as a specific concern with the RB22.
Red Bull is targeting **balance and qualifying gains**, not a headline aerodynamic overhaul, for the second half.

depth.background: Formula 1 teams get limited in-season upgrade budget under the sport's cost cap, so identifying the *right* problem to fix matters as much as having the resources to fix it. Red Bull's RB22, built for F1's new 2026 technical rules, has shown flashes of competitive pace this season but has struggled to deliver it reliably from session to session — a very different problem from simply lacking downforce or power. Max Verstappen has been racing this car while also facing swirling questions about his contract and future at the team.

cards.title: Wolff credits a Schumacher-and-Hamilton veteran engineer for turning Kimi Antonelli into F1's youngest-ever points leader
cards.what_happened: Mercedes team principal **Toto Wolff** publicly praised Bonnington for shaping Antonelli's rapid rise, describing him as **"the optimum combination of an engineer, nerdy when he needs to be nerdy and to look at the science and the data, but also super compassionate when the driver needs support"** — both a **"good mentor"** and a **"strong boss."** In his second F1 season, Antonelli has won **5 of 7 races** so far in 2026 and become the sport's **youngest-ever championship leader**, holding a **41-point** lead over Hamilton in the standings.
key_points: Antonelli has **5 wins from 7 races** and leads the championship by **41 points**
He's F1's **youngest-ever championship leader**
Race engineer **Pete 'Bono' Bonnington** — who engineered Michael Schumacher, then Lewis Hamilton for 12 seasons — now guides him
Wolff calls Bonnington 'nerdy' with data but a **'strong boss'** who mentors Antonelli

depth.background: A Formula 1 race engineer is the driver's closest technical partner — in constant radio contact, managing strategy, car setup and in-race decisions. **Pete Bonnington** built his reputation over a long Mercedes career: he was **Michael Schumacher's** race engineer during Schumacher's Mercedes comeback, then spent **12 seasons** as **Lewis Hamilton's** engineer. When Hamilton left for Ferrari and Mercedes promoted rookie **Kimi Antonelli** for 2025, Bonnington stayed on to guide the teenager instead.

cards.title: Ferrari hands Hamilton an all-new chassis for the Dutch GP as Mercedes scrambles a 'Plan B'
cards.what_happened: Ferrari is preparing an **all-new chassis** for Hamilton in time for the **Dutch Grand Prix** at Zandvoort (August 21–23), part of an aggressive upgrade package meant to close the gap in F1's title fight. Hamilton currently trails Antonelli by **50 points** in the standings. In response, Mercedes is reportedly activating a **"Plan B"** — pulling forward upgrades originally earmarked for its **2027 car** into production for the rest of this season, with minor updates arriving as soon as Zandvoort and a bigger package potentially moved up from Singapore in October to **Bahrain**, held the week before.
key_points: Ferrari will give Lewis Hamilton an **all-new chassis** for the **Dutch Grand Prix**
Hamilton trails championship leader **Antonelli by 50 points** heading out of the summer break
Mercedes is pulling **2027-car upgrades forward** into 2026 to defend against the Ferrari threat
A bigger Mercedes upgrade could be moved up to **Bahrain**, ahead of schedule

depth.background: F1 teams operate under a strict budget cap, so a major mid-season upgrade — like a whole new chassis, the central structural 'tub' a car is built around — is a significant, resource-intensive statement of intent. Lewis Hamilton moved to **Ferrari** for 2026 after over a decade at Mercedes, chasing a record-extending championship, and has shown title-contending pace including a win at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix. Mercedes, meanwhile, has been relying on teenage sensation **Kimi Antonelli**, now the championship leader in his second F1 season.

cards.title: Audi opens the door to Carlos Sainz for 2027 as his Williams future comes into doubt
cards.what_happened: In an exclusive interview during the F1 summer break, Audi team principal Mattia Binotto said it was **'flattering'** that Sainz has been linked with Audi for 2027, adding that outside interest shows people **'perceive that our project has a clear ambition and is going in the right direction.'** Separately, reports emerged that Audi's camp had discussed with Nico Hulkenberg's side whether he would step aside — reportedly even discussing a **financial arrangement** — to free up a seat for Sainz, but those talks did not progress. Hulkenberg addressed the rumours directly at Spa-Francorchamps, joking that **'the reserve driver's seat is available'** and calling it **'typical summer F1 noise.'** Audi has indicated its 2027 line-up is still expected to be Hulkenberg and Bortoleto, leaving Sainz's path forward unclear as the summer break winds down.
key_points: Audi F1 boss Mattia Binotto said Sainz's interest proves the team's project is **'going in the right direction'**
Sainz's Williams contract runs out at the **end of 2026**, and a tough season has fuelled exit speculation
Reports say Audi explored **paying Nico Hulkenberg** to give up his seat for Sainz, but the talks reportedly stalled
Hulkenberg brushed off the rumours, joking only the **'reserve driver's seat'** is available
Audi is still expected to **keep Hulkenberg and rookie Gabriel Bortoleto** for 2027, leaving Sainz's next move open

depth.background: Carlos Sainz once turned down a seat at Sauber (Audi's F1 project before it became a full manufacturer team) to join Williams for 2025 instead. That switch has not gone to plan — Williams has struggled through the 2026 season, and Sainz's contract with the team expires at the end of the year. Audi, meanwhile, has stepped up from being just an engine supplier to owning a full **'works' team** (one directly run by the car manufacturer, not just a customer), with Nico Hulkenberg and rookie Gabriel Bortoleto as its 2026 line-up. Both of those drivers are believed to already be on longer-term deals, which complicates any Sainz move.

cards.title: Red Bull reportedly lines up Aston Martin's Tom McCullough to replace Lambiase
cards.what_happened: German media reported this week that Red Bull has all but finalized a deal to hire **Tom McCullough** away from Aston Martin, where he has spent **13 years**, most recently as **Performance Director**. At Red Bull, McCullough would take the role of **Head of Racing**, overseeing all trackside operations and managing the race engineers during Grand Prix weekends — effectively succeeding **Gianpiero Lambiase**, who has been Max Verstappen's dedicated race engineer for years. McCullough is expected to leave Aston Martin at the **end of the 2026 season**. Neither Red Bull nor McCullough has officially confirmed the move, and outlets are treating it as a strong, well-sourced report rather than a done deal.
key_points: Red Bull is reported to have agreed to bring in Aston Martin's **Tom McCullough** as its new **Head of Racing**, per German media.
He would replace **Gianpiero Lambiase**, long known as **Max Verstappen's race engineer** and a senior figure at Red Bull.
McCullough has been Aston Martin's **Performance Director for 13 years** and would leave the team at the **end of 2026**.
