cards.title: Australia axes Jake Weatherald after the 'Darwin disaster', recalls Matt Renshaw — and gives Marnus Labuschagne one more Test to save his spot
cards.what_happened: Following the nine-wicket loss to Bangladesh in Darwin — Australia's first-ever Test defeat to Bangladesh — national selectors dropped opening batter Jake Weatherald, who scored 23 and 0 in the match, and recalled Matt Renshaw for the second Test in Mackay. Marnus Labuschagne, who managed only 1 and 31 at No.3, keeps his place in the squad, but head coach Andrew McDonald publicly acknowledged the right-hander has work to do to hold his spot going forward. The fallout from the Darwin loss was compounded by photos of players golfing during the post-match period, which drew criticism from fans and commentators questioning the squad's focus.
key_points: **Jake Weatherald** is dropped after scoring **23 and 0** in the shock Darwin loss to Bangladesh, replaced by **Matt Renshaw** for the second Test.
It's Australia's **first-ever Test defeat to Bangladesh**, a genuine shock result that triggered the selection shake-up.
**Marnus Labuschagne** survives for now despite managing just **1 and 31**, but coach Andrew McDonald says he still has work to do to secure his No.3 spot.
The axing follows public backlash after photos surfaced of players golfing in the aftermath of the loss.

thread.previously: After a shock nine-wicket loss to Bangladesh in Darwin — a first-ever Test defeat to Bangladesh for Australia — selectors were reportedly weighing batting changes, with anger further stoked by photos of players golfing during the fallout.
thread.changed: Selectors have now actually dropped opener **Jake Weatherald**, who made just 23 and 0 in Darwin, and recalled **Matt Renshaw** for the second Test in Mackay. **Marnus Labuschagne** — who scored only 1 and 31 — keeps his No.3 spot for now, but coach Andrew McDonald has openly said he has work to do to hold onto it.

depth.background: Australia's men's Test team is one of the most successful sides in cricket history, which is exactly why losing a Test to Bangladesh — a side Australia had never lost to before in the format — landed as such a shock. No.3 is traditionally the most important specialist batting position after the openers, requiring a player who can handle the new ball early while anchoring the innings; Marnus Labuschagne has held that role for Australia for several years but has been out of form for an extended stretch, averaging just over 25 across his last 22 Tests without a century in that span.

cards.title: Australia's selectors weigh batting changes after a 'Darwin disaster' loss to Bangladesh, as photos of players golfing spark backlash
cards.what_happened: Bangladesh chased down their target inside four days to complete a nine-wicket win in the series opener in Darwin, with all-rounder **Mehidy Hasan Miraz** starring — scoring 65 in Bangladesh's first innings and dismissing Australia's Steve Smith for 44. Australian newspapers ran front pages calling it the **'Darwin disaster,'** and captain Pat Cummins looked visibly shaken in his post-match press conference, conceding the batting failure fits a **pattern selectors need to address**, not an isolated bad day. The backlash intensified after images circulated of Australian players at Darwin Golf Club while Bangladesh's squad trained in adjacent nets — widely read as a symbol of the home side's complacency heading into the match.
key_points: Bangladesh beat Australia by **nine wickets** in Darwin — Bangladesh's **first-ever Test win in Australia**.
Captain **Pat Cummins** admitted the batting collapse continued a **'longer-term trend'**, not a one-off.
Photos of Australian players **golfing** while Bangladesh trained nearby went viral and drew accusations of complacency.
Australian coaching staff had already met state coaches in Brisbane weeks earlier over a **shortage of young batting talent**.
Australia entered the series **top of the World Test Championship table**, having won 11 of their last 13 Tests.

depth.background: Bangladesh had never won a Test match on Australian soil before this series, and Australia — the reigning top side in the World Test Championship — went in as overwhelming favourites. The defeat is being read by Australian media as one of the country's most humbling home Test losses in its 149-year Test history, not just a shock scoreline but a symptom of a deeper batting problem selectors have quietly been worried about.

prev_ref.title: KKR rejects Mumbai Indians' first Hardik Pandya offer, as seven IPL franchises circle the trade

cards.title: Mumbai Indians deny active Hardik Pandya trade talks, say nothing moves until their season review ends
cards.what_happened: A Mumbai Indians spokesperson formally denied reports linking Pandya to a trade with Chennai Super Kings, saying: **'we are not engaged in conversations regarding player trades; any trade would only be possible once the review is complete.'** The team says it is currently conducting a full post-season review of IPL 2026 and that no player-trade discussions, including over Pandya, are taking place until that process ends. Despite the denial, multiple reports say interest remains live: alongside KKR and CSK, **Lucknow Super Giants** are said to have offered Pandya the captaincy plus a package worth roughly **25 crore rupees**, while Delhi Capitals have been floated as offering all-rounder Axar Patel in a possible swap.
key_points: A **Mumbai Indians spokesperson** denied the club is in active trade talks with CSK or any other franchise over **Hardik Pandya**.
MI says any trade conversation can only begin **once its post-season review is complete** — which is still ongoing.
Despite the denial, reports say **seven of the ten IPL teams** have made at least preliminary enquiries about Pandya.
**Lucknow Super Giants** are reported to have offered Pandya both the **captaincy and a package worth 25 crore rupees**.
The speculation follows MI's disappointing **ninth-place finish** in IPL 2026 under Pandya's captaincy.

thread.previously: We reported that KKR had rejected Mumbai Indians' first offer in trade talks over captain Hardik Pandya, with seven of the ten IPL franchises reportedly circling the deal.
thread.changed: Mumbai Indians have now pushed back publicly, denying they are in active trade talks with any franchise — including Chennai Super Kings — and saying no trade conversation can happen until their post-season review is finished, even as reports of rival offers keep surfacing.

depth.background: Hardik Pandya has captained Mumbai Indians since 2024, but the team's struggles — finishing ninth in the 2026 IPL — have fuelled speculation that MI could move him on ahead of the 2027 season, similar to how Lucknow traded Rishabh Pant to Delhi Capitals. Kolkata Knight Riders had emerged as the reported frontrunner, offering to hand Pandya the captaincy that Ajinkya Rahane had just stepped down from, while board figures like Sunil Gavaskar have publicly called for the BCCI to make IPL trade fees transparent as speculation swirled.

cards.title: Bangladesh's historic Test win over Australia gets a phone call from the PM — and a Cabinet shout-out
cards.what_happened: Bangladesh beat Australia by nine wickets in the first Test at Marrara Cricket Ground in Darwin, chasing down their target in just 14.2 overs for the loss of one wicket (Tanzid Hasan Tamim). Off-spinner **Mehidy Hasan Miraz** took a five-wicket haul on the fourth day to help bowl Australia out for 284 in their second innings, setting up the small final chase. The win makes Bangladesh only the **third Asian team**, after India and Pakistan, to beat Australia in a Test match on Australian soil — a genuinely historic milestone for a team that had never managed it before. Bangladesh's Prime Minister **Tarique Rahman** personally called BCB (Bangladesh Cricket Board) director Fahim Sinha to congratulate the team, and the Bangladeshi Cabinet formally congratulated the national cricket team at its weekly meeting held today, August 17 — an unusually prominent political response to a cricket result.
key_points: Bangladesh beat Australia by **nine wickets** in Darwin — only the **third Asian team ever**, after India and Pakistan, to win a Test on Australian soil.
PM **Tarique Rahman** personally phoned **BCB director Fahim Sinha** to congratulate the team.
Bangladesh's **Cabinet** formally congratulated the team at its weekly meeting today, an unusually high-level political gesture for a sports result.
**Mehidy Hasan Miraz** took a five-wicket haul to help bowl Australia out for 284 in the second innings and set up the chase.
The win lands amid a tense political backdrop, with Bangladesh's interim leadership navigating a difficult post-Hasina transition and friction with India over cricket and diplomacy.

depth.background: Bangladesh's national cricket team, nicknamed the **Tigers**, has historically struggled overseas against the strongest Test nations, and had never before won a Test match in Australia — one of the hardest places in the world to win, thanks to bouncy, fast pitches suited to Australia's traditionally strong pace attacks. Bangladesh itself has been through a turbulent political transition since 2024, and cricket has increasingly become entangled with politics there: the country's relationship with India, in particular, has been strained by the ongoing standoff over extraditing former PM Sheikh Hasina, spilling over into sports diplomacy and scheduling disputes. A prime minister personally calling to congratulate a cricket team, and a full Cabinet formally noting a sports result, signals how much national pride is riding on cricket success right now as a rare unifying moment.

cards.title: Marnus Labuschagne's Test career back on the edge as Australia's selectors meet
cards.what_happened: Australia lost the first Test to Bangladesh in Darwin by nine wickets, a result coach **Andrew McDonald** called a factor putting several top-order batters under scrutiny. Labuschagne made just 1 and 31 in the match, extending a century drought that now spans **42 innings** since his last Test hundred in July 2023, with an average of 25.32 and only nine fifties in that stretch. Opener Jake Weatherald is also under threat after failing to deliver in the series opener. Australia's selectors met on Monday to decide the squad for the second Test in **Mackay**, with uncapped or fringe batters Matt Renshaw and Sam Konstas reportedly in contention to come in.
key_points: Labuschagne scored just **1 and 31** in Australia's shock Test loss to **Bangladesh in Darwin**.
He's now gone **42 innings without a Test century** since July 2023, averaging just **25.32** in that span.
Australia's selectors met **Monday** to decide on changes for the **second Test in Mackay**.
Both Labuschagne and opener **Jake Weatherald** are reportedly at risk of being dropped.
**Matt Renshaw** and **Sam Konstas** are named as the batters in contention to replace them.

depth.background: **Marnus Labuschagne** was once the world's top-ranked Test batter and a fixture of Australia's top order, but his form has cratered since mid-2023 — a slump so prolonged that he was dropped once before, against the West Indies, and had to force his way back through five domestic centuries in nine innings for Queensland. Australia's Test side is under fresh pressure after a rare home loss to **Bangladesh**, a side they'd be expected to beat comfortably, putting selectors under public pressure to act rather than persist with underperforming senior players.

prev_ref.title: England's managing director defends snubbing Harry Brook for the Test captaincy, after Stokes publicly questioned it

cards.title: Harry Brook breaks silence on England captaincy snub, says Joe Root was 'the right' choice
cards.what_happened: Speaking ahead of England's Test series against Pakistan, Brook addressed the captaincy snub directly for the first time, saying the decision to make Root captain **'was the right one'** and that he wasn't upset by being passed over. He said he's genuinely looking forward to seeing how England perform under Root's leadership. The comments follow weeks of public debate sparked by Stokes, who'd argued that if England believed Brook would be a good captain, they should **'just give it to them'** rather than wait. Brook continues as vice-captain in Tests and already captains England's white-ball sides.
key_points: **Harry Brook** has spoken publicly for the first time since being passed over for the England Test captaincy.
He said the decision to make **Joe Root** captain instead was **'the right one.'**
Brook said he wasn't offended and is **excited to see how the team performs** under Root's leadership.
It follows **Ben Stokes** publicly questioning the snub and England managing director **Rob Key** defending it as **'too soon'** for Brook.
Brook remains vice-captain and continues to lead England's white-ball side.

thread.previously: England managing director Rob Key defended the decision to keep Harry Brook as vice-captain rather than promote him to Test captain, calling it 'too soon,' after Ben Stokes publicly questioned the call and said the team should 'just give it' to Brook if they believed in him.
thread.changed: Brook has now broken his own silence on the snub, saying he thinks Joe Root — not himself — was 'the right' choice for the job, publicly accepting the decision rather than pushing back on it.

depth.background: England's Test captaincy came open when **Ben Stokes** stepped back from the role, and the setup had previously named **Harry Brook** vice-captain — traditionally a signal he was next in line. When the job actually opened up, though, England instead recalled the more experienced **Joe Root**, a former England Test captain, rather than promoting Brook. Stokes then publicly questioned that call on a podcast, and Rob Key defended it, turning what was a private selection decision into a public debate about England's succession planning.

cards.title: England rest captain Nat Sciver-Brunt for Ireland ODIs, hand the reins back to Charlie Dean and blood a young squad
cards.what_happened: England named a **15-player squad** for their **three-match ODI series against Ireland**, with Sciver-Brunt left out entirely as she continues long-term rehabilitation and management of her calf problem. **Charlie Dean** was named captain for the series, and several experienced players — **Sophie Ecclestone, Lauren Bell, Amy Jones**, and Wyatt-Hodge — were also left out, either managing their own fitness or making way for newer players. England described the squad as **'forward-looking**,' explicitly framing the series as an opportunity to test depth ahead of bigger assignments.
key_points: **Nat Sciver-Brunt** will miss England's September ODI series against Ireland for **long-term calf management**.
Vice-captain **Charlie Dean** takes over as captain — a role she has already filled once before, standing in during a New Zealand series.
Senior players **Sophie Ecclestone, Lauren Bell and Amy Jones** have also been left out of the 15-player squad.
**Danni Wyatt-Hodge** is also managing fitness and recovery and was not selected.
England called it a **'forward-looking' squad**, giving several up-and-coming players a shot at ODI selection.

depth.background: **Nat Sciver-Brunt** is England Women's regular white-ball captain and one of the side's most important all-rounders, but has been managing a troublesome **left calf issue** through the year. **Charlie Dean**, an off-spinner and the team's vice-captain, has already deputised as stand-in captain once before when Sciver-Brunt was unavailable through injury, giving England a tested option to lead in her absence.

cards.title: India silence Gill's captaincy critics for now, bowling Sri Lanka out for 284 to seize a 178-run lead in Galle
cards.what_happened: After India posted **462** in their first innings, led by Devdutt Padikkal's 167, Sri Lanka slipped to **90 for 5** before **Sonal Dinusha's maiden Test century** and a **146-run stand** with Niroshan Dickwella (80) briefly pulled the hosts back into the contest. India's bowlers regrouped: **Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja took three wickets each**, bowling Sri Lanka out for **284** and handing India a **178-run lead**. Bad weather then interrupted play as India began their second innings, with rain threatening to eat into Day 4.
key_points: India bowled Sri Lanka out for **284** on Day 3, seizing a **178-run first-innings lead**.
**Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja shared seven wickets** between them.
Sri Lanka slipped to **90/5** before **Sonal Dinusha's maiden Test century** and Niroshan Dickwella's 80 pulled them to 284.
The bowling response came directly after captain **Shubman Gill's leadership was publicly questioned** mid-Test.
Rain threatened to interrupt play as India headed into their second innings on Day 4.

thread.previously: Indian fans and pundits had turned on captain Shubman Gill mid-Test, questioning his tactics and form as a trending hashtag criticised his leadership; Gill publicly defended himself, saying he was 'very comfortable' in the role.
thread.changed: India's bowlers answered on the field: after posting 462 in their first innings, Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja shared seven wickets to bowl Sri Lanka out for 284, handing Gill's side a commanding 178-run lead and, at least for now, quieting the captaincy critics.

depth.background: **Shubman Gill** became India's Test captain in May 2025, taking over from the retiring Rohit Sharma. His tenure has been scrutinised for lacking a marquee series win despite heavy personal run-scoring, and this **first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle**, which began August 15, carries direct weight for India's position in the **World Test Championship (WTC)** table. Criticism of Gill's tactics and form boiled over publicly on Day 2, with former India cricketer Murali Kartik calling the series a defining test of his captaincy.

cards.title: Ravindra Jadeja joins cricket's most exclusive all-rounder club — only the 4th player ever to reach 4,000 runs and 350 wickets
cards.what_happened: On **Day 3 of the Galle Test** against Sri Lanka (August 17), Ravindra Jadeja picked up his 350th Test wicket, making him the **first Indian left-arm bowler** to reach that mark — with the next-best Indian left-armer, Zaheer Khan, a distant second on 311. Combined with his batting tally, Jadeja simultaneously became the **4th player in the history of Test cricket** to record both 4,000 runs and 350 wickets, joining Kapil Dev (5,248 runs, 434 wickets), Ian Botham (5,200 runs, 383 wickets) and Daniel Vettori (4,531 runs, 362 wickets). He reached the milestone in his **90th Test**, the second-fastest of the four to do so, behind only Botham's 83 matches. He is also now the 5th Indian bowler overall past 350 Test wickets, joining Anil Kumble (619), Ravichandran Ashwin (537), Kapil Dev (434) and Harbhajan Singh (417). The feat came fittingly in **India's 600th-ever Test match**.
key_points: Jadeja became the **first Indian left-arm bowler** to reach 350 Test wickets, during Day 3 in Galle.
He's only the **4th player in Test history** — after Kapil Dev, Ian Botham and Daniel Vettori — to combine 4,000 runs and 350 wickets.
He reached the double in **90 Tests**, the second-fastest ever behind Botham's 83.
He's now the **5th Indian overall** to 350 Test wickets, behind Kumble, Ashwin, Kapil Dev and Harbhajan Singh.
The milestone came in India's **600th Test match**, adding symbolic weight to the achievement.

depth.background: Ravindra Jadeja, now **37**, debuted for India in 2012 and spent years being underestimated as 'just' a containing bowler and lower-order hitter, even as his numbers quietly piled up across more than a decade. The exclusive club of Test all-rounders who've reached both **4,000 runs and 350 wickets** includes some of the sport's greatest names — England's Ian Botham, South Africa/New Zealand great Daniel Vettori, and India's own Kapil Dev, long considered the gold standard of Indian all-round cricket. Reaching that double is rare because it demands both **longevity** (staying fit and selected for well over a decade) and genuine two-way excellence, not just being good at one skill.

prev_ref.title: Babar Azam hit on the hand in Pakistan's last England warm-up, fitness doubt before Leeds Test

cards.title: Babar Azam declared fully fit, cleared to lead Pakistan against England after hand-injury scare
cards.what_happened: Following the finger blow in the Kent warm-up match, Babar Azam was advised rest and did not bat further in that fixture, sparking concern about his availability for the opening Test. The Pakistan Cricket Board said on **August 17** that Babar has since been through training in Leeds, has been **cleared by the medical team**, and returned to full training at **Headingley**. He is now confirmed fit and available to captain Pakistan in the upcoming three-match Test series against England, with the series opener at Headingley approaching.
key_points: Babar Azam has been **cleared by Pakistan's medical team** and returned to full training in Leeds.
He's now confirmed **fit and available** to captain Pakistan in the 3-match Test series against England.
The scare came from a blow to his finger during a **warm-up match** at Kent, off a delivery from pacer Manny Lumsden.
PCB had called the earlier withdrawal from the warm-up game **purely precautionary**, not serious damage.
It removes doubt just before the **first Test at Headingley, Leeds** begins.

thread.previously: Babar Azam was struck on the hand during a tour warm-up match at Kent and was withdrawn from the rest of the game as a precaution, casting doubt on his availability for the first Test.
thread.changed: Pakistan's medical team has now fully cleared him after training in Leeds, and he is confirmed fit to captain the side in the Headingley Test.

depth.background: Babar Azam is Pakistan's Test captain and a central figure in the batting line-up, so any injury doubt around him ahead of a major series carries outsized weight. He was hurt on **August 14-15** during a tour warm-up match against a Professional County Club Select XI at Kent, when he was struck on the hand while batting and retired hurt after scoring 5 off 17 balls. At the time, the Pakistan Cricket Board said the decision to withdraw him from the rest of that practice game was a precaution, based on the team doctor's assessment, and stressed there was **no serious damage**.

cards.title: Gavaskar demands the BCCI make IPL trade fees public, as Hardik Pandya trade talk builds
cards.what_happened: Former India captain **Sunil Gavaskar** publicly called on the BCCI to make IPL trade financial details fully transparent, arguing that keeping the numbers confidential leaves other franchises unable to verify whether a trade complies with the league's salary cap. 'It's important for full transparency,' Gavaskar said, adding that the IPL is 'the greatest T20 league in the world' and needs to guard against 'finger-pointing... from those jealous of it.' The comments follow the completed trade sending **Rishabh Pant** back to Delhi Capitals and **Kuldeep Yadav** to Lucknow Super Giants, and come as speculation builds over a possible trade involving Mumbai Indians all-rounder **Hardik Pandya**, with both **Kolkata Knight Riders** and **Rajasthan Royals** reported to have made informal approaches to Mumbai Indians — though nothing has been finalised or made public.
key_points: Legend **Sunil Gavaskar** says all IPL trade financial details should be made **public**
Right now, trade fees are known only to the **BCCI, the two franchises, and the player**
Gavaskar says the secrecy stops rival teams from checking **salary-cap compliance**
It follows the high-profile **Rishabh Pant–Kuldeep Yadav** swap between Delhi Capitals and Lucknow Super Giants
Talk is now building around a possible **Hardik Pandya trade**, with KKR and Rajasthan Royals both said to have shown interest

depth.background: The **IPL (Indian Premier League)** allows franchises to trade contracted players between each other's rosters for an agreed fee, on top of the annual player auction. Because the league operates under a hard **salary cap** — a maximum total amount each team can spend on player salaries — the actual money changing hands in a trade matters: it affects how much cap space each side has left. Currently the BCCI, the two clubs involved, and the player know the exact trade figure, but it is not published, unlike the player-movement itself, which is announced publicly. Gavaskar's comments come after the **Rishabh Pant–Kuldeep Yadav** trade, where Pant moved to Delhi Capitals at a reported ₹15 crore (about $1.8 million) fee and Kuldeep Yadav went to Lucknow Super Giants for roughly ₹13.5 crore.

cards.title: Shubman Gill's captaincy comes under public fire mid-Test as India's Sri Lanka series turns into a leadership trial
cards.what_happened: With the first Galle Test underway since **August 15**, criticism of Gill's captaincy — not the team's results, but his own tactical decisions and batting form — has built up among Indian fans and pundits, with a critical hashtag about his leadership trending on social media. Former India cricketer Murali Kartik called this series a pivotal test of Gill's captaincy given India's position in the WTC standings, saying 'Shubman Gill will always be questioned, whatever he does.' Gill responded publicly, saying, 'I am very comfortable with the captaincy role, and I think the way we have been progressing in the past one year... it has been very pleasing to see from my perspective,' while acknowledging India's inconsistency this WTC cycle and stressing how important the series is to staying in the hunt for the WTC final.
key_points: Indian fans and pundits are **openly questioning Gill's tactics and form** during the Galle Test
Former player **Murali Kartik** says **'Gill will always be questioned, whatever he does'**
Gill publicly defended himself: **'I am very comfortable with the captaincy role'**
He took over from **Rohit Sharma in May 2025**, scoring heavily but without a marquee series win yet
The series matters for India's spot in the **World Test Championship** table

depth.background: **Shubman Gill** became India's Test captain in **May 2025**, taking over from the retiring **Rohit Sharma** — a major generational handover for Indian cricket. Since then his captaincy record has been mixed: a drawn 2-2 series in England, and no marquee series win yet, though he has personally scored heavily as a batter (reportedly over 1,000 runs across nine Tests with six centuries since taking over). The current series against Sri Lanka, underway in **Galle**, matters directly to India's position in the **World Test Championship (WTC)** — the two-year league that decides who plays the Test final.

cards.title: India vice-captain KL Rahul forced off with severe cramps in Galle — a fitness scare that revives India's rotation worries
cards.what_happened: KL Rahul was forced to retire hurt on **77 off 162 balls** during the opening day of India's first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, after suffering severe cramps that spread through his body. He first received treatment from the team physio after a cramp surfaced in his right forearm during the 51st over; things worsened from there as he felt contractions in his left hand and wrist, and muscle spasms in his legs, forcing him off the field before the tea interval. His exit ended a **150-run partnership** for the second wicket with Devdutt Padikkal, his Karnataka teammate; India captain **Shubman Gill** came in to replace him at the crease, with the team well-placed at 197/1 at the time. Early reports describe the issue as severe cramping rather than a diagnosed muscle or structural injury, and India is hopeful it was a case of exhaustion after a marathon innings in humid conditions rather than anything more serious.
key_points: KL Rahul retired hurt on **77** after severe cramps spread from his forearm to his hand, wrist and legs during Day 1 in Galle.
It ended a **150-run partnership** with Devdutt Padikkal, his Karnataka teammate, with **Shubman Gill** coming in to bat instead.
Early reports describe **cramping, not a diagnosed injury** — India hopes it's a case of exhaustion after a long, humid innings.
It adds to a season of fitness scares for India's top order, coming weeks after **Jasprit Bumrah's** own shock Sri Lanka Test withdrawal.
Rahul's fitness for the **2nd Test in Colombo (Aug 23-27)** is now the immediate question for team management.

depth.background: KL Rahul is India's vice-captain and one of its most experienced batters, currently opening in the ongoing Test series against Sri Lanka. India has already been managing fitness concerns this series — frontline fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah pulled out of the tour in a shock, last-minute withdrawal that sparked its own internal blame game inside the BCCI. A cramping issue for the vice-captain, even a minor one, lands in the middle of an already fitness-anxious campaign for the team.

cards.what_happened: After a meeting with a senior BCCI official, Rohit Sharma has gone from expected to be phased out to **back in contention** for India's upcoming ODI series against the West Indies, scheduled for **September 27, September 30, and October 3** in Thiruvananthapuram, Guwahati, and New Chandigarh. This has put chief selector **Ajit Agarkar's own reappointment** in question just as his three-year term expires in September; BCCI office-bearers are expected to meet him after the ongoing Sri Lanka Test series to decide his future, with former India batter **VVS Laxman** reportedly emerging as an alternative if the board moves on from Agarkar.

BCCI secretary **Devajit Saikia** says Rohit will keep playing 'as long as he remains part of the team's plans' — contradicting the selectors' view.

India's chief selector **Ajit Agarkar**, a former fast bowler, took charge of the men's selection committee in **2023**; under his panel India has won the **2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups and the 2025 Champions Trophy**. I'm not there anymore, but even when I missed that Test match, I was like, \'he's vice-captain?\' I sort of understood the reasoning why they were saying it, but I was still like, \'what message is that sending to him?\''** He argued that if the setup genuinely believes a player will be a good leader, they should **'just give it to them'** rather than delay. England managing director **Rob Key** responded that the coaching group felt it was **'too soon'** for Brook to take on the Test captaincy, favoring Root's experience instead. England instead recalled the more experienced **Joe Root** to resume the Test captaincy.

Brook remains vice-captain despite being passed over for the top job.

depth.background: Ben Stokes stepped back from the England Test captaincy, reopening the question of who leads the side. England's setup named **Harry Brook** as vice-captain — traditionally a strong signal that a player is next in line — but when the captaincy vacancy arose, the team instead brought back the more experienced **Joe Root** rather than promoting Brook. Root had previously held the England Test captaincy for years before Stokes took over, giving him deep leadership experience but also raising questions about workload given how long and demanding the England captaincy has historically been.

cards.what_happened: Resuming from Day 1's strong position, India extended their innings through a rain-interrupted Day 2, with **Devdutt Padikkal** carrying on from his overnight century to reach **167** before finally being dismissed. Lower-order contributions, including a fighting fifty from **Dhruv Jurel**, helped India push their total past the 450-run mark, and the side closed the day on **460 for 9**. cards.title: BCCI and its own selectors are at war over Rohit Sharma's ODI future
cards.what_happened: According to multiple Indian reports, the **Agarkar-led selection panel** privately told Rohit on **two separate occasions** — right after this year's IPL, and again ahead of India's ODI series in England — that the team was moving past him for the 2027 World Cup cycle. Rohit responded on the field with a **138 off 110 balls at Lord's**, one of his best knocks in years, which reignited public support for him. Days later, **BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia** told the press Rohit "will continue to represent the country as long as he is in the scheme of things" — a statement selectors saw as **publicly overruling their private call**. Reports now say the BCCI has asked selectors to assess Rohit **series-by-series** rather than make a hard cutoff, and that he is now **in line to be picked for India's home ODI series against West Indies** in late September. Agarkar himself completes **three years as chief selector this September** and is up for a one-year extension, with the board reportedly set to discuss his future once the ongoing India-Sri Lanka Test series ends — timing that puts his tenure squarely inside this row.
key_points: Selectors reportedly told **Rohit Sharma twice** — after the IPL and again before the England ODIs — that his **2027 World Cup** plans didn't include him
Rohit answered with **138 off 110 balls** at Lord's during the England series
BCCI secretary **Devajit Saikia** publicly said Rohit stays 'as long as he is in the scheme of things', contradicting the selectors
Some selectors feel **'betrayed'**, believing the board caved to social-media pressure, not form
Chief selector **Ajit Agarkar's** own contract extension talks are now tangled up in the fallout

depth.background: **Ajit Agarkar**, India's chief selector since 2023, leads a panel working with head coach **Gautam Gambhir** to build a younger squad — centred on players like **Yashasvi Jaiswal** — for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa. **Rohit Sharma**, 39, is India's ODI captain and one of the format's greatest openers, but his 50-over workload has been under selector scrutiny for over a year. The **BCCI's administrative wing** (secretary Devajit Saikia and the office bearers) sits above the cricket-only selection committee, and normally the two operate in lockstep in public.

cards.title: Ben Stokes publicly questions England's snub of his own vice-captain
cards.what_happened: Speaking publicly for the first time since retiring, Stokes joined former teammates **Stuart Broad and Jos Buttler** on their podcast and directly challenged the ECB's decision to bypass Brook. He pointed out Brook had already been made **vice-captain** and led the side when Stokes himself was dropped for one Test after a nightclub curfew breach, yet still wasn't given the job: "He's vice-captain, and the captain is not playing, but he's not captain... what message is that sending to him?" Stokes drew a direct comparison to his own start as captain, noting he **"had no leadership or captaincy experience"** when England gave him the role in 2022. Rob Key defended the call, saying the Test captaincy is **"a huge amount to put on his plate"** given Brook already juggles all three formats, and that Brook's disciplinary record was **"not the main reason"** but was a factor. Stokes did also back Root, saying **"I wish him nothing but success"** and that his real worry was the toll the job would take on Root personally. Brook himself has stayed diplomatic, telling ESPNcricinfo just days ago that captaincy is **"blood hard"** while sidestepping questions about being overlooked.
key_points: Stokes retired from international cricket in **June 2026** after **4 years** as England Test captain
England handed the Test captaincy to **35-year-old Joe Root**, not Stokes' own vice-captain **Harry Brook**
Director of cricket **Rob Key** called it **'too soon'** for Brook to take over
Stokes, on the **For The Love of Cricket podcast**, said: 'If you think someone is going to be a good captain... just give it to them'
England open a **3-Test series vs Pakistan on August 19** at Headingley under Root, with Fleming as incoming coach

depth.background: **Ben Stokes** captained England's Test side for four years, reshaping the team around aggressive '**Bazball**' cricket alongside coach Brendon McCullum. He shocked the sport by announcing his retirement from all international cricket **mid-Test at Trent Bridge in June 2026**, citing accumulated **physical and mental exhaustion**. His vice-captain, **Harry Brook**, already captains England's white-ball (limited-overs) sides and was widely seen as the natural Test successor. Instead the ECB (England's cricket board) recalled **Joe Root**, who had previously captained England from 2017-2022, for a second stint, while **Stephen Fleming** was named the new permanent Test head coach on a **four-year deal to 2030**, starting officially on the tour of South Africa in December.

cards.title: Pakistan drop veteran pacer Diana Baig from both Asia Cup and Asian Games squads
cards.what_happened: The Pakistan Cricket Board announced two separate **15-member squads** on Sunday, August 16, for the Women's Asia Cup and the 20th Asian Games. Fatima Sana was confirmed as captain of both sides. Baig, a long-time first-choice pacer, did not make either squad — unusually, she was **not even named as a reserve/standby player**, a status normally reserved for players still in selectors' plans. Veteran all-rounder Aliya Riaz was also left out of the Asia Cup squad, though named for the Asian Games. The Asia Cup squad leans toward younger and uncapped players such as Eyman Fatima and Umm-e-Hani. The tournament itself is a high-stakes one: Pakistan open against Thailand on September 1 before a marquee clash with India on September 5 in Dubai.
key_points: **Fatima Sana** returns to captain Pakistan in Women's Asia Cup and Asian Games
Diana Baig left out of **both** squads and not even named among reserves
All-rounder **Aliya Riaz** also squeezed out of the Asia Cup squad
Women's Asia Cup runs **Aug 28–Sep 13** in Dubai; India clash falls Sept 5
Asian Games cricket event held in **Aichi-Nagoya, Japan**, Sept 17–22

depth.background: Diana Baig is a Pakistan cricket fixture: she is the **first international cricketer, male or female, from Gilgit-Baltistan**, and even played international football for Pakistan before focusing fully on cricket after 2015. A right-arm medium-fast bowler, she made her Pakistan debut in **2015** and has since been one of the team's most reliable pace options across multiple World Cups. Fatima Sana, the regular captain, had briefly missed white-ball games on Pakistan's Sri Lanka tour to fulfil a contract with Birmingham Phoenix in the Hundred, but is now back leading both squads.

cards.title: Suryakumar Yadav trade buzz builds: reports link MI star to KKR in a possible Shreyas Iyer swap
cards.what_happened: Speculation about Yadav's IPL future first picked up in June, when former India wicketkeeper Robin Uthappa suggested on a YouTube show that Yadav could return to KKR, possibly to work again under Gautam Gambhir. That early wave alone had gone cold, but a fresh report on 15 August — explicitly framed as an update ahead of the IPL 2027 trade window and auction — reignited the story: multiple outlets reported that KKR made an informal approach to Mumbai Indians, with one structure being discussed involving **Shreyas Iyer moving to MI** as part of the exchange, notable given Iyer is the man who replaced Yadav as India's T20I captain. Yadav's underwhelming IPL 2026 season, in which Mumbai Indians missed the playoffs, has added weight to the talk that the franchise may be open to moving him on. As of the latest report, neither club nor the player has made any public statement confirming a trade request or an agreed deal — this remains reported speculation, not a done deal.

One version of the deal reportedly sends **Shreyas Iyer** to MI in return
Comes months after Yadav was **stripped of India's T20I captaincy**, replaced by Iyer
Yadav managed only around **200 runs** across IPL 2026 as MI missed the playoffs
**No official confirmation** yet from MI, KKR, or Yadav himself

depth.background: Suryakumar Yadav started his IPL career at Kolkata Knight Riders from **2014 to 2017**, winning the title with them in 2014, before Mumbai Indians signed him and he became one of India's premier T20 batters. He was later made India's T20I captain and led the team to the **2026 T20 World Cup title** — but weeks later was removed from the captaincy after a poor run of form, with **Shreyas Iyer** named his replacement. IPL teams can privately negotiate player trades during an open **trade window** before each season's auction; this year's window has been open since around June 2026.

cards.title: Babar Azam hit on the hand in Pakistan's last England warm-up, fitness doubt before Leeds Test
cards.what_happened: Babar Azam was struck on the right hand by a delivery from pace bowler **Manny Lumsden** on the final ball of the 39th over on day two of Pakistan's warm-up match against a Professional County Club Select XI at Kent County Cricket Ground in Beckenham. He had scored just 5 runs at the time. Pakistan's team doctor examined him and advised he take no further part in the match as a precaution, rather than because of a confirmed serious injury. The Pakistan Cricket Board said Babar is scheduled to join the full squad's training session at Headingley on **August 17**, the Monday before the first Test against England begins on **August 19**.

Pakistan were playing a three-day practice match against a Professional County Club Select XI in Beckenham to sharpen up before the series. cards.title: Bangladesh beat Australia by 9 wickets in Darwin — their first-ever Test win on Australian soil
cards.what_happened: Bangladesh posted 426 in their first innings, built around **Tanzid Hasan's** maiden Test century — the first century by a Bangladeshi batter in a Test on Australian soil. Australia collapsed to 198 all out in reply, with Hasan Mahmud taking a career-best 6/55, forcing Bangladesh to enforce the follow-on. Australia's second innings put up more resistance, with Cameron Green making a fighting century (his highest Test score in Australia) and the total reaching 284 all out, with Mehidy Hasan Miraz taking a five-wicket haul. That left Bangladesh needing just 57 to win, which they chased down for the loss of no wickets in the second session of day four — Mominul Haque hit the winning runs, finishing 30 not out alongside Shadman Islam's unbeaten 25. Hasan Mahmud's match figures of 9/111 were described by wire reports as the best by a visiting bowler in Australia not named Jasprit Bumrah in the past 15 years, and he was named Player of the Match.
key_points: Bangladesh chased down a target of just **57** to win by **9 wickets**, completing a historic first-ever Test victory on Australian soil.
**Hasan Mahmud** took match figures of **9/111**, including a career-best 6/55, and was named Player of the Match.
Australia followed on and were bowled out for **284** despite **Cameron Green's century**, after Bangladesh posted **426** in their first innings.
It's Bangladesh's **first Test series appearance in Australia since 2003**, when the hosts swept 2-0.
Wires are calling it one of the **biggest upsets in Test cricket history**, days after Bangladesh had been bowled out for just 54 in a warm-up match.

depth.background: Bangladesh have played Test cricket for over two decades but had never previously won a Test match in Australia, and hadn't toured there for a Test series since 2003, when Australia won 2-0. Going into this match at Marrara Oval in Darwin, expectations were low — Bangladesh had been bowled out for just 54 by a Cricket Australia XI in their tour warm-up game just before the series.

cards.title: Cricket Australia's chief backs cutting back 'meaningless' bilateral ODIs — but warns of a revenue hit
cards.what_happened: Speaking in Darwin during Australia's Test against Bangladesh, Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg said he agrees that international matches 'need to matter and have context and jeopardy,' adding: 'Creating jeopardy and meaning into the games we play is important.' His comments echo remarks made earlier in the week by ICC chief executive Sanjog Gupta, who said the era of 'randomly scheduled' bilateral series 'has to come to an end,' while arguing the ODI format can survive if it's tied more closely to the ODI World Cup. Greenberg noted Gupta had made similar comments directly to Cricket Australia staff during a recent visit to Melbourne. But Greenberg also flagged a real concern: bilateral ODIs currently make up a significant share of Cricket Australia's broadcast-rights revenue, so stripping them out entirely would have a commercial cost. Greenberg is a member of the ICC working group currently finalizing the Future Tours Programme — the internationally agreed cricket schedule — for 2028-31, and the group is also sketching an early, rough version of the following 2032-35 cycle.
key_points: Cricket Australia CEO **Todd Greenberg** says international cricket needs more **'jeopardy and meaning'**, backing a rethink of routine bilateral ODI series.
His comments echo **ICC CEO Sanjog Gupta**, who says the era of 'randomly scheduled' bilateral series 'has to come to an end'.
Greenberg flagged a real tension: bilateral ODIs make up a **significant share of Cricket Australia's broadcast revenue**.
Greenberg sits on the **ICC working group** now finalizing the international schedule for **2028-31**, and sketching an early draft for 2032-35.

depth.background: One-Day Internationals (ODIs) — 50-overs-a-side matches — sit between Test cricket's prestige and T20's popularity and money, and have increasingly been criticized as filler content when played as routine bilateral series between two countries outside a World Cup. Administrators, including the ICC's own CEO, have been signaling a shift toward tying ODIs more tightly to context that matters, like World Cup qualification, rather than filling the calendar with series that carry little stake.

cards.title: Bangladesh close in on a historic first-ever Test win on Australian soil as hosts slump to 161/4, still 67 runs behind
cards.what_happened: Australia's second innings stumbled to **161 for 4 at stumps on day four**, still **67 runs behind** Bangladesh's commanding first-innings total. All-rounder **Cameron Green** (43 not out off 86 balls) and wicketkeeper **Alex Carey** (19 not out off 50 balls) are the recognized batters left at the crease, carrying what's left of Australia's hopes of saving or winning the match. Bangladesh's bowlers have kept chipping away at Australia's top order throughout the innings, and with only a handful of recognized batters left, Bangladesh need just **six more wickets** to complete what would be their **first-ever Test win on Australian soil** — and arguably the biggest victory in Bangladesh's Test cricket history. The match, the first of the series, continues into a fifth and potentially deciding day at Darwin's Marrara Stadium.
key_points: Australia closed day four on **161 for 4**, still trailing Bangladesh by **67 runs**.
Cameron Green (**43 not out**) and Alex Carey (19 not out) are the hosts' last recognized batting pair.
Bangladesh's first innings total of **426** was built on Mehidy Hasan Miraz's 65, with Josh Hazlewood taking 6-89 in reply.
A win would be Bangladesh's **first-ever Test victory in Australia** and arguably their biggest result in Test history.
Play resumes for the deciding **day five** with Bangladesh needing six more wickets.

thread.previously: We reported that Bangladesh dominated day three in Darwin, building a huge first-innings lead over Australia and pushing the hosts to the brink of defeat.
thread.changed: By the close of day four, Australia had slumped to 161 for 4 in their second innings, still trailing by 67 runs, meaning Bangladesh are now realistically one strong session away from their first-ever Test victory on Australian soil.

depth.background: **Bangladesh have never won a Test match in Australia**, in any of their previous tours, making this first Test of their 2026 series a genuine shot at cricketing history. The match is being played in **Darwin**, a less common Australian Test venue whose tropical conditions differ from Australia's traditional Test grounds. Bangladesh batted first and posted a commanding **426 all out**, anchored by Mehidy Hasan Miraz's 65, before Australia's reply collapsed to **198 all out** in their first innings, with fast bowler **Josh Hazlewood taking 6 wickets for 89 runs**. That left Australia needing to bat out or overturn a large deficit in their second innings just to avoid an innings defeat.

In a separate match on the same eliminators day, **Sunrisers Leeds' women's team advanced to the women's final**, where they will face Southern Brave — meaning Sunrisers Leeds' men's and women's sides had contrasting fortunes on the same day, with the men eliminated and the women through.

cards.title: The Hundred sets its Lord's finals: Manchester Super Giants and Sunrisers Leeds join Trent Rockets
cards.what_happened: **Manchester Super Giants** defeated **Sunrisers Leeds** by 20 runs in Friday's men's Eliminator at the Kia Oval, setting up a men's final against table-toppers **Trent Rockets** at Lord's. cards.title: Bumrah's shock Sri Lanka Test withdrawal sparks an internal BCCI blame game, reports say
cards.what_happened: Fresh reporting says the sudden nature of Bumrah's withdrawal wasn't a simple case of a player failing a late fitness test — it has instead triggered an **internal BCCI storm** over who knew what and when. According to the reports, the **CoE's sports science team had indicated to Agarkar and the selectors that Bumrah would be fit enough to travel** for the series, only for a subsequent, more thorough medical assessment to reveal his knee injury required a **longer recovery period** than first thought, forcing his withdrawal after all. That gap between the CoE's initial read and the final medical picture has reportedly left the chief selector's panel unhappy with how the CoE handled and communicated Bumrah's case. Compounding the issue, the report notes the **CoE has been without a full-time head of sports science** since Nitin Patel departed the role — a structural gap that may have contributed to the mixed signals. The BCCI is now said to be reviewing its **injury-management and communication protocols**. J&K's uncapped **Auqib Nabi**, who took 104 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, remains in as Bumrah's replacement.
key_points: Reports say India's selectors were told **Jasprit Bumrah would be fit** for the Sri Lanka Tests, only for a **later medical assessment** to rule him out.
The apparent miscommunication is between the **BCCI Centre of Excellence's sports science team** and **chief selector Ajit Agarkar's** panel.
The **Centre of Excellence has had no full-time head of sports science** since Nitin Patel's departure.
The BCCI is now said to be **reviewing its injury-management and communication process**.
Uncapped **Jammu and Kashmir pacer Auqib Nabi**, who took **104 wickets** over two Ranji Trophy seasons, was Bumrah's shock replacement.

depth.background: **Jasprit Bumrah** is India's premier fast bowler, and his fitness has been a recurring storyline for over a year because of a history of back trouble carefully managed through a workload-management system centered on the **BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE)** in Bengaluru. It was reported yesterday that Bumrah, who picked up a **knee injury** fielding in a one-day international against England in Cardiff in July, had been **ruled out of the two-Test series against Sri Lanka**, with uncapped pacer **Auqib Nabi** getting a shock call-up in his place. India's chief selector, **Ajit Agarkar**, leads the panel responsible for naming the Test squad, working off fitness assessments the CoE provides.

cards.title: Cricket Australia and players' union clash over urgency of stalled BBL pay and privatisation talks
cards.what_happened: Cricket Australia and the Australian Cricketers' Association remain **not aligned** on the urgency of resolving BBL player contracting, according to ESPNcricinfo. CA CEO Todd Greenberg said the organisation is still negotiating a pay deal with the ACA while simultaneously discussing the broader **privatisation** of BBL franchises, with hopes of making progress by September. A **contracting embargo** remains in place, leaving both teams and players uncertain about the season ahead; five senior players have reportedly rejected Australian central contracts due to pay disparities, and others are reportedly still weighing whether to play in the BBL at all. Greenberg acknowledged CA **"should have done a better job"** publicly explaining why bringing in private capital is necessary — arguing that without significantly higher salary-cap spending, Australia risks losing its best players to richer overseas T20 leagues.
key_points: Cricket Australia (CA) and the **Australian Cricketers' Association (ACA)** are not aligned on how urgently a BBL pay deal is needed.
CA CEO **Todd Greenberg** says the board is still negotiating pay terms and discussing **privatisation** with Big Bash franchises.
A **contracting embargo** has left teams and players in limbo ahead of the new BBL season.
**Five senior players reportedly rejected** Australian central contracts over pay disparities.
Greenberg admits CA "should have done a better job" explaining why private capital is needed to keep the league competitive.

depth.background: The Big Bash League (BBL) is Australia's flagship men's domestic T20 competition. Cricket Australia has been pushing a plan to sell private-equity stakes in BBL franchises — similar to moves in other T20 leagues worldwide — arguing it's needed to raise player salary caps and keep Australia's best players from being lured away by richer overseas leagues. But the plan has faced pushback, including from states like New South Wales and Queensland who rejected an earlier version of the private-capital proposal, and from the players' union over how any new money would be shared.

cards.title: Melbourne Renegades name Australia assistant coach Gavan Twining as new WBBL head coach
cards.what_happened: The Melbourne Renegades have appointed **Gavan Twining**, currently an assistant coach with Australia's national women's team, as their new WBBL head coach ahead of the upcoming season (WBBL 12). Twining has been part of the Australian set-up since late 2024 and was involved in the team's **Women's T20 World Cup** win in England this year. At the Renegades, he will work with national captain **Sophie Molineux** and leg-spin all-rounder **Georgia Wareham**. Twining will join the Renegades camp after Australia's upcoming series against Bangladesh and New Zealand concludes, and will return to the Australian team once the WBBL season finishes, juggling both roles.

He replaces **Simon Helmot**, who stepped down in April to pursue overseas franchise-league coaching roles.
Twining played a role in Australia winning this year's **Women's T20 World Cup** in England.

Twining joins after Australia's series against **Bangladesh and New Zealand**, and returns to the national set-up after **WBBL 12** ends.

The Melbourne Renegades are one of eight WBBL franchises. Their previous coach, Simon Helmot, led the team to a championship before leaving in April for opportunities coaching in overseas T20 franchise leagues, which have multiplied globally and now compete with national federations for coaching talent.

cards.title: Delhi Capitals wicketkeeper Abishek Porel denied bail, sent to 14-day judicial custody in a rape case
cards.what_happened: A court in Chinsurah, West Bengal denied bail to cricketer Abishek Porel on August 14 and ordered him held in 14 days of judicial custody. Porel was arrested on August 11 by police in Mogra, West Bengal, acting on a specific directive from the Calcutta High Court, over allegations brought by a third-year medical student studying in Karnataka. The complainant's original complaint, filed June 23 at Mogra Police Station, alleges she was in a relationship with Porel for over three years based on his assurances of marriage, which she says he later retracted; the case involves accusations of rape, physical assault, and criminal intimidation. The Calcutta High Court has set its next hearing in the matter for September 14, 2026. Porel has not been convicted of any offense, and the legal process is ongoing.
key_points: A court in **Chinsurah, West Bengal** denied bail to IPL wicketkeeper **Abishek Porel** and remanded him to **14 days of judicial custody**.
Porel, who plays for the **Delhi Capitals** and Bengal in domestic cricket, was arrested on **August 11** by Mogra police.
The case stems from a complaint filed **June 23** by a **medical student**, alleging a three-year relationship based on a **false promise of marriage**.
The arrest followed a specific directive from the **Calcutta High Court**, which has scheduled its next hearing for **September 14**.
The allegations include rape, physical assault, and criminal intimidation; Porel has not been convicted and the case is ongoing.

depth.background: Under Indian law, a criminal case alleging rape 'on the false promise of marriage' arises when a complainant says sexual relations occurred because a partner promised marriage and later reneged — a distinct and often legally contested category of case in Indian courts. Porel, a left-handed wicketkeeper-batter, plays for the **Delhi Capitals** in the IPL and represents **Bengal** in India's domestic first-class cricket, making him a recognizable name among Indian cricket followers rather than an international star.

cards.title: Devdutt Padikkal smashes a maiden Test century as India dominate day one of their historic 600th Test
cards.what_happened: India chose to bat first on winning the toss and dominated the opening day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle. Opener **Devdutt Padikkal** anchored the innings, reaching his maiden Test century off 134 balls and finishing the day unbeaten on **118**. He shared a **150-run partnership** with **KL Rahul**, who brought up his half-century before retiring hurt on **77** in the final session. Sri Lanka's only breakthrough came when spinner **Prabath Jayasuriya** dismissed captain **Shubman Gill** for 16, caught at mid-off attempting a lofted drive. India closed the day strongly placed at **273 for 2**, with **Rishabh Pant** unbeaten on 18 alongside Padikkal.
key_points: **Devdutt Padikkal** scored a maiden Test century, finishing day one unbeaten on **118**.
India closed play at **273/2** after choosing to bat first at Galle.
Padikkal and **KL Rahul** put on a **150-run partnership** before Rahul retired hurt on 77.
Captain **Shubman Gill** was the only big wicket to fall, out for 16 to Prabath Jayasuriya.
**Rishabh Pant** was unbeaten on 18 at the close alongside Padikkal.

depth.background: This is India's 600th Test match — a milestone only one other team (England) had reached before, and the first for any Asian side. India opted to bowl first when they won the toss (as covered earlier), leaving uncapped fast bowler Auqib Nabi out of the XI, with Jasprit Bumrah already ruled out of the series through injury. Devdutt Padikkal, a 24-year-old left-hander with a strong domestic first-class record, had played Tests before without converting a start into a century — making today's knock his first three-figure score at this level.

cards.title: Josh Hazlewood becomes just the ninth Australian to reach 300 Test wickets
cards.what_happened: During Australia's first Test against Bangladesh in Darwin, **Josh Hazlewood took a six-wicket haul**, dismissing Mominul Haque, Najmul Shanto, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Hasan Mahmud, Taijul Islam and Ebadot Hossain, which carried him past **300 Test wickets** for his career. He becomes the **ninth Australian** to reach the milestone, and joins **Nathan Lyon, Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc** as the fourth member of Australia's current attack to do so — the first time in Test history that four bowlers from the same attack have all individually passed 300 wickets while playing together. His career bowling average of **24.02** ranks behind only Glenn McGrath, Pat Cummins and Dennis Lillee among Australians with 300-plus Test wickets.
key_points: Hazlewood took **six wickets** in an innings against Bangladesh in Darwin to pass the milestone.
He's only the **ninth Australian bowler ever** to reach 300 Test wickets.
He joins **Nathan Lyon, Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc** as teammates who've all crossed 300 — a first in Test history.
His bowling average of **24.02** is bettered by only **Glenn McGrath, Pat Cummins and Dennis Lillee** among Australians with 300+ wickets.

depth.background: Reaching 300 Test wickets is one of cricket's most respected milestones, achieved by only a small group of the format's greatest bowlers. Josh Hazlewood has been a mainstay of Australia's pace attack since debuting in 2014, prized for his metronomic accuracy alongside more express bowlers like Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins. Australia's four-man pace-and-spin attack of Hazlewood, Starc, Cummins and off-spinner Nathan Lyon has been settled for years, making this milestone a landmark for the whole unit, not just Hazlewood individually.

cards.title: Bangladesh closes in on a stunning Test win as Australia slump to 161 for 4 following on in Darwin
cards.what_happened: Bangladesh posted a commanding first-innings total of **426**, built through the middle order, while paceman **Josh Hazlewood** was Australia's standout bowler with figures of **6 for 89**. In reply, Australia collapsed to just **198 all out**, handing Bangladesh a **228-run lead** and forcing Australia to follow on and bat again immediately. Batting a second time, Australia lost **Steven Smith**, one of the world's best Test batters, caught off spinner **Mehidy Hasan Miraz**, and closed the third day's play on **161 for 4**, with **Cameron Green (43 not out)** and **Alex Carey (19 not out)** still at the crease — still trailing Bangladesh's first-innings total by **67 runs**.
key_points: Bangladesh posted **426** in their first innings, a **228-run lead**, powered by **Josh Hazlewood's 6-89**
Australia were bowled out for just **198** in reply, forcing them to bat again
Australia closed Day 3 at **161 for 4**, still trailing by **67 runs**
Star batter **Steven Smith** was dismissed, caught off spinner **Mehidy Hasan Miraz**

depth.background: Bangladesh have never won a Test match in Australia, and Australia are one of the most dominant home Test sides in the sport — so any contest that puts Australia under real pressure on their own soil is unusual. This is the first Test of a two-match series in Darwin, played on a pitch that has clearly favored batting more than expected, with Bangladesh's middle order cashing in heavily in the first innings.

cards.title: Yashasvi Jaiswal run out in bizarre mid-pitch collision with Sri Lanka's bowler on Galle Test's opening day
cards.what_happened: Facing a delivery from Sri Lankan left-arm spinner **Keshara Nuwantha**, KL Rahul pushed the ball towards mid-on and immediately called for a single. As Jaiswal set off from the non-striker's end, Nuwantha — who had followed through and dived sharply to his right trying to stop the ball — collided with him, knocking him off balance. The contact left Jaiswal briefly stranded and disoriented, and by the time he recovered his footing, the fielding side had already gathered the ball and broken the stumps at the bowler's end with both batters caught out of their ground. Television replays showed the incident was accidental rather than deliberate obstruction by either side, and the third umpire confirmed the run-out. Jaiswal walked off for **32**, ending a promising start, while Rahul and the incoming Devdutt Padikkal steadied India to 101 for 1 at the lunch break.
key_points: Jaiswal was run out for **32** after colliding mid-pitch with Sri Lankan spinner **Keshara Nuwantha**, who had dived to stop the ball.
The mix-up started when **KL Rahul** tapped the ball to mid-on and set off for what looked like a routine single.
It is at least the **third time in his Test career** Jaiswal has lost his wicket to a running mix-up with a partner.
India recovered to **101/1 at lunch** on day one, with Rahul (32*) and **Devdutt Padikkal** (35*) rebuilding steadily.
The dismissal came on the opening day of India's historic **600th Test**, the first of a two-match series in Galle.

depth.background: India began their tour of Sri Lanka today by playing their **600th Test match** — only the third team in history, after England and Australia, to reach that mark. Yashasvi Jaiswal has been India's first-choice Test opener for the past two years and walked out with KL Rahul to start the innings after India won the toss and chose to bat. In cricket, the **non-striker** (the batter waiting at the bowler's end) must judge, in a split second, whether to run when their partner hits the ball — a call that occasionally goes wrong, sometimes with unusual consequences. Jaiswal himself has been part of more than one such mix-up earlier in his career.

cards.title: St Lucia Kings survive a rain-hit chase to edge Antigua & Barbuda Falcons in a low-scoring CPL thriller
cards.what_happened: Put in to bat, the Falcons never got going against tight St Lucia bowling, managing only **98 for 9** in their 19 overs, with Rahkeem Cornwall (26) and Amir Jangoo (23) the only batters to pass 20. Rain then reduced the Kings' chase, leaving them a **DLS target of 52** from a shortened innings — a total that looked routine on paper. Instead, the Kings' batting collapsed under pressure, losing wickets steadily to slip to **54 for 7** in just 7.4 overs before finally reaching the target with two balls to spare. Matthew Forde was the standout performer on both counts, taking **4 wickets for 29 runs** with the ball before returning to hit the winning runs himself, and was named player of the match. Despite the small numbers involved, commentators and fans described it as one of the most tense finishes of the tournament so far.
key_points: Antigua & Barbuda Falcons were bowled out for just **98/9 in 19 overs** at a rain-affected Gros Islet.
Rain cut the Kings' chase target to a revised **DLS target of 52**, but they still slipped to **54/7** before getting over the line.
Player of the match **Matthew Forde** took **4/29** with the ball and then struck the winning runs himself.
The Kings won by **3 wickets with 2 balls to spare**, their **second win over the Falcons in less than a week**.
It is St Lucia's second win in as many completed CPL 2026 matches against these opponents this season.

depth.background: The **Caribbean Premier League (CPL)** is the Caribbean's flagship T20 franchise tournament, running through August and drawing some of the biggest names in white-ball cricket to island grounds across the region. St Lucia Kings and Antigua & Barbuda Falcons had already met once this season, on August 9, when the Kings won a nail-biter by just four runs. This rematch at the Daren Sammy stadium in Gros Islet was interrupted by rain, forcing officials to use the **DLS method** — a mathematical formula used to reset targets fairly when overs are lost to weather.
