cards.title: India win the toss and bat first in their historic 600th Test, but leave uncapped Auqib Nabi out of the XI at Galle
cards.what_happened: Play began on schedule at **Galle International Stadium**, with India winning the toss and opting to bat first on what looked, in Gill's own assessment, like a good batting surface. The announced XI answered yesterday's open question: **Auqib Nabi did not get his debut**. Instead, India fielded three specialist spinners — Ravindra Jadeja, **Kuldeep Yadav**, and uncapped spinner Manav Suthar — alongside pacers Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna, betting on spin-friendly Galle conditions over an extra seamer. The top order got off to a rocky start when **Yashasvi Jaiswal was run out** within the first hour, before KL Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal steadied the innings; India were past 70 runs for one wicket as the morning session progressed. This is officially India's 600th Test and their first match of the new World Test Championship cycle, played under Gill's captaincy on a day that also happens to be India's Independence Day.
key_points: India **won the toss and chose to bat first** in what is officially their **600th Test match**, only the third team ever to reach that number.
Uncapped pacer **Auqib Nabi was left out of the XI** despite his shock call-up, with India instead picking **three spinners** — Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar.
Opener **Yashasvi Jaiswal was run out** inside the first hour, an early setback for the new-look batting order.
The Test is India's **first fixture of the 2025–2027 World Test Championship cycle** and the first under new full-time captain **Shubman Gill**.
August 15 is **India's Independence Day**, adding symbolic weight to a match already billed as a milestone occasion.

thread.previously: Yesterday's story previewed India's 600th Test — a milestone only England and Australia had previously reached — with Shubman Gill captaining and uncapped seamer Auqib Nabi in the squad after Jasprit Bumrah was ruled out injured; the open question was whether Nabi would get a shock debut.
thread.changed: The match has now actually started: India won the toss and chose to bat, and the announced XI leaves Auqib Nabi out — India went in with Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar as spinners alongside Jadeja instead of handing Nabi his debut. Play is underway, with India past 70 for the loss of Yashasvi Jaiswal, who was run out early.

depth.background: This is the same landmark Test previewed a day earlier: India entering their 600th match, a mark only England and Australia had reached before, at Galle's 50th-ever Test — a first for any Asian venue. Shubman Gill leads the side for the first time in a bilateral Test series since being installed as India's full-time red-ball captain, working alongside head coach **Gautam Gambhir**. Ahead of the game, India's pace attack had already lost **Jasprit Bumrah** to a knee injury, prompting the surprise squad inclusion of uncapped Jammu and Kashmir seamer Auqib Nabi — whose potential debut was the single biggest open question heading into the match.

cards.title: Cricket Ireland braces for protests as Afghanistan series ends at Stormont, with Amnesty warning against 'Taliban propaganda'
cards.what_happened: Ireland and Afghanistan play the **fifth and final ODI** of their series at **Stormont** today, August 15, with Afghanistan holding a strong lead after outplaying Ireland in earlier matches — including a 92-run win powered by **Ibrahim Zadran's 84**, while Ireland were bowled out for 207 despite fighting knocks from Cade Carmichael and Andy Balbirnie. Ahead of and during the series, **Amnesty International** publicly warned that hosting Afghanistan risked handing the **Taliban a propaganda platform**, and called on Cricket Ireland, its players, and the ICC to speak out on the treatment of Afghan women. Small protests, including demonstrators dressed in burkas, have already gathered outside the grounds during the earlier Stormont matches. **Cricket Ireland and the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI)** say dedicated security and policing plans are in place to protect players, staff, and fans while also allowing lawful protest. Cricket Ireland had earlier admitted **'moral discomfort'** about the series but chose to proceed with it, arguing that engagement rather than isolation was the better path.
key_points: Ireland host Afghanistan for the **fifth and final match** of a five-game ODI series at **Stormont in Belfast** today.
**Amnesty International** has warned the fixtures risk being used as **'Taliban propaganda'** and urged Cricket Ireland and the ICC to speak out on Afghan women's rights.
Cricket Ireland says **security plans are in place**, with police confirming a **'proportionate policing plan'** for any demonstrations.
Small protests, including women in burkas, have already taken place outside grounds during earlier matches in the series.
**Afghanistan has dominated the series**, including a 92-run win built on Ibrahim Zadran's 84, leaving Ireland needing a big turnaround.

depth.background: Since the **Taliban retook power in Afghanistan in 2021**, women there have been banned from playing or even watching sport, barred from universities and parks, and — according to rights groups — hunted down if they try to keep playing in secret; many of Afghanistan's former women cricketers fled the country. Under ICC rules a men's team can keep its full-member status as long as it has a men's program, so **Afghanistan's men's team keeps playing internationally** even though its women's team has been effectively erased. That contradiction has made every Afghanistan men's fixture a flashpoint: **Australia and England have both cancelled or avoided bilateral series** against Afghanistan since 2021, while others, including Ireland, have gone ahead. This five-match ODI series began in Bready on the Irish mainland before shifting to Stormont in Belfast for its last three games.

cards.title: Bangladesh push Australia to the brink on day three in Darwin as the lead balloons past 200
cards.what_happened: Bangladesh resumed day three of the first Test in **Darwin** in a commanding position after posting **351 for 6** on day two, powered by **Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century (101 runs)**, an **84 from captain Najmul Hossain Shanto**, a composed 49 from Mominul Haque, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz unbeaten on 32. That total gave Bangladesh a first-innings lead of **153 runs** over Australia's **198 all out**. As Australia batted again in their second innings on day three, the deficit kept growing — by the second session, Australia trailed by **216 runs**, with Marnus Labuschagne and Travis Head at the crease trying to build a partnership and avoid an innings defeat. Josh Hazlewood had taken 2 wickets for Australia's bowling attack the previous day but couldn't stop Bangladesh's lower order from extending the total.
key_points: By session two of **day three**, Australia trailed by **216 runs** in the first Test at Darwin — a huge deficit with the match past its halfway point.
Bangladesh's day two total of **351 for 6** was built on **Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century (101)** and a gritty **84 from captain Najmul Hossain Shanto**.
Australia's first innings closed at just **198**, meaning Bangladesh's lead was already **153** before day three even started.
Marnus Labuschagne and Travis Head were at the crease trying to steady Australia's second innings as the gap widened further.
This is Bangladesh's **first tour of Australia in years**, and a win — or even a draw — from this position would be one of their **biggest overseas results ever**.

depth.background: Bangladesh have historically struggled on **fast, bouncy Australian pitches**, and playing in **Darwin** — an unusual, tropical Test venue for Australia — adds heat and humidity as extra variables. A five-day **Test match** is decided over four innings (two per side); building a big first-innings lead, as Bangladesh have done here, puts huge pressure on the team batting last because they're chasing a target on a worn pitch. **Marnus Labuschagne** and **Travis Head** are senior, experienced Australian batters whose job on day three was to prevent the deficit from Bangladesh's dominant batting from spiraling further out of control.

cards.title: CPL debutants Jamaica Kingsmen slump to a third straight defeat
cards.what_happened: Jamaica Kingsmen lost their third straight CPL 2026 match, falling to the **Barbados Tridents by 5 runs** after being bowled out for **201 for 9** while chasing a target of **207**. It followed a tight **2-wicket opening loss to the Antigua and Barbuda Falcons** (167/7 versus 168/8) and a heavier defeat to the **Guyana Amazon Warriors** at Sabina Park, where the Amazon Warriors won by 6 wickets. With three matches gone, the Kingsmen are now **bottom of the seven-team CPL table** without a single win in their debut season.
key_points: The **Jamaica Kingsmen**, playing their **debut CPL season**, have now lost **all three of their matches**.
They fell to **Barbados Tridents by 5 runs** after being bowled out chasing, managing **201 for 9** against a target of 207.
Their campaign began with a **2-wicket loss to Antigua and Barbuda Falcons** and continued with a loss to **Guyana Amazon Warriors** at Sabina Park.
After three rounds, the Kingsmen sit **last of seven teams** in the CPL 2026 table without a win.
It's a rough start for the Caribbean Premier League's newest franchise, playing in front of home fans at Sabina Park.

depth.background: The **Caribbean Premier League (CPL)** is the Caribbean's top T20 franchise cricket tournament, featuring teams representing different islands and cities. The **Jamaica Kingsmen** are a brand-new franchise entering the competition this season, meaning they're still assembling squad chemistry and experience compared to the six established teams they're competing against. Losing narrowly, as the Kingsmen have in two of their three defeats, often reflects a team that's competitive but not yet closing out tight games — a common growing pain for expansion sides in any franchise league.

cards.title: Manchester Super Giants blitz SunRisers Leeds to reach the Hundred men's final at Lord's
cards.what_happened: Batting first under lights at the Oval, Manchester Super Giants were given a flying platform by Paul Walter and Heinrich Klaasen, who put on 114 runs together — Walter's innings included eight sixes, a new individual record for the franchise, as the pair took the total to 186 for 4 from their 100 balls. In reply, SunRisers Leeds never quite got the asking rate under control: Josh Tongue struck twice inside his opening spell, top-edging Mitch Marsh and trapping captain Zak Crawley leg-before four balls later, and despite a fighting effort from Harry Brook (49) and an unbeaten 54 from Ryan Rickelton, Leeds fell 20 runs short. The result ends SunRisers Leeds' 2026 campaign — hours after their women's side also lost their own Eliminator on the same night at the Oval — and sends Manchester Super Giants through to face Trent Rockets in Sunday's men's final at Lord's.
key_points: **Manchester Super Giants** beat **SunRisers Leeds** by **20 runs** in Friday night's Eliminator at the Kia Oval to book a spot in Sunday's men's final.

Opener **Paul Walter** smashed **80 off 46 balls** including a club-record **8 sixes** in an innings, sharing a **114-run third-wicket stand** with **Heinrich Klaasen (63 off 26)** — Manchester's biggest-ever third-wicket partnership in T20 cricket.
Manchester posted **186-4** from their 100 balls; SunRisers fell short despite fifties from **Harry Brook (49 off 31)** and **Ryan Rickelton (54 not out off 34)**.
Seamer **Josh Tongue** took **4 wickets for 26 runs**, removing SunRisers openers Mitch Marsh and captain Zak Crawley early to swing the chase back Manchester's way.
Manchester Super Giants now face **Trent Rockets** in the men's final at **Lord's on Sunday, August 16**, with SunRisers Leeds' 2026 campaign over.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's franchise short-form competition, where each innings is a fixed 100 balls rather than the usual 120 of T20 cricket, and the top four men's and women's teams from the group stage progress to knockout play. SunRisers Leeds had topped the group table and looked the form side coming into the knockouts, while Manchester Super Giants scraped into the playoffs on net run rate. Trent Rockets had already secured their place in the final by finishing group-stage leaders and winning their own semi-final-equivalent fixture, leaving the Oval Eliminator to decide their opponent.

cards.title: Pakistan captain Babar Azam retires hurt in a hand injury scare, days before the England Test series begins
cards.what_happened: On day two, Pakistan slumped from **164 for 2 to 238 all out**, handing the PCC Select XI a **67-run first-innings lead** after the hosts had made 305. **Abdullah Shafique** was the innings' top scorer with **61**. During the collapse, captain **Babar Azam** was struck on the hand by a delivery from **Manny Lumsden** and **retired hurt**, ruling him out of the rest of this warm-up game and raising doubts over his fitness for the opening Test. On the other side, England's **Emilio Gay**, also using the match to prepare for the Pakistan series, was dismissed for a **duck** in the second innings after edging behind — his second failure of the match. The PCC Select XI reached **128 for 3** in their second innings by stumps, with **Shoaib Bashir** taking 4 for 76 with the ball for the home side.
key_points: Babar Azam **retired hurt** after being struck on the hand by a **Manny Lumsden** delivery in Pakistan's final warm-up match
Pakistan **collapsed from 164-2 to 238 all out**, surrendering a **67-run first-innings deficit**
The warm-up was against a **PCC Select XI** at **Beckenham**, Pakistan's last hit-out before the **England Test series**
**Abdullah Shafique** top-scored with **61** in the innings
England's **Emilio Gay** made a **pair** in the same match, for a very different reason — form, not injury

depth.background: This is a three-day tour match between Pakistan and a **Professional County Club Select XI** at Beckenham, Pakistan's final preparation game before their full Test series against **England** begins. Pakistan had bowled the home side out for **305** on day one, but were themselves under pressure after collapsing from a strong position in their own first innings.

cards.title: Sunrisers Leeds grind past Southern Brave to reach the Hundred women's final
cards.what_happened: Defending champions **Sunrisers Leeds** beat **Southern Brave** by **five wickets** in the Hundred women's Eliminator at the Kennington Oval, chasing down Southern Brave's **114 for 7** with **116 for 5** and 11 balls to spare. **Hannah Baker** took **2 wickets for 13 runs** off her 20 balls and was named Player of the Match for a tight bowling spell that kept the target low. In the chase, **Lauren Winfield-Hill** made **37**, and **Deepti Sharma** anchored the finish with an unbeaten **28** to see Sunrisers home. The win sends Sunrisers Leeds into **Sunday's final** at Lord's, where they will defend the title they won last year. It comes after Sunrisers had already needed a separate win over Manchester Super Giants to even reach this Eliminator, in a tense finish to the group stage this week.
key_points: **Sunrisers Leeds** beat Southern Brave by **five wickets**, chasing 114/7 with **116/5** and 11 balls in hand.
**Hannah Baker** (2/13) was Player of the Match for a disciplined bowling display.
**Deepti Sharma's unbeaten 28** anchored the chase, with Winfield-Hill making 37.
Sunrisers advance to **Sunday's final at Lord's** to defend their Hundred women's title.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's franchise cricket competition, with eight men's and eight women's teams playing a 100-ball format each August. Sunrisers Leeds are the reigning women's champions and needed a nervy group-stage win over Manchester Super Giants earlier this week just to qualify for the knockout stage, before facing Southern Brave in Friday's winner-takes-all Eliminator at the Oval.

cards.title: Guyana Amazon Warriors open their CPL 2026 title bid with a comfortable win over Jamaica Kingsmen
cards.what_happened: **Guyana Amazon Warriors** began their **Caribbean Premier League (CPL) 2026** campaign with a six-wicket win over **Jamaica Kingsmen** at Sabina Park, Kingston. Put in to bowl first, Guyana bundled Jamaica out for just **117**, with **Mohammad Nabi** returning figures of **4 wickets** to rip through the middle order. Guyana then chased the target down comfortably, with **Shai Hope unbeaten on 56** off 41 balls anchoring the run-chase alongside contributions from Nabi and Quentin Sampson. The result put the Amazon Warriors top of the early CPL table and extended Jamaica Kingsmen's losing run to **three matches** from three this season. Guyana fielded a heavily overseas-stocked squad this year, including Afghanistan all-rounder Nabi, New Zealand's Glenn Phillips, and South Africa's Imran Tahir and Dwaine Pretorius, giving the team an experienced core to build a title push around.
key_points: **Guyana Amazon Warriors** bowled out Jamaica Kingsmen for just **117** to open their CPL 2026 campaign.
**Mohammad Nabi** took **4 wickets**, and **Shai Hope's unbeaten 56** sealed the chase.
The win put Guyana **top of the early CPL 2026 table**.
**Jamaica Kingsmen** have now **lost all three** of their matches this season.

depth.background: The Caribbean Premier League is the Caribbean's flagship T20 franchise competition, running annually since 2013 and expanded to **seven teams** for 2026. Guyana Amazon Warriors built a strong overseas contingent this season specifically to chase the title, pairing Caribbean talent with experienced international players like Nabi, Phillips, Tahir and Pretorius.

prev_ref.title: Bangladesh reach 96/1 at stumps, trailing Australia by just 102, after bowling the hosts out for 198

cards.title: Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century flips Bangladesh from trailing to 153 runs clear against Australia
cards.what_happened: On day two of the first Test in Darwin, Bangladesh's batting lineup built on their day-one bowling performance in dramatic fashion. Opener **Tanzid Hasan** scored **101**, becoming just the second Asian batter in history — after Pakistan's Hanif Mohammad in 1964 — to score a century on a debut Test tour of Australia. **Najmul Hossain Shanto** supported him with **84**, and the pair anchored a total that reached **351 for 6** by stumps. Bangladesh lost some late wickets but **Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32 not out)** and **Hasan Mahmud (13 not out)** dug in through the final overs to see the team safely to the close. Having trailed by 102 runs at the end of day one, Bangladesh now lead Australia by **153 runs** with four wickets in hand — a complete reversal of fortunes inside a single day's play.
key_points: **Tanzid Hasan** scored **101**, his maiden Test century, on Bangladesh's historic first Test tour of Australia.
He's only the **second Asian batter ever** — after Hanif Mohammad in 1964 — to score a century on a debut tour Down Under.
**Najmul Hossain Shanto** added **84** as Bangladesh reached **351 for 6** at stumps on day two.
Bangladesh have gone from trailing by 102 runs to now leading by **153 runs**.
**Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*)** and **Hasan Mahmud (13*)** batted out the final overs to protect the lead.

thread.previously: At stumps on day one in Darwin, Bangladesh had bowled Australia out for just 198 and replied with 96/1, still trailing by 102 runs.
thread.changed: By stumps on day two, Bangladesh piled on runs to reach 351/6 — turning a 102-run deficit into a 153-run lead — with Tanzid Hasan scoring a maiden Test century.

depth.background: Bangladesh had never played a Test match in Australia until this series, ending a **23-year wait** for a tour Down Under — historically one of the hardest places for touring teams to bat. On day one, Bangladesh's bowlers stunned the hosts, dismissing Australia for just 198, before ending the day 96/1 in reply, still 102 runs behind. Test centuries on a first-ever tour of Australia are rare for any team, let alone one still establishing itself in the format.

cards.title: Bangladesh push Australia to the brink in Darwin as Starc and Miraz clash on a tense day two
cards.what_happened: On day two of the first Test in Darwin, Bangladesh took firm control, with opener **Tanzid Hasan Tamim** producing a history-making innings that made batting look straightforward against the Australian attack for most of the day. By stumps, **Australia trailed by 153 runs**, having lost three wickets in the final session — and it would have been four had **Cameron Green** not put down a catch on the last ball of the day. Tensions boiled over during the day when **Mitchell Starc** accused Bangladesh's **Mehidy Miraz** of deliberately blocking his follow-through path, with the two exchanging words on the field after a long, hard session for the home bowlers.
key_points: Australia trail Bangladesh by **153 runs** at stumps on day two in Darwin.
**Tanzid Hasan Tamim's** history-making innings anchored Bangladesh's dominant day.
**Mitchell Starc** and **Mehidy Miraz** exchanged words after Starc accused Miraz of blocking his follow-through.
Australia lost **three wickets** in the final session — a fourth chance went down when Cameron Green dropped a catch.
It is a rare position of real control for Bangladesh in a Test match on Australian soil.

depth.background: Bangladesh have historically struggled badly on tours of Australia, where fast, bouncy pitches have traditionally favoured the host attack. Darwin, hosting this Test, is a newer and less familiar venue on the international circuit, adding an extra layer of unpredictability. Openers like Tanzid Hasan Tamim have been central to a slow but real improvement in Bangladesh's Test batting depth in recent years, even as results away from home remained difficult.

cards.title: India will play their 600th Test — the first Asian team to reach the milestone — as the Sri Lanka series opens at Galle
cards.what_happened: India's first Test against Sri Lanka, starting **August 15** at Galle International Stadium, will be India's **600th Test match overall**, making them the first Asian side and just the third team in history — after England and Australia — to reach that number. The match is also the **50th Test hosted at Galle**, the first Asian venue to reach that mark. Captain **Shubman Gill**, who described the milestone as a 'huge honour,' will lead a squad that includes vice-captain KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rishabh Pant, Ravindra Jadeja, and uncapped seamer **Auqib Nabi**, who earned a shock maiden call-up after **Jasprit Bumrah** was ruled out with a knee injury. Sri Lanka will field a 16-member squad led by Dhananjaya de Silva, with Kamindu Mendis as his deputy. The two-match series runs through late August.
key_points: India become the **first Asian team**, and only the **third team ever**, to play **600 Tests**.
The Galle Test is also the **50th Test match** ever played at that ground — a first for any Asian venue.
Captain **Shubman Gill** called leading the side in this Test a **'huge honour and privilege.'**
India's squad includes **Auqib Nabi**, uncapped, called up after **Jasprit Bumrah** was ruled out injured.
The first of two Tests runs **August 15–19** at Galle International Stadium.

depth.background: Only England and Australia had previously reached 600 Test matches — a mark of just how long and central those two nations have been to the format since Test cricket began in 1877. India, despite a huge domestic cricket culture, is reaching this landmark later because Test cricket globally has always been dominated in volume by England and Australia's early head start. Galle, meanwhile, has become one of world cricket's most picturesque and historic grounds since Sri Lanka started hosting Tests there, set beside the Indian Ocean next to a centuries-old Dutch fort.

cards.title: Pakistan slip to 261 behind on day two of their final Test warm-up before the England series
cards.what_happened: On day two of their three-day warm-up match at Beckenham, Pakistan's top order struggled to make inroads, with the side closing the day trailing by **261 runs** after the PCC Select XI's first-innings total of **305**. Openers **Imam-ul-Haq (26 not out)** and **Azan Awais (15 not out)** were still at the crease at the close of play, having avoided losing a wicket so far in Pakistan's reply. On day one, Pakistan's bowlers — sharing six wickets between them — had restricted the PCC Select XI to 305 all out. With the match reduced to three days because of player availability, day three (August 15) is Pakistan's last chance to build some batting form and rhythm before the series opener.
key_points: Pakistan closed day two trailing by **261 runs** in their three-day warm-up match at Beckenham.
Openers **Imam-ul-Haq (26*) and Azan Awais (15*)** were unbeaten at the close.
The match is Pakistan's **last hit-out** before the first Test at **Headingley on August 19**.
The fixture was **shortened from four days to three** due to player availability.
Pakistan had bowled the **PCC Select XI** out for **305** on day one.

depth.background: Before a Test series, touring teams typically play one or more 'warm-up' matches against a mix of county and invitational players to get used to English conditions — the pitch, the weather, and the swinging ball — before the real series begins. Pakistan are preparing for a three-match Test series against England that starts **August 19 at Headingley in Leeds**, their first assignment under a series that also marks a fresh start for England, who are being led by a returning captain, Joe Root, this series. This particular warm-up fixture, against a **Professional County Club (PCC) Select XI** at Beckenham, was trimmed from four days to three because of player availability.

cards.title: Southern Brave face Sunrisers Leeds in today's Hundred Women's Eliminator, with Trent Rockets waiting in the final
cards.what_happened: **Southern Brave** face **Sunrisers Leeds** in the Hundred Women's Competition Eliminator at **The Oval** today, starting at **1:15pm local time**. Sunrisers Leeds reached this stage by beating Birmingham Phoenix in the earlier eliminator round. The winner of today's match goes on to face **Trent Rockets Women**, who finished top of the table and secured direct qualification, in the final at **Lord's on Sunday, August 16**.
key_points: **Southern Brave** play **Sunrisers Leeds** in the Hundred Women's Eliminator today at **The Oval**.
The match starts at **1:15pm** local time; the winner advances straight to the final.
**Trent Rockets Women** already secured direct qualification and wait in the final at **Lord's on Sunday**.
Sunrisers Leeds reached the eliminator after knocking out Birmingham Phoenix in an earlier decider.

depth.background: **The Hundred** is England's short-form (100-ball) cricket competition, run alongside separate men's and women's tournaments each August. Teams that finish top of the group table qualify directly for Sunday's final at **Lord's**, while the second- and third-placed sides play a knockout **Eliminator** for the last final spot. This year, **Trent Rockets Women** topped the table and go straight through, leaving Southern Brave and Sunrisers Leeds to fight it out.

cards.title: Bangladesh claws back to 175 for 2 on day two in Darwin, trailing Australia by just 23 runs
cards.what_happened: On day one, Bangladesh's bowlers bundled Australia out for just 198, with fast bowler Hasan Mahmud claiming a career-best 6 for 55, and the tourists closed the day at 96 for 1 in reply. On day two, Bangladesh continued building on that platform, reaching 175 for 2 after 50 overs with Mominul Haque unbeaten on 35 and Tanzid Hasan unbeaten on 32, cutting the deficit to Australia's total to just 23 runs. During Australia's innings, veteran fast bowler Mitchell Starc passed Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath to become the most successful left-arm bowler in Test cricket history.
key_points: Bangladesh reached **175/2** after 50 overs on day two, having bowled Australia out for **198** in their first innings
**Mominul Haque (35 not out)** and **Tanzid Hasan (32 not out)** are steering a fightback that has trimmed the deficit to just **23 runs**
The platform follows **Hasan Mahmud's career-best 6 for 55**, which skittled Australia's first innings on day one
This is Bangladesh's **first-ever Test tour of Australia**, ending a 23-year wait for a red-ball series Down Under
Australia's **Mitchell Starc** became Test cricket's most successful left-arm bowler during the innings, passing Rangana Herath

thread.previously: At stumps on day one, Bangladesh had reached 96 for 1 in reply after bowling Australia out for 198, trailing by 102 runs.
thread.changed: Bangladesh have extended their reply to 175 for 2 after 50 overs on day two, cutting the deficit to just 23 runs behind Australia's total.

depth.background: Bangladesh's tour of Australia is historic in itself — this is the first time the team has played a Test series in Australia, 23 years after first joining the small group of nations with Test status. The match is being played in Darwin, a venue known for hot, humid conditions that can behave differently to Australia's more familiar southern grounds. Bangladesh went into day one as heavy underdogs against an Australian side that includes veteran fast bowler Mitchell Starc, one of the most successful bowlers in the format's history.

prev_ref.title: India's injury crunch deepens: Sai Sudharsan ruled out of the Sri Lanka Tests with a toe fracture, and captain Shubman Gill is now under an injury cloud too

cards.title: Jasprit Bumrah ruled out of the Sri Lanka Tests as India hands uncapped Auqib Nabi a shock call-up
cards.what_happened: The BCCI announced a 15-member squad for the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka, naming Shubman Gill as captain and KL Rahul as vice-captain. Bumrah was left out entirely as he continues recovering from the knee injury sustained during India's ODI series in England, and uncapped fast bowler Auqib Nabi — who took 104 wickets in his last two Ranji Trophy seasons for Jammu and Kashmir, including 60 in this year's title-winning campaign — was named as his replacement. Gill, who had been under an injury cloud after hurting his finger in the warm-up match against a Sri Lanka Cricket XI, has since been passed fit to lead. Sai Sudharsan was separately ruled out of the series with a fractured toe. The first of the two Tests begins August 15 at Galle.
key_points: **Jasprit Bumrah** misses the two-match series as he continues recovering from a left-knee injury picked up in the England ODIs
**Shubman Gill** has been declared fit to captain the side after a finger scare in the warm-up match
**Auqib Nabi**, 26, earns his maiden India call-up after taking **104 wickets** across his last two Ranji Trophy seasons
KL Rahul is vice-captain; **Sai Sudharsan** is also out of the series with a fractured toe
The first Test starts **August 15** in Galle — India's first red-ball tour of Sri Lanka in **nine years**

thread.previously: As of yesterday, Sai Sudharsan had been ruled out with a toe fracture and Shubman Gill's own participation was in doubt after a finger injury in the warm-up match.
thread.changed: Gill has now been passed fit and will captain the side, while Jasprit Bumrah has been confirmed out of the series entirely, with uncapped fast bowler Auqib Nabi drafted in as his replacement.

depth.background: India last toured Sri Lanka for a Test series in 2017, when Virat Kohli's side completed a 3-0 clean sweep. This series is part of the 2025-27 World Test Championship (WTC) cycle, in which India currently sit fifth in the standings and Sri Lanka sixth. Bumrah, India's premier fast bowler, has been carefully managed through injuries in recent months, while allrounder Ravindra Jadeja's fitness has also been closely watched heading into this tour.

cards.title: Trent Rockets reach both Hundred finals as men's Eliminator between Manchester Super Giants and Sunrisers Leeds looms at the Oval
cards.what_happened: Trent Rockets have already locked in their place in both the men's and women's Hundred finals at Lord's on August 16, after topping their respective group tables. In the men's competition, the battle for the second final spot comes down to Friday's Eliminator at The Oval between Manchester Super Giants and Sunrisers Leeds — the same two sides who met just days earlier, when Manchester's big win pulled them level with Sunrisers on 20 points and ahead on net run-rate, securing the higher Eliminator seeding. On the women's side, Trent Rockets sealed top spot with 28 points from eight group matches, meaning they progress straight to Sunday's final without playing in an Eliminator.
key_points: **Trent Rockets** have already secured their place in both the men's and women's Hundred finals at Lord's on **August 16**.
In the men's competition, **Manchester Super Giants** face **Sunrisers Leeds** in Friday's Eliminator at The Oval, with the winner also advancing to the final.
Manchester Super Giants reached the Eliminator after a big win over Sunrisers Leeds on Tuesday, edging them into second place on **net run-rate**.
Trent Rockets' women's side automatically qualified for Sunday's final after topping their table with **28 points** from eight group games.

thread.previously: We reported that Sunrisers Leeds had reached the Eliminator stage after Birmingham Phoenix's win eliminated MI London.
thread.changed: Manchester Super Giants have since beaten Sunrisers Leeds directly to claim the higher Eliminator seeding, meaning the two sides now face off again today for the final spot in Sunday's final — while Trent Rockets have locked in both the men's and women's final berths.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format franchise cricket competition, running both men's and women's tournaments in parallel each August. Teams play a round-robin group stage, after which the top side goes straight to the final while the second- and third-placed teams meet in a knockout Eliminator for the other final spot.

prev_ref.title: Scotland and Canada clash again in Dundee with 2027 World Cup qualification hopes on the line

cards.title: Scotland thump Canada by 170 runs in Dundee rematch to boost their 2027 World Cup qualification hopes
cards.what_happened: Scotland posted a commanding **347 for 7** batting first at Forthill in Dundee, then bowled out Canada for just **177**, winning by **170 runs**. Left-arm bowler Lyle Robertson was the standout performer, taking **6 wickets for 52 runs** to earn Player of the Match honours. The comprehensive win comes just a week after the two sides met in a far closer contest, which Scotland won by only 9 runs (281/7 to Canada's 272), underlining how much more dominant this second meeting was.
key_points: Scotland beat Canada by **170 runs** in Dundee, posting **347/7** before bowling Canada out for just **177**.
Left-armer **Lyle Robertson** starred with **6 wickets for 52 runs**, earning Player of the Match.
The result comes just days after Scotland edged the same opponent by a much tighter **9 runs** in an earlier meeting.
The match was part of the **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2**, a qualification pathway toward the 2027 World Cup.

thread.previously: We previewed this Scotland-Canada rematch in Dundee as a key fixture for both sides' 2027 World Cup qualification hopes, following Scotland's narrow 9-run win in their first meeting.
thread.changed: Scotland delivered a far more emphatic result this time, winning by 170 runs behind Lyle Robertson's 6-for, significantly boosting their net run-rate in the qualification table.

depth.background: Scotland and Canada are both competing in the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2, a multi-year qualifying league among associate cricket nations vying for a place at the 2027 Cricket World Cup. The two sides had already met earlier this month in a tight 9-run Scotland win, making this rematch a chance for Scotland to build a bigger points cushion.

cards.title: India cruise past Sri Lanka Cricket XI in their Galle warm-up as bowling coach Morkel backs KL Rahul to anchor the Test series
cards.what_happened: India opened their Sri Lanka tour with a comfortable **six-wicket win over a Sri Lanka Cricket XI** in a three-day warm-up match, built around an unbeaten **142 from Devdutt Padikkal**. In the build-up, India's bowling coach Morne Morkel spoke publicly about the value KL Rahul brings to the squad, highlighting his experience and his role in helping younger players adjust to conditions in Sri Lanka. Rahul trained alongside captain Shubman Gill, Padikkal and Rishabh Pant in pre-match sessions at the Galle International Stadium, where the first of two Tests begins on **August 15**. The warm-up win gives India momentum heading into a series where they are already missing frontline pace bowler Jasprit Bumrah.
key_points: India beat a **Sri Lanka Cricket XI by six wickets** in their three-day warm-up match, with **Devdutt Padikkal scoring an unbeaten 142**.
India's bowling coach **Morne Morkel** publicly backed **KL Rahul** to play a key role in the upcoming Test series.
Rahul is the **sole survivor** from India's batting group on their last tour of Sri Lanka in 2017, giving him rare experience in these conditions.
Captain **Shubman Gill trained alongside Rahul, Padikkal and Rishabh Pant** in pre-match sessions at Galle International Stadium.
The first Test against Sri Lanka begins **August 15 in Galle**, with India missing Jasprit Bumrah to injury.

depth.background: India's tour of Sri Lanka comes at a moment when the squad is already carrying significant injury concerns — Jasprit Bumrah was ruled out with a knee issue, and captain Shubman Gill has also been managing a finger injury heading into the series. KL Rahul, a senior and experienced batter, is the only player left in India's current squad who also featured on India's previous Test tour of Sri Lanka in 2017, making his knowledge of local conditions unusually valuable to a squad otherwise light on recent experience there. The two-Test series marks an important early assessment of India's depth heading into a demanding season.

cards.title: Pakistan's pacers claim six wickets but their top order is left chasing 305 in an England warm-up match at Beckenham
cards.what_happened: In their three-day warm-up fixture at Beckenham against a Professional County Club Select XI, Pakistan's bowling attack — led by **Ali and Abbas, who shared six wickets** — bowled the Select XI out for 305. Pakistan's own batting effort in reply was slow to get going: they finished the first day on **44 for 0 after 13 overs**, still 261 runs behind. The match continues through August 15, giving Pakistan's top order more time at the crease to find rhythm before the series proper begins. The tour's first Test starts August 19 at Headingley in Leeds, followed by matches at Lord's and Edgbaston.
key_points: A **Professional County Club Select XI scored 305** against Pakistan's bowlers in a three-day warm-up match at Beckenham.
Pakistan bowlers **Ali and Abbas shared six wickets** between them to restrict the Select XI's total.
In reply, Pakistan closed Day 1 on just **44/0 after 13 overs**, still trailing by 261 runs.
The match is Pakistan's final tune-up before the **first Test against England begins August 19 at Headingley, Leeds**.
Pakistan's Test squad is captained by **Babar Azam**, on tour after a series in the West Indies.

depth.background: Pakistan's tour of England is part of the **ICC World Test Championship 2025–27 cycle**, and comes directly after a Test series in the West Indies, meaning the squad has had limited turnaround time between assignments. Warm-up matches like this one against a County Select XI are the last chance for touring teams to adjust to English conditions — different pitch and weather behaviour from anywhere else in the world — before a Test series begins. Pakistan's squad, led by Babar Azam, arrived in England having also brought in a new batting coach, Michael Smith, ahead of this series.

cards.title: BCCI seeks the Indian government's go-ahead before confirming a Bangladesh tour, as cricket ties stay strained
cards.what_happened: BCCI sources say the board has locked in a proposed window for a six-match tour of Bangladesh but will not confirm it until it receives formal approval from the Indian government — standard practice for tours to countries where diplomatic sensitivities are in play. This follows a visit by BCB president Tamim Iqbal to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, which cricket officials on both sides described as a positive step toward normalizing relations. The tour, originally scheduled for August 2025, was deferred by mutual agreement to September 2026 after the earlier diplomatic rupture.
key_points: BCCI says it will approach the **Indian government** for formal clearance before confirming a tour of Bangladesh
Tensions began in **January 2026** when BCCI asked KKR to release Bangladeshi bowler Mustafizur Rahman from the IPL
Bangladesh's board (BCB) then **refused to travel to India** for the 2026 T20 World Cup, citing security advice
A recent visit by **BCB president Tamim Iqbal** to the BCCI's Bengaluru academy has revived hopes for the tour
The series was originally set for **August 2025** before being deferred to **September 2026**

depth.background: Cricket ties between India and Bangladesh soured amid the political turmoil in Bangladesh under its interim government led by Muhammad Yunus, feeding into a broader chill in bilateral relations. The flashpoint came when BCCI, citing violence against religious minorities in Bangladesh, asked Kolkata Knight Riders to release Bangladeshi pace bowler Mustafizur Rahman from their IPL 2026 squad — a request Bangladesh's board answered days later by pulling its national team out of traveling to India for the 2026 T20 World Cup over security concerns. Since then, ties have shown signs of thawing under new Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

cards.title: Mitchell Starc becomes Test cricket's most successful left-arm bowler ever, passing Rangana Herath
cards.what_happened: During day two of the Australia-Bangladesh Test in Darwin, Mitchell Starc dismissed opener Shadman Islam to take his **434th Test wicket**, moving past Rangana Herath's **433** to become the leading left-arm bowler in Test cricket history. The milestone arrived in Starc's **106th Test appearance** and, fittingly, on **International Left-Handers Day**. The achievement also puts him level with India great **Kapil Dev** on the all-time wicket-takers list, and within six wickets of South Africa's **Dale Steyn (439)** for a place in the game's top ten leading wicket-takers overall, regardless of arm or bowling style.
key_points: Starc reached **434 Test wickets**, passing Sri Lanka's **Rangana Herath (433)** to become the most successful left-arm bowler in Test history.
He got there by dismissing Bangladesh opener **Shadman Islam** during the historic **Darwin Test**.
The milestone came in his **106th Test**, and fell on **International Left-Handers Day** (August 13).
Starc is now **level with Kapil Dev** on the all-time wicket-takers list, and just **six behind Dale Steyn's 439** for the top ten overall.

depth.background: Mitchell Starc has been Australia's frontline left-arm fast bowler for over a decade, known for swinging the new ball and reverse-swinging the old one. Left-arm bowlers face a quirk regardless of pace or style: there have simply been far fewer of them across cricket history than right-arm bowlers, which makes elite career wicket tallies rarer among them. Sri Lankan left-arm spinner **Rangana Herath** had held the left-arm wicket-taking record with 433 dismissals since his retirement. Starc reached the milestone during Australia's landmark first-ever home Test against Bangladesh, a fixture Bangladesh waited 23 years to secure.

cards.title: Scotland and Canada clash again in Dundee with 2027 World Cup qualification hopes on the line
cards.what_happened: Playing at their home ground of Forthill in Dundee, **Scotland batted first** against Canada in the 126th match of the League 2 cycle. At the time of writing, Scotland had reached **267/4**, with batter Michael Jones unbeaten on 41 and wicketkeeper Matthew Cross also not out, building a total aimed at extending their strong position near the top of the table. Scotland currently sit second in the League 2 standings with 38 points from 32 matches (16 wins), while Canada are fifth with 20 points from 20 games and need a strong finish to stay in contention for a World Cup Qualifier spot.
key_points: Scotland and Canada are playing their second meeting in a week in the **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2**, this time in Dundee
Scotland sit **2nd** in the League 2 table with 38 points from 32 matches; Canada are **5th** with 20 points from 20 games
The two teams last met on **August 7**, when Scotland won by 9 runs in a high-scoring game (281/7 vs 272)
League 2 results feed directly into qualification for the **2027 Cricket World Cup** — making every match here count for both sides
Scotland reached **267/4** in their innings today, with Michael Jones unbeaten on 41, as they push to extend their points lead

depth.background: The **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2** is a multi-year one-day international league for cricket's second tier of nations, running from 2023 to 2027. It's a key step on the qualification pathway toward the **2027 Cricket World Cup**, so results here have real stakes even though the teams involved — Scotland, Canada, Namibia, UAE, USA, and others — rarely make global headlines. Scotland and Canada have faced each other repeatedly in this cycle, most recently on August 7 in a tight 9-run Scotland win, and today's rematch in Dundee is part of the same tightly-fought race for qualification points.

cards.title: India's injury crunch deepens: Sai Sudharsan ruled out of the Sri Lanka Tests with a toe fracture, and captain Shubman Gill is now under an injury cloud too
cards.what_happened: India batter **Sai Sudharsan** has been ruled out of the upcoming two-Test series in Sri Lanka because of a **toe stress fracture** that hasn't healed enough for him to be declared fit. He had been named in the initial 15-man squad, but his selection — like Bumrah's — was conditional on medical clearance from the BCCI's Centre of Excellence, and he ultimately failed to get it in time; he did not travel with the squad and **no replacement has been named yet**. Adding to India's pre-series injury concerns, Test captain **Shubman Gill** is now also under an injury cloud after hurting his **right ring finger** during a training session in Colombo — a new issue, separate from an earlier finger problem that had already been reported resolved. The two-Test series begins **August 15 in Galle**, with the second Test starting **August 23** at the SSC in Colombo.
key_points: **Sai Sudharsan** is ruled out of the two-Test Sri Lanka series with a **toe stress fracture**.
He had been given a conditional spot pending fitness clearance from the BCCI's **Centre of Excellence (CoE)** — he didn't recover in time.
No replacement for Sudharsan has been named yet, and he did not travel with the squad to Sri Lanka.
Captain **Shubman Gill** is now also under an injury cloud after hurting his **right ring finger** in a training session in Colombo.
The series starts **August 15 in Galle**, with the second Test in **Colombo from August 23**.

thread.previously: When India named its 15-man Test squad for Sri Lanka, Jadeja returned from injury but Jasprit Bumrah was ruled out; Sai Sudharsan and Bumrah's spots had been made conditional on fitness clearance, and Gill's own earlier finger injury was reported as resolved.
thread.changed: Sudharsan has now failed that fitness test and is officially ruled out with a toe stress fracture, with no replacement yet named — and captain Shubman Gill has picked up a new, separate injury, hurting his right ring finger in training in Colombo just before the series starts.

depth.background: India named its Test squad for the Sri Lanka tour with some fitness question marks already attached: Sudharsan and Bumrah's places were both conditional on medical clearance after recent injuries, and Bumrah ultimately missed out. Sudharsan picked up a **toe stress fracture** — a small crack in the bone from repeated stress rather than a single impact — after returning from India A's tour of Sri Lanka in July, and had been at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence trying to recover in time.

cards.title: Bangladesh reach 96/1 at stumps, trailing Australia by just 102, after bowling the hosts out for 198
cards.what_happened: Australia were bowled out for just 198 on the opening day, with Hasan Mahmud claiming a career-best 6 for 55 — his third Test five-wicket haul — as Bangladesh's fast bowlers took all 10 Australian wickets, only the second time that has happened in the team's Test history. Steve Smith top-scored for the hosts with 71 off 109 balls. In reply, Bangladesh reached 96 for 1 by stumps, trailing by just 102 runs, with Mominul Haque and Tanzid Hasan both unbeaten and looking well set. Starc was the one Australian bowler who consistently troubled the Bangladesh batters, but the rest of the attack — including veteran spinner Nathan Lyon — couldn't find similar impact as conditions eased through the day.
key_points: Bangladesh closed day one at **96/1**, trailing Australia's first-innings **198** by just **102 runs**.
**Mominul Haque and Tanzid Hasan** both finished the day not out, building a solid platform in reply.
Only **Mitchell Starc** looked genuinely threatening with the ball; the rest of Australia's attack, including Nathan Lyon, made little impact.
Bangladesh had earlier bowled Australia out for **198**, with **Hasan Mahmud** taking a career-best **6 for 55**.
It's Bangladesh's **first Test tour of Australia in 23 years** — and they've taken the early honours.

depth.background: Bangladesh arrived in Australia for their first Test tour of the country in 23 years, historically one of the toughest assignments in world cricket given Australia's pace-friendly home conditions. At Marrara Stadium in Darwin, Australia won the toss and chose to bat first — the conventional move at a ground where the pitch typically gets harder to bat on as a match wears on. Instead, Bangladesh's pace attack dismantled the Australian batting order on day one.

cards.title: The Hundred's Eliminator picture is set: Sunrisers Leeds through after Birmingham Phoenix knock out MI London
cards.what_happened: Birmingham Phoenix beat MI London in their final group match, a result that eliminated MI London from contention and confirmed Sunrisers Leeds as the fourth and final qualifier for the knockout stage. That completes the picture for the men's competition: Manchester Super Giants will play Sunrisers Leeds in the Eliminator at The Oval on August 14, with the winner advancing to face Trent Rockets — who topped the table and already have a direct spot — in the final at Lord's on August 16.
key_points: **Birmingham Phoenix** beat **MI London** in the last regular-season match, eliminating them and sending **Sunrisers Leeds** through instead.
The men's **Eliminator** is now confirmed: **Manchester Super Giants vs Sunrisers Leeds**, August 14 at The Oval.
**Trent Rockets** already secured top spot and a direct place in the final at Lord's on August 16.
The Eliminator winner will face Trent Rockets in the final.
The result closes out group-stage play across the men's competition.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's 100-ball franchise cricket competition, with eight men's and eight women's teams. Going into the last day of group games, Trent Rockets had already locked up first place and a direct final berth, while Manchester Super Giants had secured the other guaranteed spot — the Eliminator. The final qualification slot, between MI London and Sunrisers Leeds, came down to the last matches of the group stage.

cards.title: Hasan Mahmud's career-best 6-for stuns Australia as Bangladesh's pacers bowl them out for 198 in Darwin
cards.what_happened: Australia won the toss and chose to bat first at Marrara Stadium in Darwin, but were bowled out for 198 by the end of the first day. Hasan Mahmud led the destruction with a career-best 6 for 55 — his third Test five-wicket haul — while Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain chipped in with two wickets each. It marked only the second time in Bangladesh's Test history that fast bowlers have taken all 10 wickets in an innings, after a similar feat in Rawalpindi in 2024. Steven Smith was the one bright spot for Australia, top-scoring with 71 off 109 balls including seven fours and a six.
key_points: Bangladesh bowled Australia out for just **198** on day one of the first Test in Darwin.
**Hasan Mahmud** took a career-best **6 for 55** — his third Test five-wicket haul.
Bangladesh's **fast bowlers took all 10 Australian wickets** — only the second time that's happened in the team's Test history.
**Steven Smith** top-scored for Australia with **71 off 109 balls**.
It's Bangladesh's **first Test tour of Australia in 23 years**.

depth.background: Bangladesh has not played a Test series in Australia in 23 years, making this tour a rare and significant assignment for a team more often associated with home conditions and spin bowling than fast bowling on the road. The first Test began August 13 at Marrara Stadium in Darwin and runs through August 17.

cards.title: Root scraps England's midnight curfew in his first move as reinstated Test captain
cards.what_happened: Root confirmed England will not operate under a curfew for the upcoming three-match Test series against Pakistan, arguing that if players are trusted to make good decisions on the field, they should be trusted to do the same off it. It's the first real decision of his reinstated captaincy, and directly reverses the disciplinary approach that led to Stokes and Atkinson's suspension earlier in the year. The series begins August 19.
key_points: Joe Root has **abolished England's midnight curfew** ahead of the Pakistan Test series.
It's his **first concrete decision** since being reinstated as Test captain.
Root says players should be trusted to **manage themselves like adults** off the field, just as they are on it.
The curfew is the same rule **Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended for breaching** earlier this year.
The three-match series against Pakistan begins **August 19**.

depth.background: England's Test set-up has been through turbulence this year: Ben Stokes retired in June during the New Zealand series, having earlier been suspended for a Test — along with pace bowler Gus Atkinson — for breaching the team's midnight curfew during a night out. Former coach Brendon McCullum also stepped down after England lost that series 2-1. Root, England's most-capped modern batter, has now returned to the Test captaincy he previously held, alongside a new coaching setup.

cards.title: Australia win the toss and bat first as the historic Bangladesh Test begins in Darwin
cards.what_happened: Australia won the toss and captain **Pat Cummins** elected to bat first on a green Darwin surface in humid conditions, with opener **Travis Head** expecting a tough opening period against the new ball. Australia's confirmed XI is: Jake Weatherald, Travis Head, Marnus Labuschagne, Steve Smith, Cameron Green, Alex Carey, Beau Webster, Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins (captain), Nathan Lyon, and Josh Hazlewood. Both Green and Webster won selection battles for their all-rounder spots, and Lyon returns to the side after sitting out the back end of the Ashes with a hamstring injury. This marks the first time in over a year that Australia's leading pace trio — Cummins, Hazlewood, and Starc — has played together. Bangladesh has named Ebadot Hossain and Mahmudul Hasan in its own XI as the tourists begin their first Test series on Australian soil in 23 years.
key_points: Australia captain **Pat Cummins won the toss** and chose to **bat first** on a green, humid Darwin pitch.
The confirmed Australia XI includes **Cameron Green and Beau Webster**, both winning selection battles for the spot.
**Nathan Lyon returns** after missing the back end of the Ashes with a hamstring injury.
The Cummins-Hazlewood-Starc pace trio is playing together for the **first time in more than a year**.
This is Bangladesh's **first Test tour of Australia in 23 years**, marking a historic return fixture.

thread.previously: We reported Australia was set to reunite its Cummins-Starc-Hazlewood pace attack for the first Bangladesh Test, with the hosts still finalizing their XI amid fitness 'niggles' in camp.

depth.background: Bangladesh last toured Australia for a Test series back in 2003, when Australia won comfortably — so this five-day match at Darwin's Marrara Cricket Ground, starting the current series, is being treated as a genuinely historic fixture for Bangladeshi cricket. Australia has been juggling injuries and form questions in its bowling attack over the past year, including during the recent Ashes series, which is why the reunion of its three most experienced fast bowlers together is being watched closely.

cards.title: Australia bat first as Bangladesh's 23-year wait for a Test tour Down Under finally ends in Darwin
cards.what_happened: Play began today in Darwin with Australia's captain **Pat Cummins** winning the toss and electing to bat first, fielding a full-strength side: Travis Head, Jake Weatherald, Marnus Labuschagne, Steven Smith, Cameron Green, Alex Carey (wicketkeeper), Beau Webster, Cummins, **Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and Josh Hazlewood** — reuniting Australia's premier pace trio of Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood for the first time in this series. Bangladesh, led by captain **Najmul Hossain Shanto**, have signalled they may field two spinners even on a fast, bouncy Australian pitch, after being dismissed for just 54 in their warm-up match's second innings. Weather forecasts point to dry, sunny conditions for all five days.
key_points: Australia won the toss and chose to **bat first** in the opening Test at **Marrara Cricket Ground, Darwin** — Bangladesh's **first Test tour of Australia in 23 years**.
It's also Darwin's **first Test match in 22 years**, played in **clear, sunny conditions around 31°C**.
Australia's XI features their full frontline pace attack — **Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood together** — plus Travis Head, Steven Smith and captain Pat Cummins.
Bangladesh arrive under pressure after being **bowled out for just 54** in their second innings of the warm-up match against a Cricket Australia XI.

thread.previously: Yesterday's story covered Australia naming their squad and reuniting the Cummins-Starc-Hazlewood pace trio ahead of the series opener.
thread.changed: Today the match actually started: Australia won the toss, chose to bat, and confirmed their full XI, while Bangladesh's likely tactics (fielding two spinners despite quick, bouncy conditions) became clear after their poor warm-up form.

depth.background: Bangladesh have toured Australia for Test cricket only rarely, and not at all in over two decades — a gap driven by scheduling, cricket-calendar priorities, and Australia's traditionally packed home summer. Darwin, in Australia's tropical Northern Territory, is an unusual and rarely-used Test venue, chosen partly to give Bangladesh conditions (heat, humidity) closer to what they're used to at home, even though the pitch and bounce still differ sharply from subcontinental cricket. Bangladesh's poor warm-up form has raised doubts about how competitive they can be against a full-strength Australian pace attack.

cards.title: England opener Emilio Gay named in warm-up squad ahead of Pakistan Tests, easing shoulder-injury fears
cards.what_happened: On **August 7**, while batting for Durham against Middlesex in a one-day match, Gay first felt discomfort in his right shoulder, then aggravated it two overs later hitting a boundary; he immediately called for the physio and retired hurt on 9 off 17 balls, undergoing a scan over the following days. Despite that scare, Gay has now been named in the **PCC Select XI** — a first-class invitational team — for a three-day tour match against Pakistan starting **August 13** at Beckenham, Kent's ground. Sky Sports reported it understands Gay is expected to be fit for the Test series, and his inclusion in this squad is the clearest sign yet that the shoulder issue isn't ruling him out of the opener at Headingley on **August 19**.
key_points: England Test opener **Emilio Gay** was named in the 14-player **PCC Select XI** for a three-day warm-up match against touring Pakistan, starting **August 13 at Beckenham**.
Gay had retired hurt on **9 off 17 balls** on **August 7**, clutching his shoulder while batting for Durham, after aggravating discomfort that began two overs earlier.
His selection suggests he's expected to prove fitness in time for the **first Test at Headingley on August 19**, the opener of a three-match series against Pakistan.
The squad is captained by **Tom Haines** and includes uncapped and fringe players like Shoaib Bashir and Josh Hull.
A lost place for Gay would have forced England to reshuffle its top order just days before a marquee home series.

depth.background: Gay only nailed down England's Test opening slot earlier this year, making his fitness a genuine selection question rather than a formality. The warm-up match against Pakistan's touring side is the traditional final fitness and form check before a Test series — Pakistan's three-Test tour runs Headingley (Aug 19), Lord's (Aug 27-31) and Edgbaston (Sept 9-13).
